name: Support-Assisted Footwork
target_behavior: Footwork with a stability aid
purpose: Footwork with a stability aid
standard_setup: support rail or frame
execution: Footwork patterns performed with a stability aid. The pattern is the target; the aid is not a lesser version of the drill.
what_good_looks_like:
Feet run the same step sequence whether the hand is on the aid or not.
Weight stays centered over the base foot through each step, no lean into the support.
Contact with the aid is light — fingertips or open palm, not a grip.
Steps land on a steady rhythm, no pause to check balance before moving.
what_bad_looks_like:
Athlete leans body weight into the aid instead of resting a hand on it.
Feet stall or shorten between steps to recover balance.
Pattern changes shape when the aid is taken away — wider base, slower steps, skipped steps.
Grip on the support tightens as the round goes on.
corrections:
Move the aid out until only light fingertip contact is possible.
Slow the pattern down and call each step aloud until the sequence repeats cleanly.
Pull the aid away for short stretches and have the athlete run the identical pattern unsupported.
Put a loose towel or light stick in the support hand so any hard grip becomes visible immediately.
transfer:
The pattern drilled here with support is the same pattern used without it in live work — the aid changes the risk, not the footwork.
Clean, repeatable footwork sequences showed up more often in winners of fast-finishing championship fights than in losers [A8-053], which is the kind of pattern habit this drill is building.

name: Sensory-Adapted Cue Drill
target_behavior: Technical work with adapted cueing
purpose: Technical work with adapted cueing
standard_setup: varies
execution: Coach delivers cues through the athlete's available channel — visual, tactile, or verbal. Cue modality is agreed with the athlete beforehand.
what_good_looks_like:
Athlete responds within one beat of the cue, no visible search or hesitation.
Coach delivers the cue through the single pre-agreed channel only.
Athlete's technical response matches what the cue called for, not a stock combination run on autopilot.
what_bad_looks_like:
Coach stacks two or three channels into one delivery - visual, verbal, and tactile at once - instead of keeping instruction load low [A1-039].
Athlete freezes, looks to teammates, or delays response - the cue isn't landing on the agreed channel.
Coach re-cues immediately and repeatedly rather than letting the athlete work the first cue [A2-040].
Athlete's response doesn't match the cue given - guessing, not reading.
corrections:
Coach strips the delivery back to one channel and one instruction, and stops there [A1-039].
Coach widens the gap between cues and lets the athlete's first response stand before intervening again [A2-040].
Coach re-confirms the channel agreement with the athlete rather than switching mid-drill.
In group sessions, coach limits how many athletes receive adapted cueing at once - supervision capacity is the binding constraint, not room size [B2-046].
transfer:
Reading a single clear cue under light contact is the same skill as reading an opponent's tell in live sparring.
Working off one clean signal at a time, without a coach hovering to re-prompt, builds the self-directed reading a boxer needs once the pads and coach step away.

name: Non-Contact Boxing Circuit
target_behavior: Boxing-style conditioning without contact
purpose: Boxing-style conditioning without contact
standard_setup: bag, rope, timer
execution: Circuit of bag, rope and bodyweight stations for participants not pursuing contact. A complete lane in its own right, not a preparatory stage.
what_good_looks_like:
Participants rotate through bag, rope and bodyweight stations with no gap between transitions.
The session moves through a fixed order — warm-up, drills, strength/endurance work, cool-down — with clearly marked high-intensity intervals inside it [B1-062].
Rope turns stay continuous, feet springing off the floor, no double-bounce.
Bag strikes extend fully and return to guard before the next combination begins.
what_bad_looks_like:
Participants cluster at one station while another sits empty.
Rope turning slows or stops mid-interval; feet go flat instead of springing.
Bag combinations thrown from the shoulders only, hips and feet not turning with the punch.
Rest periods run long because no one calls time.
corrections:
Coach calls the rotation aloud and balances station numbers before the next round starts.
Coach demonstrates rope timing at half speed, then rebuilds it to full tempo with the participant.
Coach stops the bag worker, resets stance, rebuilds the combination from the feet upward.
Coach calls interval start and stop audibly and moves the group on that cue, not on individual pace.
transfer:
The rotation habit, rhythm and interval discipline built here carry directly into any boxing-conditioning setting that does not require contact exposure.
Structured non-contact boxing circuits run as their own programme have shown strong retention and attendance in community and clinical settings, supporting this as a complete lane rather than a warm-up for sparring [B1-063][B1-059].

name: Technique-Only Fitness Session
target_behavior: Technical practice for non-competitive participants
purpose: Technical practice for non-competitive participants
standard_setup: mirror, bag
execution: Technical work for its own sake, with no progression expectation toward contact.
what_good_looks_like:
Feet reset to stance after every combination, no flat-footed throws.
Guard hand returns to cheek before the next strike starts.
Pad or air targets are struck with full extension and immediate retraction, no follow-through into a body.
Breathing stays audible and rhythmic through combinations, no breath-holding on power shots.
what_bad_looks_like:
Weight loads onto the back leg and stays there, no hip transfer.
Guard drops after the first strike and never comes back up.
Combinations speed up into full-force throws against a partner, drifting toward contact.
Wrist buckles or rotates off-line on straight punches [B2-015].
corrections:
Stop the round, walk the boxer through the single strike at half speed, rebuild the combination one punch at a time.
Call "hands" the moment the guard drops, wait for it to reset before restarting the drill.
Switch the pair back to air shadowboxing or a stationary pad, remove the moving partner target.
Point to the wrist line on contact, have the boxer punch a static pad slowly until the fist lands flat.
transfer:
Clean footwork and guard discipline built here is what a coach checks for before contact is ever introduced, live work asks for the same reset-and-return pattern under pressure.
The pacing and combination work used in non-contact boxing sessions has carried into community and clinical settings, where it has been applied to build fitness, balance and functional gait outside of any competitive context [B1-062][B1-059].

name: Phrased breathing with action groupings
target_behavior: deliberate action sequencing and tactical organization of offensive and defensive combinations
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Tuesday stabilizes organized combination patterns through structured repetition.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete, working in shadow. The coach stands where shoulders and breathing can be seen.
execution:
Coach names an action grouping (a short combination plus a defensive move) as one phrase.

Athlete sets stance with the cue "Get set first."

Athlete breathes out sharply on each action inside the phrase.

At the end of the phrase the athlete takes one controlled breath in, in stance, before the next phrase.

Athlete repeats the same phrase with the same breathing until it is steady, then the coach names the next.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Breath with 2-3 action sequences
target_behavior: maintaining stable positioning throughout all movements
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Wednesday applies positional control under coach-called combinations.

execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and athletes set stance.

Coach calls a 2-3 action sequence of steps, slips or guard shifts (no punches).

Athlete breathes out short on each action and breathes in calmly after the sequence, back in stance.

Coach watches for a held breath or rising shoulders and gives one short cue.

Coach calls the next sequence; continue for the time the session plan sets.

Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:

Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Fast defense-counter under pressure with maintained technique
target_behavior: execution tempo while maintaining technical control and positional discipline
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Wednesday applies speed with control under coach-called rapid sequences.
standard_setup: Pairs in stance at a distance where shadowed punches stop well short; one partner feeds, one defends and counters into the air. The coach stands side-on, where the defender's base can be seen before every counter.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and sets the feeder's job: steady shadowed feeds that stop short and never touch.

Defender makes one small defence, recovers shape, then counters into the air or resets and exits, whichever the picture allows.

Coach calls rapid sequences of feeds; the defender keeps the same technique at the faster pace.

Counters come only from position; when the defender counters from a broken base, the coach gives one brief cue.

Partners swap roles at the coach's call, after the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
The system allows offense after defense only when the athlete has recovered enough structure to make a real choice.
Not every defense must produce an immediate counter.
The most important transfer is usable position, not flashy reply.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete counter because the picture is there or because the athlete expects every defense to become offense.
Can the athlete choose reset or reposition when that is the better answer.
Does the defensive action leave a clear scoring lane or only emotional urgency.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Head movement chains without drift through extended sequences
target_behavior: controlled movement with clean stops, emphasizing deceleration and balance recovery
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Thursday maintains movement quality and clean stops during extended sequences.
standard_setup: Athletes in stance on a tape cross, with room to slip and roll; athletes face the coach. The coach stands to the side, where heads and feet can be seen.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first."

Coach calls a chain of head movements (for example slip, slip, roll) and the athlete flows through it.

After each movement the head comes back to centre and the feet stay on the spot.

The chain repeats through extended sequences, as the session plan sets; the coach gives one short cue and notes when drift first appears.

Between sequences athletes recover with a few calm breaths.
what_good_looks_like:
Head comes back to centre after every slip or roll, with no drift off the spot
Feet stay set under the movement; the athlete does not wander
Movements stay small late in the sequence, the same as early
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Defense-verify-counter under pressure with partner escalation
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Wednesday applies setting mechanics under coach-called offensive opportunities.
standard_setup: Pairs facing each other at the range the coach sets; the feeder wears mitts. The coach stands to the side of the pairs and tells each feeder when to escalate.
execution:
Feeder starts with single attacks at the light touch level the coach sets.

Athlete defends, then verifies the set (feet, guard, eyes) before any counter. Cue: "Get set first."

From the set the athlete counters with one earned punch to the feeder's held mitt, or resets.

When the single-attack response holds, the coach tells the feeder to escalate: quicker feeds or a two-punch feed, at the same touch level.

Against a two-punch feed the athlete defends both, sets, then counters after the final attack.
what_good_looks_like:
The system allows offense after defense only when the athlete has recovered enough structure to make a real choice.
Not every defense must produce an immediate counter.
The most important transfer is usable position, not flashy reply.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete counter because the picture is there or because the athlete expects every defense to become offense.
Can the athlete choose reset or reposition when that is the better answer.
Does the defensive action leave a clear scoring lane or only emotional urgency.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Position quality through volume punching with high-repetition sequences
target_behavior: maintaining positional integrity during punch execution and impact
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Thursday maintains stance integrity during extended offensive sequences under fatigue.
standard_setup: Each athlete at a heavy bag with a timer, or in shadow if no bag is free. The coach stands side-on, where feet and guard can be seen, and watches most closely as the volume builds.
execution:
Athlete sets stance at the bag. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete throws a high-repetition sequence for the time the session plan sets, each punch returning to guard.

Athlete keeps the feet under the body and does not lean on or push the bag as the volume builds.

Coach watches for the first thing that breaks and gives one short cue; the athlete fixes position before continuing.
what_good_looks_like:
Position on the last punches looks like position on the first.
Slower is fine; a broken stance is not.
The hand returns and the feet recover after every punch.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Quick combos without position loss with accelerated mitt work
target_behavior: execution tempo while maintaining technical control and positional discipline
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Tuesday stabilizes faster tempo execution through repetition at elevated pace.
standard_setup: Pairs: one holder with mitts, one athlete in stance at punching distance. The holder presents clear mitt targets for the athlete's punches to land on, and never feeds back at the athlete; the coach stands side-on, where the athlete's feet and guard can be seen.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first."; the athlete sets stance and guard before the first combination.

Holder calls a short combination and shows the targets; the athlete throws it quickly, each punch landing on its mitt.

Athlete finishes every combination with a defensive action or an exit and is back in stance before the next call.

Holder raises the pace of the calls only while the athlete keeps position; when position is lost, the holder stops the feed and the coach gives one brief cue.

Pairs swap at the coach's call, after the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like: Every combination ends with either a defensive action or an exit, never with the boxer standing still admiring the work
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Organized 2-3 punch combinations with deliberate sequencing
target_behavior: deliberate action sequencing and tactical organization of offensive and defensive combinations
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Monday introduces planned action sequences with clear beginning and end points.
standard_setup: Open floor, each athlete facing a mirror, the coach, or a partner standing out of reach; all punches are shadow punches that touch nothing. The coach stands where each athlete's feet and hands can be seen.
execution:
Coach names one 2-3 punch combination and its end action (a defensive move or an exit step).

Athlete sets stance with the cue "Get set first."

Athlete throws the combination in the set order, each punch returning before the next, then finishes with the named defense or exit.

Athlete freezes in stance at the end to show the sequence is finished.

Coach gives one short cue and the athlete repeats the same combination before a new one is named.
what_good_looks_like: Every combination ends with either a defensive action or an exit, never with the boxer standing still admiring the work
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Elevated tempo breathing with faster cycle rates
target_behavior: execution tempo while maintaining technical control and positional discipline
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Tuesday stabilizes faster tempo execution through repetition at elevated pace.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to shadow box. The coach stands where shoulders and jaw can be seen and breathing can be heard.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first."; the athlete sets stance and breathes calmly.

Athlete shadow boxes in short action cycles, a short sharp exhale with each punch and a full breath in the gaps.

Coach raises the cycle rate in steps; the breath stays paired with the punches at each step.

Once each round the athlete checks that the jaw is not clenched and the shoulders are not at the ears.

Athlete works for the time the session plan sets; the coach gives one brief breath cue when the pattern breaks.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Calm footwork during pressure scenarios with spatial awareness
target_behavior: composure and measured responses during defensive scenarios and incoming pressure
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Wednesday applies composed defense under live coach-called attack patterns.
standard_setup: A marked area with edges in tape or cones, big enough to move in; one athlete works inside against a partner who walks forward to pressure, never touching. The coach stands outside the area where the edges and both athletes can be seen.
execution:
Athlete sets stance in the middle with the cue "Get set first."

Coach calls the scenario (for example, start near an edge); the partner walks forward to pressure without touching and the athlete moves calmly to keep distance.

Athlete keeps track of the edges and, before reaching one, steps laterally or angles off instead of backing straight into it.

Athlete finishes each escape in stance, facing the partner, and breathes out.

Coach gives one short cue after the run.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete knows where the edges are without staring at them.
The edge is avoided early with a side step or angle, not by backing into it.
Each escape ends in stance, facing the partner, guard up.
The feet stay calm: no rushed or crossing steps.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Tactical organization under cardio stress with extended structured flows
target_behavior: deliberate action sequencing and tactical organization of offensive and defensive combinations
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Thursday maintains organized execution during complex, extended sequences under fatigue.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete, working in shadow; flows run when the athletes are already working hard, for the time the session plan sets. The coach stands where several athletes can be seen.
execution:
Coach names one structured flow (for example, enter, combination, defend, exit, reset) and its order.

Athlete sets stance with the cue "Get set first."

Athlete runs the flow continuously in its order, ending each pass set before starting the next.

As breathing gets hard, the athlete keeps the same order and finish; output can drop, organization cannot.

Coach gives one short cue for the first part of the flow that breaks.
what_good_looks_like:
The flow keeps its order and its finish late in the work.
Each pass ends set before the next starts.
Punches and steps may slow, but stance and guard stay usable.
The athlete does not add or skip parts to get through.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Neck mobility and chin tuck position with mirror work
target_behavior: maintaining stable positioning throughout all movements
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Monday introduces core stance mechanics and static holds.
standard_setup: Each athlete stands in stance facing a mirror, with room to turn the head freely. The coach stands to the side of the line, where every chin can be seen in profile.
execution:
Coach shows the chin tuck once and gives the cue "Get set first."

Athlete turns the head slowly left and right and nods up and down through an easy range, coming back to centre each time.

Athlete sets stance, tucks the chin with eyes level, looking through the top of the eye sockets, and checks the picture in the mirror.

Athlete holds the tuck for the time the session plan sets while the coach gives one short cue to fix one thing.

Athlete relaxes, then sets stance and chin again from scratch; each new set is one rep.
what_good_looks_like: Chin tucked, eyes level, looking through the top of the eye sockets rather than up
what_bad_looks_like: chin up (film from the side, every session, for four weeks)
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Stance hold during coach combinations with 3-step sequences
target_behavior: maintaining stable positioning throughout all movements
purpose: Footwork establishes positional control. Wednesday applies positional control under coach-called combinations.
standard_setup: Open floor with room to step in every direction; athletes face the coach. The coach stands in front, where every athlete's feet can be seen.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and athletes set stance.

Coach calls a 3-step sequence (for example forward, back, side) and the athletes step it.

Athlete freezes in stance at the end of the sequence; the coach checks width, weight and feet and gives one short cue.

Athlete re-sets if needed, and the coach calls the next sequence; continue for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Base width roughly shoulder-width plus a half-step, lead foot pointed slightly inward toward the opponent, rear foot at roughly 45°
Weight distribution near 50/50 at rest, shifting to demand — not permanently forward (loses the ability to move back) or permanently back (loses power and forward pressure)
Knees soft and unlocked; hips slightly under, not stuck out behind
Rear heel light, not planted, not up on the toe
what_bad_looks_like: feet too narrow (draw a line on the floor and stand across it); square to the opponent (drill from a taped 45° line); weight on the front foot (drill with the rear foot on a small pad so you can feel loading)
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Continuous head movement with controlled tempo against partner feeds
target_behavior: composure and measured responses during defensive scenarios and incoming pressure
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Tuesday stabilizes calm defensive responses through progressive intensity drilling.
standard_setup: Pairs face each other at a distance where the feeder's punches stop short; the feeder throws slow single or paired straights that never touch. The coach stands side-on to see head, stance and the feeder's pace.
execution:
Coach sets the feeder's job and pace before the round: feeds stop short and keep one steady rhythm.

Athlete sets stance with the cue "Get set first."

Feeder feeds continuously at the set tempo; the athlete moves the head off the line for each feed and back to centre, at the same controlled pace.

Athlete breathes out with each movement and keeps the stance under the head.

Coach raises the tempo one step at a time only while the movement stays controlled.
what_good_looks_like:
The head moves just off the line and back, at the pace of the feeds.
Stance and guard stay in place under the moving head.
Breathing keeps going; no held breath between feeds.
Tempo rises only when the coach raises it, not because the athlete hurries.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Pause-verify-execute breathing
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Monday introduces deliberate set position checks before any punch.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance facing the coach or a mirror, with room to throw. The coach stands in front, where shoulders, chest and hands can be seen.
execution:
Athlete sets stance and pauses, taking one calm breath in while still.

Athlete verifies the set: feet, guard, chin, shoulders down. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete executes the action on a short sharp exhale: one earned punch in shadow, or a step if punches are not yet earned.

Athlete breathes in on the return to stance and pauses again before the next rep.

Coach watches for breath holding and raised shoulders and gives one short cue.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Defensive integrity through movement combos
target_behavior: controlled movement with clean stops, emphasizing deceleration and balance recovery
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Thursday maintains movement quality and clean stops during extended sequences.
standard_setup: Open floor with room to move in all directions; athletes face the coach. The coach stands where hands, heads and feet can be seen.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and athletes set stance and high guard.

Coach calls movement combos that mix steps, pivots, slips and rolls.

Athlete keeps the guard high and the stance usable through the combo, and finishes each defensive move back in shape before the next.

Coach checks at the end of each combo and gives one short cue; continue through extended sequences, as the session plan sets.

Between sequences athletes recover with a few calm breaths.
what_good_looks_like:
Guard stays high through every step, pivot, slip and roll
Each defensive move ends back in shape, in stance, before the next
Feet stay usable and eyes stay forward
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Speed-control standard during fast rounds with 2-minute high-intensity intervals
target_behavior: execution tempo while maintaining technical control and positional discipline
purpose: Footwork establishes positional control. Thursday maintains controlled speed during extended high-tempo rounds under fatigue.
standard_setup: Open floor with a tape line or cones per athlete and a round timer set to 2-minute intervals. The coach stands side-on, where feet and hips can be seen through the interval.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." before each interval.

Athlete works fast footwork in stance through the 2-minute interval (forward, back, lateral and angles), freezing in stance on the coach's call.

Coach checks each freeze; speed is kept only as long as position is kept.

Between intervals the athlete resets posture and breath before the next one starts.

Coach sets the number of intervals from the session plan and gives one brief cue when position slips.
what_good_looks_like:
Late in the interval the feet still arrive in stance at each freeze.
The athlete may slow down, but the stance does not break.
The feet stay working: no crossing, flat feet or blind turns.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Stance transitions (forward-back) through slow stepping
target_behavior: maintaining stable positioning throughout all movements
purpose: Footwork establishes positional control. Tuesday reinforces positioning through repetition drills.
standard_setup: One straight floor line per athlete, running front to back, with room for several steps each way. Athletes set stance on the line; the coach stands to the side, where the feet can be seen moving.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and athletes set stance on the line.

Athlete steps slowly forward along the line, lead foot first and rear foot following, and stops in stance.

Athlete steps slowly back, rear foot first and lead foot following, and stops in stance.

Coach watches each stop for crossed, drifting or bouncing feet and gives one short cue.

Athlete repeats forward and back for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like: Forward and backward on a line — lead foot moves first going forward, rear foot first going back, never crossing, never bouncing off both feet at once
what_bad_looks_like: Do feet cross, drift, freeze, or over-step under simple demands.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Consistent action quality with reliable breathing patterns
target_behavior: consistent, reliable execution of all learned skills across varying conditions and fatigue levels
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Wednesday applies consistent execution under coach-called mixed scenarios and unpredictable patterns.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to shadow box. The coach stands where action quality can be seen and breathing heard, and calls the actions.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first."

Coach calls mixed, unpredictable actions; the athlete answers each with clean technique and a short sharp exhale on each punch.

Athlete breathes in the gaps and keeps the shoulders down between actions.

Coach checks that action quality and breathing hold together, and gives one brief cue when either slips.

Athlete works for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Quicker head movement maintaining form with tempo progression
target_behavior: execution tempo while maintaining technical control and positional discipline
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Monday introduces increased speed within controlled parameters.
standard_setup: Athletes in stance facing a mirror or the coach, each with room for a short step. The coach stands side-on, where head path, knees and guard can be seen.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first."; the athlete sets stance and guard.

Athlete moves the head off the centreline and back to the middle at a steady tempo, the head travelling a small distance, driven from the legs and trunk.

Coach raises the tempo one step at a time; the athlete keeps the same small, balanced movement at each step.

When the movement grows, the guard drops or the eyes leave the front, the coach gives one brief cue and takes the tempo back one step.

Athlete works for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
The head moves a small distance off the line and back, from the legs and trunk, not the neck.
Stance, guard and eyes look the same at the faster tempo as at the slow one.
The athlete is back in shape before the next movement.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Guard through pivot-step-reset chains
target_behavior: controlled movement with clean stops, emphasizing deceleration and balance recovery
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Wednesday applies clean stopping mechanics under coach-called direction changes.
standard_setup: Open floor; a cone or tape cross per athlete as the start spot, with a target line to face. The coach stands where hands and feet can be seen.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and athletes set stance and guard.

Coach calls a chain of pivots and steps (for example pivot, step back, step left, pivot).

Athlete moves through the chain with the guard held: lead hand at cheek/eyebrow height, rear hand at the jaw.

Athlete resets at the end of the chain facing the target; the coach checks guard and stance and gives one short cue.

Coach calls the next chain; continue for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Lead hand at cheek/eyebrow height, elbow in front of the ribs, not flared
Rear hand at the jaw, elbow tight to the ribs
what_bad_looks_like: Can the athlete pivot or change angle without collapsing posture.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Defensive set position before counter with partner-fed single attacks
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Monday introduces deliberate set position checks before any punch.
standard_setup: Pairs facing each other at the range the coach sets; the feeder wears mitts and the athlete starts in stance. The coach stands to the side of the pairs, where the feed, the athlete's feet and the counter can all be seen.
execution:
Feeder throws one single straight attack at the light touch level the coach sets.

Athlete defends with one slip, or the defense the coach names.

Athlete recovers to a set stance: feet, guard, eyes. Cue: "Get set first."

Only from that set does the athlete counter with one earned punch to the feeder's held mitt, or reset without countering.

Feeder waits until the athlete is set before the next single attack.
what_good_looks_like:
The system allows offense after defense only when the athlete has recovered enough structure to make a real choice.
Not every defense must produce an immediate counter.
The most important transfer is usable position, not flashy reply.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete counter because the picture is there or because the athlete expects every defense to become offense.
Can the athlete choose reset or reposition when that is the better answer.
Does the defensive action leave a clear scoring lane or only emotional urgency.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Exhale-freeze at movement end
target_behavior: controlled movement with clean stops, emphasizing deceleration and balance recovery
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Monday introduces directional stepping with deliberate stops.
standard_setup: Athletes in stance with room to step in all directions. The coach stands where shoulders can be seen and breathing can be heard.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and athletes set stance.

Athlete steps in the direction the coach sets and, as the movement ends, freezes in stance with one short exhale.

Athlete breathes in calmly in the freeze while the coach checks stance and shoulders.

Coach gives one short cue; the next step starts after the inhale. Continue for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Set standard in offensive chains
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Wednesday applies setting mechanics under coach-called offensive opportunities.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance facing the coach with room to step. The coach stands side-on to a group, where the set before the chain and the finish after it can both be seen.
execution:
Coach names the set standard: feet, weight, guard, chin, eyes. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete sets to that standard and holds until the coach calls the chain.

Coach calls a short offensive chain from punches the athlete has earned; the athlete throws it in shadow.

Athlete finishes back at the same set standard and holds it for the coach's check.

If the set broke, the coach names the link where it broke with one short cue.
what_good_looks_like:
The set before the chain and the set after it look the same.
No link of the chain starts from a broken stance.
The athlete can see and defend at the finish.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Slip-roll combos under live feed with partner pressure
target_behavior: controlled movement with clean stops, emphasizing deceleration and balance recovery
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Wednesday applies clean stopping mechanics under coach-called direction changes.
standard_setup: Pairs with room to move backward and to the sides: a feeder who walks forward and an athlete who defends. The coach stands to the side of the pairs, where both can be seen.
execution:
Coach states the feeder's job (slow, light straights and hooks at the set pace while walking forward, nothing harder) and gives the cue "Get set first."

Feeder moves forward and sends a slow straight or hook; the athlete slips the straight or rolls under the hook.

Athlete comes back to stance after each slip or roll and stops clean before the next feed; any touch is a light glove touch at the point the coach sets.

Coach calls changes of direction or pace for the feeder and gives one short cue to the athlete.

After the time the session plan sets, roles switch.
what_good_looks_like:
Slips stay small and rolls come from the knees, head off the centerline
Athlete stops in stance after each slip or roll, without backing straight out
Feet stay available and eyes stay on the feeder
Athlete solves each feed with the smallest move that works
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Combination clarity through volume work with high-repetition organized chains
target_behavior: deliberate action sequencing and tactical organization of offensive and defensive combinations
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Thursday maintains organized execution during complex, extended sequences under fatigue.
standard_setup: Open floor, each athlete facing a mirror, the coach, or a partner standing out of reach; shadow punches only. The coach stands where several athletes' finishes can be seen.
execution:
Coach names one organized chain (a short combination plus its finish: a defense or an exit).

Athlete sets stance with the cue "Get set first."

Athlete repeats the same chain many times in a row, each repeat ending with the defense or exit and a set stance.

As the volume builds, the athlete keeps each punch, the order and the finish clear; slower is fine.

Coach gives one short cue when a chain blurs, and the athlete continues.
what_good_looks_like: Every combination ends with either a defensive action or an exit, never with the boxer standing still admiring the work
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Full action breathing with position holds
target_behavior: maintaining positional integrity during punch execution and impact
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Wednesday applies positional discipline during combination work with targets.
standard_setup: Each athlete at a heavy bag or held mitts, or in shadow, with room to step. The coach stands where shoulders, chest and feet can be seen at each hold.
execution:
Athlete sets and breathes in. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete throws a combination on the target or in shadow, with a short exhale on each punch.

Athlete holds position at the end of the action while breathing in, and the coach checks the hold.

The next action starts only when the hold and the breath are both settled.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Set discipline during speed work with rapid but controlled combos
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Footwork establishes positional control. Thursday maintains set discipline during rapid combination work and fatigue.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in rows facing the coach with room to step. The coach stands in front, where every athlete's feet and finish position can be seen as the calls speed up.
execution:
Athlete sets and the coach checks the set. Cue: "Get set first."

Coach calls rapid but controlled combinations from punches the athlete has earned; the athlete throws them in shadow.

Athlete finishes each combination back in a set stance before the next call.

Coach slows the calls when sets are skipped, and speeds them up only while the sets hold.
what_good_looks_like:
Combinations are fast, but each one starts and ends in a set stance.
Speed drops before the set does.
Feet stay under the body at every finish.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Position-first standard under cardio load with extended combination flows
target_behavior: maintaining positional integrity during punch execution and impact
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Thursday maintains stance integrity during extended offensive sequences under fatigue.
standard_setup: Open floor or a heavy bag, with a timer and room to move. The coach stands where shoulders, feet and guard can be seen through the flow.
execution:
Athlete sets stance and breathes in before the flow. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete works an extended combination flow for the time the session plan sets: position first, then each combination, a short exhale with each punch.

After each combination the athlete returns to position before the next one starts.

Coach gives short breath and position reminders and watches for rushing as the load builds.
what_good_looks_like:
Position comes before every combination, from the start of the flow to the end.
Breathing stays with the punches.
Combinations may slow, but none starts from a broken stance.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Steady performance breathing with maintained consistency markers
target_behavior: consistent, reliable execution of all learned skills across varying conditions and fatigue levels
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Tuesday stabilizes reliable performance through repetition under varying conditions.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to shadow box. The coach stands where shoulders can be seen and breathing heard, and names the breathing markers before the round.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and names the breathing markers for the round: exhale on action, shoulders down, a calm breath to recover.

Athlete shadow boxes, repeating the work under the conditions the coach varies (pace, direction, number of punches).

Coach checks the same markers in every condition.

Between rounds the athlete recovers with a few calm breaths before the next one.

Coach gives one brief breath cue when a marker slips; the athlete works for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Performance standards through final testing with demonstrated mastery
target_behavior: consistent, reliable execution of all learned skills across varying conditions and fatigue levels
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Thursday maintains performance reliability during extended, demanding final-week testing rounds.
standard_setup: Open floor for solo work, or pairs at stop-short distance where a feeder is used. The coach stands side-on with the defensive standards to be tested.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and names the defensive standards the test covers: guard, small defence, recovery, exit.

Athlete shows each standard first fresh, then again in the extended test round.

Any feeds are shadowed and stop short; the defender recovers shape after each defence.

Coach marks each standard as shown or not shown at the end of the round, and notes the first one that failed.

Rounds follow the session plan.
what_good_looks_like:
Each defensive standard is shown fresh and again late in the test.
Every defence ends in a usable position: return, exit or reset.
Stance and guard keep working when speed drops.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Consistent execution during mixed work with coach-called random skill combinations
target_behavior: consistent, reliable execution of all learned skills across varying conditions and fatigue levels
purpose: Footwork establishes positional control. Wednesday applies consistent execution under coach-called mixed scenarios and unpredictable patterns.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to move in every direction and shadow box. The coach stands where the whole group's feet can be seen, and calls the combinations.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first."

Coach calls random combinations of skills (for example step, slip, punch, exit) and the athlete answers each call at once.

Athlete finishes every combination in stance, facing forward, guard up.

Coach keeps the calls short; when footwork breaks inside a combination, one brief cue and the call is repeated.

Athlete works for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Footwork is the same quality in every random combination.
Each combination ends in stance, balanced and looking forward.
Feet never cross or freeze while the hands work.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Optional punch introduction: straight punches in shadow boxing (Week 1)
target_behavior: maintaining stable positioning throughout all movements
purpose: Punches operate on an earned privilege system where introduction depends on demonstrated prerequisite control and positional discipline
standard_setup: available if earned through demonstrated positional control
execution: straight punches in shadow boxing only
what_good_looks_like:
Jab: Initiation without telegraph — no shoulder dip, no hand cocking, no weight shift
Jab: Straight line from the guard to the target, elbow following the hand
Jab: Rotation of the fist so the knuckles land flat, thumb turning down toward the end
Jab: Retraction faster than extension.
Rear straight: Rear foot pivots, heel turning out, ball of the foot driving into the ground
Rear straight: Hip rotates before the shoulder; shoulder before the arm — proximal to distal
Rear straight: Weight transfers onto the lead foot without falling forward
Rear straight: Immediate return to guard on the same line
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Fast breathing with action tempo in high-speed flows
target_behavior: execution tempo while maintaining technical control and positional discipline
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Wednesday applies speed with control under coach-called rapid sequences.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to shadow box flows of punches and movement. The coach stands where shoulders can be seen and breathing heard, and calls the flows.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and calls a short flow of punches and movement.

Athlete works the flow at high speed, with a short sharp exhale on each action and a breath in the gaps.

Coach calls the next flow quickly; the athlete keeps the breath tied to the tempo of the actions.

Between flows the athlete takes one calm breath and resets stance and guard.

Athlete works for the time the session plan sets; one brief breath cue when the pattern breaks.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Punch delivery while preserving stance structure
target_behavior: maintaining positional integrity during punch execution and impact
purpose: Footwork establishes positional control. Monday introduces punch delivery while preserving stance structure.
standard_setup: Open floor, one straight tape line per athlete and a short line at 45 degrees for the rear foot; athletes stand across the line in stance, facing a mirror or the coach, and punch in shadow. The coach stands side-on, where feet, hips and head can be seen as the punch goes out.
execution:
Athlete sets stance across the line. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete delivers one punch the coach names, in shadow, bringing the hand back faster than it went out.

Athlete freezes after the return; the coach checks that the feet are still on their lines, the weight is near 50/50 and the guard is back.

Coach gives one short cue to fix one thing, and the athlete punches again from the set.
what_good_looks_like:
Base width roughly shoulder-width plus a half-step, lead foot pointed slightly inward toward the opponent, rear foot at roughly 45°
Weight distribution near 50/50 at rest, shifting to demand — not permanently forward (loses the ability to move back) or permanently back (loses power and forward pressure)
Knees soft and unlocked; hips slightly under, not stuck out behind
Rear heel light, not planted, not up on the toe
what_bad_looks_like: feet too narrow (draw a line on the floor and stand across it); square to the opponent (drill from a taped 45° line); weight on the front foot (drill with the rear foot on a small pad so you can feel loading)
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Steady breathing during defensive flow with rhythm maintenance
target_behavior: composure and measured responses during defensive scenarios and incoming pressure
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Tuesday stabilizes calm defensive responses through progressive intensity drilling.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete to move; athletes work in shadow, or facing a partner who calls defensive actions without touching. The coach stands where several athletes' shoulders and breathing can be seen.
execution:
Coach gives a short breath reminder and the cue "Get set first."

Athlete flows through defensive actions in shadow (head off the line, guard adjustments, steps) at one steady rhythm set by the coach.

Athlete breathes out on each defensive action and in during the gaps, keeping the breath on the same rhythm as the movement.

Coach raises the intensity one step at a time (quicker rhythm or longer flow) only while the breathing stays steady.

At the end of each flow the athlete recovers with a few calm breaths in stance.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Defensive breathing with decision-making windows
target_behavior: composure and measured responses during defensive scenarios and incoming pressure
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Wednesday applies composed defense under live coach-called attack patterns.
standard_setup: Pairs face each other at a distance where the feeder's punches stop short; the feeder controls when a decision window opens by pausing. The coach stands side-on to see breathing and feet.
execution:
Coach gives a short breath reminder before the round and the cue "Get set first."

Feeder throws stop-short attacks; the athlete defends and breathes out with each defensive action.

Feeder then pauses: this is the decision window; the athlete takes a controlled breath in and chooses to reset in place, step to a better spot, or exit.

Athlete shows the choice calmly and sets stance before the next attack.

Coach shortens the windows only while the breathing stays steady.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Set-breathe-punch timing in combination flows
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Wednesday applies setting mechanics under coach-called offensive opportunities.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance facing the coach, with room to throw and step. The coach stands in front, where shoulders, chest and feet can be seen.
execution:
Athlete sets stance. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete breathes in once while set.

On the coach's call the athlete throws a combination flow of earned punches in shadow, a short sharp exhale with each punch.

Athlete returns to stance, breathes in, and re-sets before the next call.

Coach watches the order: set, then breath, then punch, never a punch before the set.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Composed guard adjustments with deliberate positioning
target_behavior: composure and measured responses during defensive scenarios and incoming pressure
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Tuesday stabilizes calm defensive responses through progressive intensity drilling.
standard_setup: Pairs face each other at a distance where the feeder's punches stop short; the athlete stands in stance with a high guard. The coach stands side-on to see elbows and hands.
execution:
Athlete sets stance and high guard with the cue "Get set first."

Feeder shows a slow, stop-short punch to one target; the athlete moves the guard just enough to cover that line, deliberately, without reaching for the punch.

Athlete returns the hands to the home guard: lead hand at cheek height, rear hand at the jaw, elbows in.

Athlete breathes out with each adjustment and keeps stance.

Coach raises the intensity step by step (more shows, less time between them) only while the adjustments stay small and calm.
what_good_looks_like:
Lead hand at cheek/eyebrow height, elbow in front of the ribs, not flared
Rear hand at the jaw, elbow tight to the ribs
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Controlled speed under cardio load with maintained form at high pace
target_behavior: execution tempo while maintaining technical control and positional discipline
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Thursday maintains controlled speed during extended high-tempo rounds under fatigue.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to shadow box at a high pace. The coach stands where form can be seen and breathing heard across the group.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." before each round.

Athlete shadow boxes at a high pace, exhaling with each punch and keeping stance, guard and punch form.

Athlete works in bursts with organised resets, setting posture and breath again before the next burst.

Coach keeps the pace high only while form holds; when form drops, the coach shortens the burst or lengthens the reset.

Athlete works for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Posture and punch form are still recognisable at the end of the round.
Breathing stays coachable: exhale on the punches, recovery in the resets.
The athlete still arrives in stance after each burst.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Live defense-counter-position check under partner feed
target_behavior: maintaining positional integrity during punch execution and impact
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Wednesday applies positional discipline during combination work with targets.
standard_setup: Pairs facing each other at a distance where the feeder's attacks stop short of the athlete; the feeder wears mitts. The coach stands to the side, where the defense, the counter and the athlete's position can all be seen.
execution:
Feeder throws unscripted single feeds, varying side and timing, that stop short of the athlete.

Athlete defends, then counters to the feeder's held mitt, or resets when there is no counter window.

After each exchange the athlete checks position (feet, guard, eyes) before the next feed.

Coach watches whether counters come from position or from urgency, and gives one short cue.
what_good_looks_like:
The system allows offense after defense only when the athlete has recovered enough structure to make a real choice.
Not every defense must produce an immediate counter.
The most important transfer is usable position, not flashy reply.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete counter because the picture is there or because the athlete expects every defense to become offense.
Can the athlete choose reset or reposition when that is the better answer.
Does the defensive action leave a clear scoring lane or only emotional urgency.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Target work with stance freeze after each punch
target_behavior: maintaining positional integrity during punch execution and impact
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Monday introduces punch delivery while preserving stance structure.
standard_setup: Each athlete at a target at punching range: a heavy bag, or a mitt held still by a partner or the coach. The coach stands side-on, where the feet can be seen at each freeze.
execution:
Athlete sets stance at range. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete throws one punch to the target.

Athlete freezes in stance as soon as the punch returns: feet, weight, guard, eyes on the target.

The coach or holder checks the freeze and gives one short cue; the athlete re-sets for the next punch.
what_good_looks_like:
Base width roughly shoulder-width plus a half-step, lead foot pointed slightly inward toward the opponent, rear foot at roughly 45°
Weight distribution near 50/50 at rest, shifting to demand — not permanently forward (loses the ability to move back) or permanently back (loses power and forward pressure)
Knees soft and unlocked; hips slightly under, not stuck out behind
Rear heel light, not planted, not up on the toe
what_bad_looks_like: feet too narrow (draw a line on the floor and stand across it); square to the opponent (drill from a taped 45° line); weight on the front foot (drill with the rear foot on a small pad so you can feel loading)
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Composed breathing under sustained pressure with extended defensive scenarios
target_behavior: composure and measured responses during defensive scenarios and incoming pressure
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Thursday maintains defensive composure during high-volume, extended defensive sequences.
standard_setup: Pairs with room to move; the partner keeps sustained pressure on by walking forward and throwing stop-short attacks, never touching. The coach stands where the athlete's shoulders and face can be seen and runs each scenario for the time the session plan sets.
execution:
Coach gives a short breath reminder and the cue "Get set first."

Coach names the scenario (for example, partner pressing forward, or work near an edge) and the partner keeps the pressure on through it.

Athlete defends and breathes out on each defensive action, with a controlled breath in during the gaps.

Athlete keeps the shoulders down and the breathing steady as the scenario goes on; the coach checks the breath late in the scenario as much as early.

At the end, the athlete recovers with a few calm breaths before the next scenario.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Consistent set checks in counter scenarios under fatigue
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Head Movement develops evasive capabilities. Thursday maintains set discipline during rapid combination work and fatigue.
standard_setup: Pairs facing each other at the range the coach sets, the feeder in mitts, with a timer. The coach stands to the side of the pairs and runs the fatigue block the session plan sets before the check.
execution:
The pair runs the defense-set-counter check fresh first, so the coach sees the athlete's normal set.

After the fatigue block the session plan sets, the pair runs the same check: the feeder attacks at the light touch level set, the athlete defends.

Athlete sets (feet, guard, eyes) before any counter. Cue: "Get set first."

From the set the athlete counters with one earned punch to the held mitt, or resets.

Coach compares the set with the fresh one and names the first thing that breaks.
what_good_looks_like:
The system allows offense after defense only when the athlete has recovered enough structure to make a real choice.
Not every defense must produce an immediate counter.
The most important transfer is usable position, not flashy reply.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete counter because the picture is there or because the athlete expects every defense to become offense.
Can the athlete choose reset or reposition when that is the better answer.
Does the defensive action leave a clear scoring lane or only emotional urgency.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Consistent execution under peak demand with final-week performance assessment
target_behavior: consistent, reliable execution of all learned skills across varying conditions and fatigue levels
purpose: Punch Integration synthesizes offensive techniques. Thursday maintains performance reliability during extended, demanding final-week testing rounds.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to shadow box at peak effort. The coach stands where form can be seen and breathing heard, with the assessment points listed.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and names what the assessment checks: stance, punch form, breathing and the finish.

Athlete shadow boxes at peak effort in bursts with organised resets, exhaling on each punch.

Coach checks the same points early and late in the round.

Athlete resets posture and breath between bursts before going again.

Coach notes the earliest sign of decline for each athlete; rounds follow the session plan.
what_good_looks_like:
Stance, punch form and breathing are still recognisable at peak effort.
Breathing stays coachable and the athlete recovers in the resets.
The athlete arrives in stance after each burst.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Position quality before every punch through extended rounds
target_behavior: establishing proper position before initiating offensive actions
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Thursday maintains set discipline during rapid combination work and fatigue.
standard_setup: Open floor with room to move, a timer, athletes in stance facing the coach or a mirror. The coach stands where feet and guard can be seen and watches most closely late in the round.
execution:
Athlete works through the extended round the session plan sets, in shadow or on the coach's calls.

Before every punch the athlete shows a set: feet, guard, chin. Cue: "Get set first."

Athlete throws earned punches only from that set and returns to it after each.

Coach watches late in the round for the first thing that breaks and gives one short cue.
what_good_looks_like:
Position before the last punch of the round looks like position before the first.
Speed may drop; stance and guard still work.
Every punch starts from a set.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Execution standards across all domains with full-program integration
target_behavior: consistent, reliable execution of all learned skills across varying conditions and fatigue levels
purpose: Defense builds protective instincts. Wednesday applies consistent execution under coach-called mixed scenarios and unpredictable patterns.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to move and shadow box. The coach stands where feet, guard and the finish of each scenario can be seen, and calls the scenarios.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first."

Coach calls mixed scenarios that join the four domains (move, defend, punch and breathe) in unpredictable order.

Athlete answers each scenario and finishes ready to see the next problem, back in stance.

Coach checks the standards of every domain in each scenario and gives one brief cue to the first one that fails.

Athlete works for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Every scenario ends in stance with the guard up, ready to defend.
Standards from all four domains hold together, not one at a time.
The athlete can see the next problem after each action.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.

name: Performance reliability through repeated mixed drills incorporating all weekly themes
target_behavior: consistent, reliable execution of all learned skills across varying conditions and fatigue levels
purpose: Footwork establishes positional control. Tuesday stabilizes reliable performance through repetition under varying conditions.
standard_setup: Open floor with tape lines or cones set as a short circuit of footwork drills, one per weekly theme. The coach stands where the whole circuit can be seen, or gives each assistant a watch zone.
execution:
Coach gives the cue "Get set first." and names the circuit: one footwork drill for each of the seven earlier weekly themes (Hold Position, Move and Stop Clean, Set Before Punch, Connect Without Losing Position, Stay Calm in Defense, Organize Actions, Speed With Control); the coach picks the drill for each.

Athlete works each drill in turn, then repeats the whole circuit.

Coach checks each drill against its own week's theme as the athlete passes.

When a theme fails, the coach gives one brief cue at that drill.

Athlete repeats the circuit for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Each of the seven weekly themes still shows in its own drill.
Quality is the same on the second pass of the circuit as on the first.
The athlete arrives in stance at the end of every drill.
common_errors: Sacrifice position for speed; Skip the set-check sequence; Demonstrate inconsistent breathing patterns
corrections: Coaches should intervene before poor patterns become habitual, using brief verbal cues rather than extended explanations during active drilling.
