name: Using the ropes deliberately
target_behavior: Rolling, blocking and countering from the ropes as a tactic
purpose: Teaches the ropes as a chosen position: the boxer goes to the ropes on purpose, rolls, blocks and counters there as a tactic, and leaves before the ropes become a trap. Started at low intensity.
standard_setup: Advanced only; requires excellent defense. Start at low intensity
execution:
Coach sets the roles and the intensity before the bell: start at low intensity; the partner attacks the boxer on the ropes at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer sets up on the ropes on purpose, in stance with the guard set, and defends by rolling and blocking.

Boxer counters from the ropes when the partner's attack leaves an opening.

Boxer holds on the ropes only briefly from structure, then exits, pivots off or denies.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
The ropes are a chosen spot: the boxer is calm and organised there.
Rolls and blocks leave the boxer able to counter, not shelled.
The boxer leaves the ropes on purpose (exit, pivot or deny) before they become a trap.

name: Plan A stopped working (mid-round switch)
target_behavior: On the signal, switches to a plan B built from skills already trained and boxes it with structure, instead of forcing plan A or freelancing.
purpose: Trains live re-planning: when the coach signals mid-round that plan A has stopped working, the boxer switches approach on the spot, as a bout can demand.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, boxer and partner in sparring kit. Before the round the coach and boxer agree plan A, a plan B from skills the boxer has trained, and the signal (a word or a clap) that means plan A has stopped working.
execution: “Your plan A just stopped working” — coach signals mid-round; boxer must switch approach
what_good_looks_like:
Within a few exchanges of the signal the boxer is plainly boxing a different approach.
Plan B comes from trained skills, not something new.
Stance, exits and resets hold through the switch.
The signal brings clarity, not panic or a rush of speed.

name: Dead bug, bird dog
target_behavior: Keeps the trunk still and the lower back neutral while the arms and legs move.
purpose: Trunk stability with limb movement
standard_setup: A mat. Dead bug: athlete on the back, arms up, hips and knees bent. Bird dog: athlete on hands and knees. Coach kneels side-on to see the lower back.
execution:
Dead bug: athlete braces with the lower back flat, then slowly extends one arm and the opposite leg and returns, alternating sides.

Bird dog: athlete braces on hands and knees, reaches one arm forward and the opposite leg back, holds briefly, and returns, alternating sides.

Run 2–3 × 8/side (the Long Road's prescription).

Athlete then runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The lower back stays flat (dead bug) or level (bird dog) on every rep.
The hips do not rotate or shift as the limbs move.
Reps are slow and controlled, and the boxing check after stays clean.

name: Double and triple jab
target_behavior: Second and third jab arriving off-beat
purpose: Teaches the second and third jab to arrive off the beat of the first, so a double or triple jab breaks rhythm instead of being three identical punches.
standard_setup: Bag or pads
execution:
Athlete works the bag, or a coach holds pads, at jab range in stance.

Athlete throws double and triple jabs, changing the timing so the second and third jab land off the beat of the first.

Athlete keeps the feet moving with the jabs so the hand never runs ahead of the feet, and recovers to guard after the last jab.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The second and third jab never come at the same timing as the first.
The feet stay under the jabs; the hand does not run ahead.
The athlete ends in guard, ready to exit or follow.
common_errors: Three identical jabs at identical timing

name: Medicine ball punch throw
target_behavior: Explosive punching pattern under load
purpose: Builds explosive punching power: the punching action thrown with a light medicine ball at maximum speed, a power exercise rather than a strength or conditioning one.
standard_setup: 3–4 kg ball, seated or standing
execution:
Athlete sits (back against a wall, or on a bench) or stands in stance, holding a 3–4 kg ball at the chest on the punching side.

Athlete throws the ball with the punching action, at maximum speed with full follow-through, to a wall or open space the coach sets.

Athlete rests fully between sets; this is a power exercise, not conditioning.

Run 4–6 × 3–5/side (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Every throw is maximum speed with full follow-through.
The ball stays light enough that the throw looks like a punch, not a push.
Full recovery between sets; no throwing while breathing hard.
common_errors: Heavy ball turning it into a strength exercise

name: Style guess
target_behavior: Rapid adaptation
purpose: Trains rapid adaptation: the partner is given a style in private, and the boxer must read it and adjust once the round starts.
standard_setup: Partner’s style unknown until the round starts
execution:
Before the round the coach gives the partner a style in private, set out as a few role behaviors (for example pressure forward, counter only, or move and jab).

Boxer and partner spar at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer reads the style in the opening exchanges and changes approach to suit it.

Between rounds the boxer names the style and the one thing changed.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Within the opening exchanges the boxer's approach changes to fit the partner's style.
The change is one clear adjustment, not random switching.
Between rounds the boxer can name the style and the adjustment.

name: Fatigued technical work
target_behavior: Keeps the assigned technique scoring to strict technical KPIs while tired, at moderate physical intensity, so round-3 technique holds.
purpose: Round-3 technique
standard_setup: Placed in the last 15–20 min of the session. Bag or shadow space, a clock, a phone or camera to film, and a tally sheet for the KPI (for example guard drops). The coach names the one KPI before the block.
execution:
Coach names one technical KPI (for example guard height) and how it is scored.

Athlete works the assigned technique on the bag or in shadow for the last 15–20 min of the session, at moderate physical intensity.

Coach films and counts the KPI each round (for example guard drops per round).

Coach compares the result with the same skill checked fresh earlier in the session and logs the first breakdown.
what_good_looks_like:
The KPI holds round to round (for example guard drops stay low).
The technique looks like the fresh version: slower if need be, but not broken.
The athlete still responds to one cue.

name: 20/10 punch-outs
target_behavior: Repeats maximal 20 s bursts with the guard intact, and uses each 10 s window to move and reset in guard.
purpose: Trains repeated maximal bursts with the guard kept: 20 s of maximal output, then 10 s of guard and movement, six times a round.
standard_setup: 20 s maximal, 10 s guard and move, × 6
execution:
Run in the last 15–20 minutes of a session, once the main behavior of the day is already stable.

Each round: 20 s maximal output on the bag, then 10 s guard and move, × 6.

In every 10 s window the athlete keeps the guard up and moves, resetting stance and breath.

Run 3 rounds (the Long Road's prescription); the coach watches the guard during the bursts.
what_good_looks_like:
Bursts stay at maximal output with real punches, not slaps.
The guard holds in the bursts and in the 10 s windows.
Each burst starts from an organised stance.

name: Mirror movement
target_behavior: Distance maintenance under another person’s rhythm
purpose: Trains distance maintenance under someone else's rhythm: the partner leads all movement and the boxer keeps exactly the same distance, reading and following on the feet.
standard_setup: Partner leads, boxer maintains exact distance
execution:
Partner and boxer face each other in stance at a distance the coach sets; the partner leads, the boxer follows.

Partner moves forward, back, sideways and around, changing rhythm, at the low speed the coach sets.

Boxer moves to keep exactly the same distance the whole time.

Coach watches the gap: reacting late, or drifting closer or further, is the failure mode.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
The gap stays the same whatever the partner does.
The boxer moves as the partner moves, not a beat after.
Stance holds: no crossed feet, guard up.
common_errors: Reacting late; drifting closer or further

name: Accuracy when tired
target_behavior: Lands on a small target at the same hit rate tired as fresh.
purpose: Keeps punch accuracy when tired: after conditioning, the athlete hits pads or a small target and the hit rate is scored.
standard_setup: Pads or small target after conditioning
execution:
Run in the last 15–20 minutes of a session, after conditioning, once the main behavior of the day is already stable.

Coach holds pads (or sets a small target) and shows or calls the targets.

Athlete punches for accuracy; the coach or a partner counts hits and misses each round.

Run 4 × 2 min, scored (the Long Road's prescription); compare the hit rate with the athlete's fresh rate.
what_good_looks_like:
The hit rate holds round to round and stays close to the fresh rate.
Accuracy is not traded for speed or volume.
Stance and guard stay organised between punches.

name: Hurdle hops, pogo hops, ankle stiffness work
target_behavior: Spends as little time on the ground as possible on every contact, bouncing off stiff ankles with minimal knee bend.
purpose: Builds reactive strength in the ankles and legs with quick, stiff, springy ground contacts: the fast plyometrics that follow the slow, landing-based jumps.
standard_setup: Open floor with a marker line; low hurdles for hurdle hops. Athlete stands tall, feet hip-width. Coach stands side-on to see knee bend and ground contact.
execution:
Athlete starts with pogo hops in place: jump from the ankles only, minimal knee bend, landing quietly on the balls of the feet.

Athlete keeps contacts quick and low; if contacts slow, the coach calls for faster, lighter contacts.

When pogos are clean, athlete moves to hurdle hops over low hurdles with the same quick, stiff contacts.

Coach ends the exercise the moment ground contact lengthens or jump height drops; contacts are those the session plan sets (the record gives no prescription).

After the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check; coach logs clean reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
Contacts are quick and quiet, on the balls of the feet.
The knees bend only a little; the bounce comes from the ankles.
Height and rhythm stay the same from the first contact to the last.

name: Front squat
target_behavior: Squats to depth with the torso upright and the elbows high, so the bar stays over the middle of the foot.
purpose: A squat with the bar on the front of the shoulders: a more upright torso and less compression of the spine, with more demand on the quadriceps and trunk. A useful alternative to the back squat.
standard_setup: Squat rack with the bar at upper-chest height. The bar rests on the front of the shoulders, elbows high, in a clean grip or a crossed-arm grip. Coach stands side-on.
execution:
Athlete unracks the bar, steps back to a squat stance and braces.

Athlete descends with the torso upright and elbows high, to the depth they can hold with a neutral spine.

Athlete drives up keeping the elbows up and the chest tall.

Sets, reps and load are those the session plan sets (the Long Road gives no front-squat prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The torso stays upright and the elbows do not drop.
The spine stays neutral at the bottom.
The boxing check after the lift stays clean.

name: Fatigue Integrity Test
target_behavior: Skill holds as fatigue rises, and when it breaks, the breakdown point is seen and logged.
purpose: identify when skill breaks under fatigue.
standard_setup: bag or pads with controlled bursts.
execution: maintain stance, guard, punch quality, exits under fatigue.
what_good_looks_like:
The final minute still meets the round's primary standard.
Stance, guard and exits stay usable as bursts go on; speed may drop, structure does not.
Bursts stop when form breaks, and the breakdown point is logged.
common_errors: sloppy volume.
corrections: reduce burst length or complexity.
transfer: late-round technical sparring only if contact gates pass.

name: Shoulder tag
target_behavior: Pure distance and timing
purpose: Trains distance and timing with no head impact: each boxer tries to touch the partner's shoulder without being touched.
standard_setup: Touch partner’s shoulder without being touched
execution:
Two boxers face off in stance in open space.

Each boxer tries to touch the partner's shoulder with a quick, light touch and get back out without being touched.

Both keep stance and guard; touches go to the shoulder only.

Coach scores clean touches that end with an exit and calls any touch made by lunging or leaving stance.

Run 5 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Touches land and the boxer is out before the partner can answer.
The boxer is rarely touched: distance is held just outside the partner's reach.
The feet carry the touch; no lunging or reaching from a broken stance.

name: Lateral Line Hops
target_behavior: Hops side to side over the line with small, fast, rhythmic hops on the balls of the feet, upper body quiet and balance kept.
purpose: Trains quick, small side-to-side foot speed and rhythm with a quiet upper body, to carry into light, fast boxing feet.
standard_setup: A line or marker on the floor for each athlete, with room to hop either side of it. Athletes face the coach so the coach sees the feet, the rhythm and the upper body. The time or count is what the session plan sets.
execution:
Stand next to a line or marker.
Hop side-to-side quickly over line.
Keep jumps small and fast.
Stay on balls of feet.
what_good_looks_like:
1–3 inch hops
Fast rhythm
Quiet upper body
common_errors: Common errors: jumping too high, slow rhythm, losing balance.

name: Combination Catch – 1 – 2
target_behavior: The athlete catches the partner's jab with the rear glove, returns jab-cross at once from long range, and steps back out.
purpose: Simplest counter sequence; the highest-percentage counter in boxing
standard_setup: Catch – 1 – 2
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the rep: the partner throws a single jab at the pace set; the athlete catches it and returns 1 – 2, then steps back.

Partner jabs from long range; athlete catches it with the rear glove, deflecting it rather than absorbing it.

Athlete returns the jab and the cross straight away, from the catch position.

Athlete steps back the moment the cross lands and resets stance and eyes before the next feed.

Partner feeds the picture and does not try to win the rep.
what_good_looks_like:
The catch deflects the jab with the rear glove and leaves the athlete ready to answer.
The 1 – 2 starts from the catch position, with no reset first.
The step back starts as the cross lands and ends in stance.

name: ENTRY → SCORE → EXIT (CONTINUOUS)
target_behavior: The athlete waits for a real opening on a moving partner, lands once, and exits at once, keeping the entry-exit cycle clean as fatigue builds.
purpose: find the real opening and leave clean under fatigue
standard_setup: Open floor or ring space with room to enter and leave on an angle. One partner moves lightly and presents openings; the athlete starts in stance at range. The coach stands where both the entry and the exit can be seen.
execution: 45 sec / 15 sec × 5. Partner moves lightly. Athlete finds opening, lands once, exits, re-engages.
what_good_looks_like:
The entry is balanced; the feet arrive before the hand.
One clean touch lands on a real opening, then the athlete leaves at once.
The athlete arrives back in stance before re-engaging.
The cycle stays clean in the last work periods, not only the first.
common_errors: rushed entries, reaching, sloppy exits
correction_path: slow the eyes first; clean entry beats fast entry

name: High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT)
target_behavior: Accumulates 6–12 minutes at or above 90% of maximum heart rate in the session; the protocol is only the vehicle.
purpose: central adaptation
standard_setup: A mode where intensity can be held high (running, bike, rower or curved treadmill) and a heart-rate monitor to count time above 90% of maximum. Placed 1–2×/week, year-round.
execution:
Athlete runs a fresh check of one assigned boxing task before the block.

Coach picks one protocol: 4:2 (4 min work : 2 min recovery) × 3–5, 6:3 × 3, or 8:4 × 2–3.

Athlete works each interval hard enough to reach the red zone and hold it; starting the interval faster gets there sooner.

Coach tracks time at or above 90% of maximum heart rate across the session; if it is falling short, the coach breaks intervals into short repeats or trims recovery slightly.

After the block, athlete repeats the same boxing check; coach logs the first breakdown.
what_good_looks_like:
Red-zone time reaches 6–12 minutes for the session.
The athlete reaches the red zone early in each interval and holds it.
The boxing check after the block is still trainable.

name: Add pivot after combination
target_behavior: Finishes a combination with a pivot off the lead foot to a new angle, arriving in stance facing the target with the guard back.
purpose: Primary Focus: Slip-counter integration, combination layering, ring control
standard_setup: Open floor with room to pivot, athletes in lines facing the coach; floor tape or a cone beside each athlete can mark the angle. Shadow only: no partner and no contact. The coach stands in front where feet and guards can be seen.
execution:
Coach names the combination (for example 1-2 or 1-2-3 from the same Technical Block) and shows the lead-foot pivot that follows it.

Athlete throws the combination in shadow and, as the last punch returns, pivots off the lead foot to a new angle.

Athlete arrives in stance facing the target, guard up, and holds it for a beat so the coach can check.

Athlete repeats for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Pivoting off the lead foot to create angles after a combination
Every combination ends with either a defensive action or an exit, never with the boxer standing still admiring the work
what_bad_looks_like: Can the athlete pivot or change angle without collapsing posture.

name: Defense First Round
target_behavior:
reading punches
calm reactions
proper defensive technique
immediate transition from defense to offense
purpose: Develop defensive reactions and composure.
standard_setup:
Athlete A attacks first.
Athlete B must defend before throwing punches.
execution:
Athlete B defends using:
slip
parry
step back
catch or block if appropriate
After defending, athlete B may counter.
Athletes alternate roles.
what_good_looks_like:
Athlete B sees the punch with eyes open and defends with a small, balanced action.
No flinching away; B stays in stance.
B answers only after the defense, from recovered balance.
The roles hold: A attacks first, B defends first.

name: No punch from a stationary position
target_behavior: Punching on the move
purpose: Teaches punching on the move: a punch thrown from standing still does not count, so the boxer learns to throw while moving forward, back and to both sides. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: No punch may be thrown from a stationary position
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: no punch may be thrown from a stationary position, and a punch from set feet is called and does not count; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer throws only while the feet are travelling: forward, back, to either side or circling.

Partner boxes at the agreed pace; the boxer defends as usual and keeps moving into the next punch.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Punches land while the feet are travelling, in every direction.
The boxer never stops to punch and then moves.
Stance holds while punching on the move.

target_behavior: Boxes the assigned style recognisably for the whole round while keeping the system's stance, exits and resets.
purpose: Builds a second mode by making the boxer box a full round in a style that is not their own.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, a partner in sparring kit. Before the round the coach assigns the style by its behaviours (for example a pressure fighter closes distance continuously and throws in volume), not by naming a boxer to copy.
execution: Assigned-style rounds: box a full round as a style that is not your own
what_good_looks_like:
The style is recognisable from the first exchange to the last bell.
The boxer shows the style's key behaviours, not a caricature of it.
Stance, exits and resets stay clean inside the new style.
The round stays on its declared purpose.

name: Band-resisted head rotation and anti-rotation
target_behavior: Turns the head smoothly against the band and, in anti-rotation, keeps it from being turned, with the chin level and the shoulders still.
purpose: Trains the neck to turn the head against a band and to resist being turned, as part of the warm-up neck work.
standard_setup: A light band anchored at head height to the athlete's side, attached to a head harness or padded headband. Athlete stands tall side-on to the anchor. Coach stands in front to see head and shoulder line.
execution:
Rotation: athlete turns the head away from the anchor against the band, slowly, and returns under control.

Anti-rotation: athlete holds the head facing forward while the band pulls toward the anchor; stepping away from the anchor adds tension.

Athlete turns to face the other way and repeats both.

Run 2 × 10 each direction (the Long Road's prescription).

Athlete then runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the exposure and the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The head turns smoothly with no jerk against the band.
In anti-rotation the head does not drift toward the anchor.
The shoulders and trunk stay still, and the boxing check after shows no stiffness or guard loss.

name: Breathing rhythm coupled to punching
target_behavior: Exhales sharply on every punch and breathes in fully between combinations, without holding the breath.
purpose: Ties breathing to punching, a short sharp exhale with each punch and a full breath in the gaps, so the boxer stops holding the breath in exchanges.
standard_setup: Shadowboxing space, a bag or pads. The coach stands close enough to hear the exhale on each punch and to see the shoulders.
execution: Short sharp exhale with each punch; full breath in the gaps. Boxers who hold their breath during exchanges are the ones whose arms fill up.
what_good_looks_like:
Every punch has its own short, audible exhale.
Between combinations the athlete takes a full breath.
Shoulders stay down; the arm is relaxed between punches and firm at impact.
Late in the round the pattern is still there.

name: Progressive muscular relaxation
target_behavior: Releases tension on purpose, first through the whole body, then at the jaw, shoulders and hands in a quick check between exchanges.
purpose: Teaches the athlete to feel the difference between tension and release, muscle group by muscle group, then shrinks it to a quick jaw, shoulders and hands check usable in the ring.
standard_setup: A quiet floor space with mats, athletes lying or sitting. The coach talks the group through the muscle groups in order and stands where faces and hands can be seen.
execution: Full-body protocol: tense each muscle group 5 s, release 15 s, moving systematically - Then build an abbreviated version usable in the ring: jaw, shoulders, hands — three checkpoints you can run in two seconds between exchanges
what_good_looks_like:
Each muscle group is clearly tensed, then clearly let go.
After the release the athlete looks softer: jaw unclenched, shoulders down, hands open.
In the ring version the three checkpoints are done in about two seconds.

name: Jump squat
target_behavior: Maximum intent on every rep: the athlete tries to jump as high as possible every time.
purpose: Builds lower-body explosive power: a fast dip and a maximal jump, at bodyweight or with a light load, with full recovery between sets.
standard_setup: Open floor; a bar or dumbbells when loaded (20–40% 1RM). Athlete stands with feet about hip- to shoulder-width. Coach stands side-on to see the dip, the jump and the landing.
execution: rapid countermovement, maximal jump, soft landing, reset between reps
what_good_looks_like:
Every jump is a maximal effort.
The landing is soft, and the athlete resets before the next rep.
The reset or skill check after the set shows no stance collapse or delayed reset.

name: Pressure vs Counter Drill
target_behavior: Each athlete holds the assigned role for the whole round: the pressure athlete takes space with angles without chasing, and the counter athlete keeps distance and answers rather than leads.
purpose: One athlete pressures while the other counters.
standard_setup: Ring or open space with room to move. Two athletes face each other in stance, in the sparring gear the gym uses; the coach names who pressures and who counters before the bell. The coach stands outside the action where both athletes' feet and tempo can be seen, with a clock for the round.
execution:
Assign clear roles before round begins.
Pressure athlete advances using angles.
Counter athlete maintains distance and responds.
Switch roles next round.
what_good_looks_like:
The pressure athlete walks forward behind the feet and cuts angles, ready to score, without chasing or throwing out of frustration.
The counter athlete keeps distance and answers what the pressure athlete shows.
Tempo stays controlled and both athletes stay in their roles for the whole round.

name: Combination 1 – 2 – 3 – 2
target_behavior: From long into mid range the athlete commits to all four punches of 1 – 2 – 3 – 2, ends the scoring phase on the last cross, and steps off at an angle at once.
purpose: Full commitment sequence for a hurt opponent
execution:
Coach names the sequence and its exit before the rep: 1 – 2 – 3 – 2, then step off at an angle.

Athlete starts in stance at long range (shadow, bag or pads); jab and cross close the distance.

Athlete lands the lead hook in the closed distance and finishes with the cross.

Athlete steps off at an angle the moment the last cross lands: the final shot ends the scoring phase, with nothing added.

Athlete resets stance and eyes before the next rep; the coach moves the sequence up the coupling ladder only when it holds.
what_good_looks_like:
All four punches are committed, and stance holds through the hook and the last cross.
The last cross is the visible end of the exchange; nothing is added after it.
The step off at an angle starts as the last cross lands and ends in stance.

name: Jump Lunge (after iso)
target_behavior: Jumps straight up from split-squat depth, switches legs, and lands softly back at the same depth, stable at once.
purpose: Turns the tension built in the split-squat iso hold into explosive leg power: jump, switch legs and land in control in the same position.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete to jump and land in a long split stance, straight after the split-squat iso hold. Athletes side-on to the coach so the coach sees take-off, landing and torso. The rep count is what the session plan sets.
execution:
Start in split squat position.
Explode upward and switch legs mid-air.
Land softly and immediately stabilize.
Keep torso controlled.
what_good_looks_like:
Start at split squat depth
Jump straight up
Land softly at same depth
common_errors: Common errors: crashing into ground, losing balance, shallow movement.
corrections: Fix: Crashing → absorb | Off balance → control landing

name: Cue words for relaxation
target_behavior: Hears or says the cue word and produces the matching relaxed state, in training and later under pressure.
purpose: Builds two or three cue words that switch on a relaxed state, by pairing each word with that state over and over in training so it works under pressure.
standard_setup: Any session. The athlete picks two or three words with the coach (for example “loose,” “breathe,” “long,” “soft hands”), and the coach writes them down so every coach uses the same words.
execution: Anchor 2–3 words during training (“loose,” “breathe,” “long,” “soft hands”) and deploy them in competition - The anchoring matters: the word must be paired with the physical state hundreds of times in training before it will produce the state under pressure
what_good_looks_like:
Each word produces a visible change: shoulders drop, hands soften, breathing slows.
The same two or three words are used every session.
Under pressure the word still works.

name: CONTINUOUS TOUCH → EXIT
target_behavior: The athlete lands one touch and leaves at once, with no second punch, no delay and no stopped feet, keeping the loop moving.
purpose: one action then immediate exit at pace
standard_setup: Use open floor space or ring space. One feeder or partner presents a stable target or controlled live picture. Athlete starts in stance with enough room to enter, score, and leave on angle or line.
execution: 30 sec on / 15 sec off × 4. Step in → jab → exit → re-engage. Keep the loop moving.
what_good_looks_like:
Entry is balanced and hand placement does not outrun foot position.
Scoring action is clear enough that a coach can identify the end of the exchange.
Exit happens immediately, not after a pause.
Athlete arrives in stance after the reposition.
what_bad_looks_like:
Athlete lands then watches the result instead of leaving.
Athlete drifts forward after contact.
Athlete exits without balance and needs extra steps to recover.
Entry becomes longer and sloppier over repeated reps.
common_errors: delayed exits, second punches, feet stopping

name: No stepping forward
target_behavior: Working off the back foot
purpose: Teaches working off the back foot: with no forward step allowed, the boxer has to score while giving or holding ground, using feet, angles and counters against a partner who comes forward. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Boxer may not step forward
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the boxer may not step forward, and a forward step is called; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Partner comes forward at the agreed pace; the boxer moves back, sideways and pivots, but never steps forward.

Boxer scores as the partner comes in when the counter picture is clean, then leaves on an angle rather than straight back.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer scores while going back or sideways, from balance.
Angles and pivots replace backing straight up.
The boxer reads the partner's pressure instead of reacting to it.

name: Romanian deadlift
target_behavior: Hinges from the hips with a neutral spine and minimal knee bend, stopping where hamstring tension limits range.
purpose: Trains the hip hinge and the posterior chain, loading the hamstrings at length.
standard_setup: Barbell (or dumbbells) held at the hips, feet about hip-width, knees soft. Coach stands side-on to see the back and the bar path.
execution: hips back, minimal knee bend, bar tracing the thighs, descend until hamstring tension limits range with a neutral spine, drive hips forward
what_good_looks_like:
The bar stays on the thighs all the way down and up.
The spine stays neutral, and range ends where hamstring tension stops it.
It stays a hinge, not a squat or a back extension, and the boxing check after is clean.
common_errors: turning it into a squat or a back extension

name: 1–2 progression with balance check
target_behavior: Throws the 1-2 as one action with two contacts and finishes balanced in stance, guard back after every punch.
purpose: Primary Focus: Foundational stance, jab, pivot automation
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in lines facing the coach with room to step. Shadow only: no partner and no contact. The coach stands in front, then walks the lines, checking feet and guards at each balance check.
execution:
Coach demonstrates the 1-2 as one action with two contacts, the rear foot turning on the 2.

Athlete throws the 1-2 in shadow and freezes in stance after the 2: the balance check.

Coach checks the freeze: weight not falling forward, feet not crossed or narrow, both hands back at the guard.

Athlete repeats for the time the session plan sets, adding speed only while the balance check holds.
what_good_looks_like:
Jab: Initiation without telegraph — no shoulder dip, no hand cocking, no weight shift
Jab: Straight line from the guard to the target, elbow following the hand
Jab: Rotation of the fist so the knuckles land flat, thumb turning down toward the end
Jab: Retraction faster than extension.
Rear straight: Rear foot pivots, heel turning out, ball of the foot driving into the ground
Rear straight: Hip rotates before the shoulder; shoulder before the arm — proximal to distal
Rear straight: Weight transfers onto the lead foot without falling forward
Rear straight: Immediate return to guard on the same line
1-2 as a coupled unit. Not two punches; one action with two contacts. Then 1-1-2, 1-2 with a step, 1-2 and out.
what_bad_looks_like: Does the athlete lose balance whenever the hands start working.

name: Corner Escape Drill
target_behavior: The defender leaves the ropes or corner with a pivot or angle, not a straight-line retreat, and arrives balanced in a better spot within 5 seconds.
purpose: Defender escapes from ropes or corner under light pressure.
standard_setup: Ring with ropes and corners, or a wall space used as the edge. The defender starts in stance near the ropes; the pressure partner starts in stance in front and advances without punching. The coach stands to the side where the defender's feet and exit line can be seen, counting the 5 seconds.
execution:
Defender starts near ropes.
Pressure partner advances without punching.
Defender pivots or angles out within 5 seconds.
Reset position and repeat.
what_good_looks_like:
The defender pivots or angles off early and calmly, before being pinned.
The defender arrives balanced, in stance, with eyes on the partner.
The defender never backs straight along the line into the ropes or corner.

name: 1-second rule
target_behavior: Defense-to-counter coupling
purpose: Couples defense to counter under live pressure: a defensive action counts only when a return follows within a second, so defenses stop ending dead.
standard_setup: A defensive action only scores if followed by a return within 1 s
execution:
Coach sets the rule before the bell: a defensive action scores only if a return follows within 1 s; the coach or a scorer keeps the count.

Boxer and partner spar at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer defends, then returns inside the second; a defense with no return in time does not score.

Coach scores every round out loud or on a tally; the constraint only works if it is enforced.

Run 5 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 6).
what_good_looks_like:
Defensive actions are followed by a return inside the second.
Returns come from position, not from a scramble to beat the clock.
The score kept matches what the coach saw.
common_errors: Not scoring it — the constraint only works if enforced

name: Punch-on-the-move
target_behavior: Throwing while moving forward, back, and both laterals
purpose: Teaches the boxer to punch while moving forward, back and to both sides, so punching never needs the feet to stop.
standard_setup: Open floor
execution:
Athlete shadowboxes on open floor in stance.

Athlete punches while travelling forward, back, left and right, landing the punches during the step, not after it.

Coach calls out any punch thrown from a stationary position; stopping to punch, then moving, is the failure mode.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Punches land while the feet travel, in all four directions, including while retreating and circling.
The stance holds while punching on the move.
No stop-punch-move pattern.
common_errors: Stopping to punch, then moving

name: Pivot off the lead foot after the 1-2
target_behavior: Throws the 1-2 and pivots off the lead foot to finish across the tape, in stance and facing the target.
purpose: Teaches one new item, the pivot off the lead foot after the 1-2, so the boxer finishes off the line and across the tape, first in shadow, then on pads on an unpredictable cue.
standard_setup: Coach demonstration and constraint setup: a strip of tape on the floor the boxer must end up across
execution:
4 × 2 min shadow with the constraint, mirror feedback
3 × 2 min on pads with the coach feeding an unpredictable cue for when to pivot
what_good_looks_like:
The 1-2 lands, then the pivot comes off the lead foot without a pause.
The boxer finishes across the tape, where the partner's shoulder was.
Guard and base are usable at the finish.
On pads the pivot comes on the coach's cue, not early.

name: Combination Pull – 1 – 2
target_behavior: The athlete pulls back so the partner's jab falls short, lands jab-cross as the partner recovers, and steps in or off.
purpose: They fall short; you land as they recover
standard_setup: Pull – 1 – 2
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the rep: the partner throws a single jab at the pace set; the athlete pulls, returns 1 – 2, then steps in or off.

Partner jabs from long range; athlete pulls back with weight to the rear foot and hands up, just enough for the jab to fall short.

Athlete returns the jab and the cross as the partner recovers.

Athlete steps in or off as the cross lands and resets stance and eyes before the next feed.

Partner feeds the picture and does not try to win the rep.
what_good_looks_like:
The pull is just far enough for the jab to fall short, with the hands up.
The 1 – 2 lands as the partner recovers, not after the athlete resets.
The step in or off ends in stance.

name: Sled pushes and short sprints
target_behavior: Drives forward with full intent on every rep, pushing back into the ground, and keeps every rep explosive rather than tired.
purpose: Builds horizontal force, driving forward hard against a sled or over a short sprint: the quality used to close distance.
standard_setup: A sled on turf or a clear lane for sprints, with start and finish markers. Coach stands at the side to see body lean and foot strike.
execution:
Coach sets the sled load and distance, or the sprint distance, from the session plan (the record gives no prescription).

Sled: athlete leans into the sled with arms long, drives the legs back into the ground and pushes at full intent to the marker.

Sprint: athlete starts from a set position and accelerates hard to the marker, then slows down gradually.

Athlete recovers between reps so every rep stays explosive.

After the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check; coach logs clean explosive reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
Every rep is a full-intent drive; speed and push do not fade within the set.
Body lean and leg drive stay strong to the marker.
The reset check after shows no stance collapse or delayed reset.

name: Pre-activation drill — brace on a cue, absorb a light controlled perturbation
target_behavior: Braces the neck on the cue, before the push arrives, and holds head position through a light controlled perturbation.
purpose: Trains the neck to brace on a signal and then absorb a light, controlled push, so the bracing response is quick and ready.
standard_setup: Athlete in stance wearing headgear. The coach stands in front within arm's reach to give a light push on the headgear, or a swinging bag is set to give a light tap. The coach agrees the cue types (visual and auditory) before starting.
execution:
Coach shows the cue types: a visual cue (for example a raised hand) and an auditory cue (for example a call).

On the cue, athlete braces the neck: chin tucked, neck firm, eyes forward.

Coach then gives a light, controlled push on the headgear (or the swinging bag gives a light tap); athlete holds head position.

Run 2 × 5 per cue type (the Long Road's prescription).

Athlete then runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the exposure.
what_good_looks_like:
The brace comes on the cue, before the push.
The head moves little on the push and returns to position at once.
The push stays light and controlled on every rep.

name: One-step
target_behavior: Precise distance judgment
purpose: Sharpens distance judgment in live work: with only one step allowed at a time, every step has to be the right size and direction.
standard_setup: Neither boxer may take more than one step at a time
execution:
Coach sets the rule: neither boxer may take more than one step at a time; spar at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Each step is a single step-and-slide that finishes in stance before the next.

Boxers enter, defend and exit within the one-step rule.

Coach calls any double step, shuffle or run.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Every step finishes in stance before the next starts.
The boxer lands and leaves with single steps, so distance is set by choice, not by chasing.
Feet prepare each punch before the hands go.

name: Step-Slide Footwork
target_behavior: Every step keeps the stance: lead foot first, back foot follows, feet never cross, in every direction.
purpose: Builds the basic boxing step: the lead foot moves first and the back foot follows, forward, back and sideways, so the athlete moves without crossing the feet or losing stance.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete to move forward, back and to both sides; no partner. The coach stands in front where every athlete's feet can be seen.
execution: Step-slide movement.
what_good_looks_like:
The lead foot moves first and the back foot follows on every step.
The feet never cross and the stance stays the same width.
Knees stay bent and hands stay up while moving.

name: Combination 3 – 2
target_behavior: From mid range the lead hook moves the guard sideways, the cross goes straight through the gap it leaves, and the athlete pivots out.
purpose: Hook displaces guard; cross through the gap
execution:
Coach names the sequence and its exit before the rep: 3 – 2, then pivot.

Athlete starts in stance at mid range (shadow, bag or pads) and throws a short lead hook that returns through the guard.

Athlete sends the cross straight through the gap the hook opened.

Athlete pivots out the moment the cross lands and resets stance and eyes before the next rep.

Coach moves the sequence up the coupling ladder only when it holds at the current rung.
what_good_looks_like:
The hook is short and comes back through the guard; it does not swing wide.
The cross travels the straight line the hook opened.
The pivot starts as the cross lands and ends facing the target in stance.

name: Partner is instructed to do the specific thing the boxer struggles with
target_behavior: Stays composed and keeps working trained answers to the problem the partner keeps giving, instead of rushing, freezing, retaliating or backing straight out.
purpose: Builds adversity tolerance in sparring: the partner is told to do the one thing the boxer handles worst, so the boxer practises solving it under live pressure instead of avoiding it.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, both boxers in sparring kit. Before the round the coach tells the partner the one behaviour to keep giving (for example edge pressure, a rhythm break, a long-guard picture) and at what pace; the coach stands where both can be seen.
execution:
Coach picks the one problem the boxer struggles with most and defines it as a behaviour the partner can repeat.

Coach briefs the partner on that behaviour and the pace, at controlled-sparring level.

Partner keeps giving the problem through the round; the boxer works the answers they have trained.

Between rounds the coach gives one correction tied to an existing cue and one success condition.

Coach logs what held and what broke.
what_good_looks_like:
The partner's problem shows up clearly, again and again.
The boxer keeps stance and breathing while solving it.
The boxer uses trained answers (feet, angles, resets), not panic or retaliation.
The round stays a lesson, not a fight about the weakness.

name: Round starts with 30 seconds left, boxer losing
target_behavior: Urgency management
purpose: Teaches urgency management: the round starts with 30 seconds left and the boxer behind, so the boxer has to raise output and win the closing seconds without throwing away structure.
standard_setup: Round starts with 30 s remaining, boxer is losing
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the round starts with 30 seconds on the clock and the coach tells the boxer the (made-up) score they are behind by; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Partner boxes normally at the agreed pace; the boxer must win the 30 seconds.

Boxer raises output from the bell with clean, visible work, feet first, and does not chase or lunge to catch up.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
Output rises from the first second, not after a slow start.
The extra work is clean and visible; feet still set up the hands.
The boxer does not chase: urgency is not confused with opportunity.

name: Shot clock
target_behavior: Reduces hesitation and range-drifting
purpose: Removes hesitation in range: once the boxer enters range they must throw within 3 s, so range is used, not drifted through.
standard_setup: Must throw within 3 s of entering range
execution:
Coach sets the rule: once in range, the boxer must throw within 3 s; partner spars at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Coach counts out loud from the moment the boxer enters range.

Boxer throws from balance inside the count, then exits or resets.

If the count runs out, the coach calls it and the boxer resets outside range.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer throws within the count every time range is entered.
The punches come from balance, not lunges to beat the clock.
The boxer does not drift in and out of range without throwing.

name: Rope Escape Situation
target_behavior:
footwork
defensive movement
composure under pressure
escaping without panic
purpose: Develop ring awareness and escape movement.
standard_setup: One athlete begins near the ropes.
execution:
Athlete must:
pivot
angle step
step around opponent
re establish center ring position
Athletes switch roles each round.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete at the ropes escapes by pivot, angle step or stepping around, not by backing straight out.
The escape arrives in a balanced stance with eyes up, and the athlete retakes the center.
The escape looks calm and early, not like running away.

name: Handicap rounds
target_behavior: The stronger boxer boxes the weakest mode with structure for the whole round, without slipping back into the strong mode when it gets hard.
purpose: Evens a mismatched pair and trains the stronger boxer's weakest mode: the more skilled boxer must fight the round in the mode they are worst at.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, a more skilled and a less skilled boxer in sparring kit. Before the round the coach names the stronger boxer's weakest mode (for example going backwards, or close range).
execution: Handicap rounds: the more skilled boxer must fight in their weakest mode
what_good_looks_like:
The stronger boxer stays in the weak mode all round.
The less skilled boxer still gets usable rounds, not a beating.
The stronger boxer's stance and exits hold in the weak mode.

name: Guard retention under fire
target_behavior: Guard integrity when hit
purpose: Builds a guard that holds when shots land: the partner throws light, continuous work and the boxer's only job is to keep the guard and keep defending.
standard_setup: Partner throws at 30% continuously; boxer only defends
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the bell: the partner throws at 30% continuously; the boxer only defends.

Partner keeps a steady flow of light shots at the set pace; the partner does not speed up or throw harder.

Boxer keeps the guard in place, eyes up and feet working, and finishes each defense back in shape; a defense may end in a return, an exit or a reset (the record's rule).

Coach calls out any guard drop or squaring up.

Run 4 × 60 s (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
The guard stays at its set height while shots land and the hands come back to it after every block or catch.
The boxer keeps moving and seeing; no turning square, no freezing.
Each defense finishes in a usable stance.
common_errors: Partner throwing too hard; boxer allowed to move away

name: Jab-to-the-eyes drill
target_behavior: Accuracy on a moving small target
purpose: Sharpens jab accuracy on a small target that moves at head height: a partner moves a focus mitt so the jab has to find it.
standard_setup: Partner with focus mitt held at head height, moving
execution:
Partner holds one focus mitt at head height and moves it, and their feet, so the target never sits still.

Athlete jabs to the mitt from stance, adjusting feet and range to the moving target, and recovers to guard after each jab.

Coach checks the holder: a static target is the drill's failure mode, so the mitt keeps moving in a way the athlete can still learn from.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 4).
what_good_looks_like:
The jab lands clean on the mitt wherever it moves.
The athlete adjusts with the feet, not by reaching.
Guard and stance are back after every jab.
common_errors: Static target

name: Cut-off drill
target_behavior: Trap the partner in a corner within 30 s
purpose: Teaches cutting off a moving partner: stepping to where the partner is going, not following where they are, to trap them in a corner.
standard_setup: Partner must move continuously
execution:
Coach sets the space (ring or marked area) and the roles: the partner must move continuously and stay out of the corners; the boxer works to trap the partner in a corner.

Boxer cuts across the partner's line, stepping to where the partner is going, and closes the escape lanes on the feet, without punching.

Coach times each rep; the trap must come within 30 s.

Run 6 reps (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer cuts across the line instead of following behind.
The boxer stays calm and in stance while the partner keeps moving.
The partner ends in a corner inside the time.
common_errors: Chasing — following where they are instead of stepping where they’re going

name: Secret style change at 90 seconds
target_behavior: Notices the partner's style change quickly and changes their own approach to fit it, keeping structure.
purpose: Trains live re-planning: the partner switches style at the 90-second mark without the boxer knowing, so the boxer must notice the change and adapt within the round.
standard_setup: Ring and timer with a clock the coach can watch; both boxers in sparring kit. Out of the boxer's hearing, the coach gives the partner the style to switch to at the 90-second mark, described by its behaviours.
execution: Partner receives secret instructions to change style at the 90-second mark
what_good_looks_like:
Within a few exchanges of the change the boxer has seen it and is boxing differently.
The boxer's answer fits the new style.
Structure holds through the switch; the change brings clarity, not panic.

name: Push-hands entry
target_behavior: Denying range
purpose: Trains denying range: the partner tries to touch the boxer's chest and the boxer frames and steps off, so the partner never settles at their distance.
standard_setup: Partner tries to touch boxer’s chest; boxer frames and steps off
execution:
Partner tries to touch the boxer's chest at the pace the coach sets.

Boxer frames with the forearm to stop the reach, then steps off at an angle.

Boxer resets in stance facing the partner, ready for the next attempt.

Coach calls any time the boxer backs straight up or lets the partner settle.

Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The frame meets the partner's reach before it lands on the chest.
The step-off takes the boxer to a new angle, not straight back.
The boxer finishes in stance facing the partner.

name: Manual resistance or harness dynamic work — all planes
target_behavior: Moves the head through each plane at a steady, controlled tempo against even resistance, with no jerking.
purpose: Builds neck strength through full movement in every plane (forward, back and to each side) against a partner's hand or a neck harness, at a controlled tempo.
standard_setup: Manual: athlete seated or kneeling tall; a partner or coach places a hand on the forehead, the back or the side of the head. Harness: athlete seated or braced over a bench with a light load on a head harness. Coach watches tempo and trunk position.
execution:
Athlete starts with the head in neutral, chin level.

Manual: the partner gives steady resistance while the athlete moves the head slowly through range forward, back, and to each side; the partner matches force so the movement stays slow.

Harness: the athlete moves the head through the same planes against the harness load at the same slow tempo.

Run 2 × 10 each, controlled tempo (the Long Road's prescription).

Athlete then runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the exposure and the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The tempo is slow and even in every plane, with no jerks.
The trunk stays still; only the head and neck move.
The boxing check after shows no stiffness, posture collapse or guard loss.

name: Ladder in stance
target_behavior: Foot speed while maintaining boxing stance
purpose: Builds foot speed without giving up the boxing stance: agility-ladder footwork done in stance, where speed never comes at the cost of the stance.
standard_setup: Agility ladder
execution:
Coach lays out an agility ladder; the athlete starts at one end in boxing stance, guard up.

Athlete moves through the ladder with step-and-slide footwork, forward, back and laterally, without crossing the feet or bouncing off both feet.

Coach stops a rep where the stance is abandoned for speed; that is the drill's failure mode.

Run 6 × 30 s (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The feet move fast while the stance stays a boxing stance.
No crossed feet, no bouncing off both feet; the guard stays up.
Speed rises only as far as the stance holds.
common_errors: Abandoning stance to move faster — defeats the point

name: Compound feint live drill
target_behavior: Draws a first reaction, then a counter-reaction with a second feint, and lands the real shot from balance; or resets when the reaction does not come.
purpose: Trains the compound feint live: one feint draws a reaction, a second draws the counter-reaction, then the real shot, scored on whether the second reaction was drawn.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, both boxers in sparring kit, working at the drill's 50%. The coach keeps a simple count of second reactions drawn and stands where the partner's reactions can be seen.
execution: Live drill at 50%, scored on whether the second reaction was drawn
what_good_looks_like:
The first feint draws a readable reaction; the second draws the counter-reaction.
The real shot follows the second reaction, not a guess.
The boxer stays balanced after each feint.
When no reaction comes, the boxer resets instead of forcing the shot.

name: Explosive Push-Ups
target_behavior: Lowers to full depth under control, explodes up with intent, and lands softly with the body still in one line.
purpose: Turns push-up tension into explosive upper-body power: lower under control, then push the floor away fast.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete in push-up position, straight after the push-up iso hold. Athletes side-on to the coach so the coach sees depth, hips and landing. The rep count is what the session plan sets.
execution:
Start in push-up position.
Lower under control, then explode up.
Hands may leave ground slightly.
Land and absorb force softly.
what_good_looks_like:
Full depth then explode
Hands may leave ground
Soft elbow landing
common_errors: Common errors: sagging hips, partial range, slow intent.

name: Jab Only Sparring
target_behavior:
distance management
timing
defensive reactions
rhythm
purpose: Develop distance control, timing, and footwork.
standard_setup: Two athletes spar normally but only the jab is allowed.
execution:
Athletes move and box normally while using only the lead hand.
Athletes should:
step in to jab
step out after jab
circle after punching
defend incoming jabs with head movement, parry, or foot movement
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete steps in to jab without reaching, then steps out or circles after punching.
The guard stays up and the athlete never stands still after scoring.
Incoming jabs are defended with head movement, parry or feet.
Only the lead hand is used, all round.

name: Foot feint — draw a reaction without entering
target_behavior: Draws the partner's reaction with a half-step or weight shift alone, staying in stance and out of range.
purpose: Trains the foot feint: a half-step or weight shift that reads as an entry and draws a reaction, without the boxer actually entering.
standard_setup: Open floor or ring, boxer and partner in stance just outside entry range. Before the round the coach tells the partner their only job: react when they read an entry. The coach stands side-on to see the boxer's feet and the partner's reaction.
execution: Partner reacts to entries only; boxer scores by drawing a reaction without entering. 3 × 2 min
what_good_looks_like:
The half-step or weight shift draws a clear reaction from the partner.
The boxer never actually crosses into range.
After each feint the boxer is balanced and ready.
The partner cannot tell the feint from a real entry.

name: Combination 1 – 2 – pivot
target_behavior: The athlete scores with the 1 – 2 from long into mid range and changes the angle at once by pivoting off the lead foot.
purpose: Score and immediately change the angle
standard_setup: 1 – 2 – pivot
execution:
Coach names the sequence and its exit before the rep: 1 – 2, then pivot off the lead foot.

Athlete starts in stance at long range (shadow, bag or pads) and throws the 1 – 2 as one action with two contacts.

Athlete pivots off the lead foot as the cross lands: the rear foot travels, the lead foot stays.

Athlete finishes the pivot facing the target, resets stance and eyes, and goes again.

Coach moves the sequence up the coupling ladder only when it holds at the current rung.
what_good_looks_like:
The 1 – 2 is one action with two contacts.
The pivot starts as the cross lands, off the lead foot, with the rear foot travelling.
The athlete ends on the new angle facing the target, balanced and in stance.

name: Body Shot Round
target_behavior:
bending knees
positioning
safe entry
maintaining defense while attacking low
purpose: Develop level changes, positioning, and safe entry.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Two athletes face each other in stance in the gear the Friday sheet names (wraps, headgear, gloves). The coach states the rule before the bell (only body punches score) and stands side-on where both athletes' head position and knees can be seen.
execution:
Athletes must:
change levels
move inside safely
keep head off center
exit after punching
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete changes levels by bending the legs, not the waist.
The head stays off center on the way in and the athlete does not fall in.
The athlete exits after the body shot with the guard still in place.
Only body punches are thrown to score.

name: Attentional shifting drill
target_behavior: Switches attention at once between wide (the whole room) and narrow (one target) on the call, while the punching keeps going with good form.
purpose: Trains deliberate shifts of attention: while working the bag, the boxer switches between a wide scan of the room and a single narrow target on the coach's call.
standard_setup: Heavy bags with open space around them so the room can be scanned. The coach stands where they can call clearly and see the boxers' eyes.
execution: During bag work, the coach calls “wide” (scan the whole room while continuing to work) or “narrow” (single target only) at random intervals. 3 × 2 min
what_good_looks_like:
On “wide” the eyes lift and scan the room while the hands keep working.
On “narrow” the eyes lock on one target on the bag.
The switch is immediate and the punching does not stop.
The boxer does not drift into judging how they are doing.

name: Medicine ball overhead slam and chest pass
target_behavior: Throws the ball at maximum speed with full effort on every rep, and finishes balanced and ready.
purpose: Builds general upper-body ballistic power: slamming a medicine ball down from overhead and passing it hard from the chest. Easy to load and progress.
standard_setup: A medicine ball (a slam ball for slams) and a solid wall for chest passes, on open floor. Coach stands side-on to see the throw and the finish.
execution:
Overhead slam: athlete lifts the ball overhead, then slams it into the floor as hard as possible, hinging with the throw.

Chest pass: athlete faces the wall in a balanced stance and drives the ball from the chest into the wall at maximum speed, catching the rebound.

Athlete resets to a balanced stance, hands up, between reps.

Sets and reps are those the session plan sets (the record gives no prescription).

After the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check; coach logs clean explosive reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
Every throw is fast and full effort.
After each throw the athlete is balanced, hands back up, ready to go again.
The reset check after the set is clean.

name: The refocusing routine
target_behavior: After any mistake, runs physical cue, breath and task cue in under 2 seconds and goes straight back to work.
purpose: Gives the boxer a trained response to a mistake: a three-step reset (physical cue, breath, task cue) used after every mistake in training so it is automatic in competition.
standard_setup: Any training block (shadow, bag or pads). The boxer picks the three steps with the coach, for example touch gloves together, one exhale, “jab first”, and the coach notes them so every coach prompts the same routine.
execution: A three-step reset: physical cue → breath → task cue. Example: touch gloves together → one exhale → “jab first” - Rehearse it until it takes under 2 seconds - Deploy it after every mistake in training, without exception, so it is automatic in competition. Most boxers have no trained response to making a mistake, which is why one clean shot taken can cost them a round
what_good_looks_like:
After every mistake the routine appears without being told.
The three steps run in order and take under 2 seconds.
The next action follows the task cue, not the last mistake.
The boxer does not dwell or speed up after the mistake.

name: Film-to-Drill Converter
target_behavior: Every film finding leaves the review as one trainable task: a drill, mitt cue, bag constraint, partner drill, sparring constraint or fight-plan rule.
purpose: convert film notes into training actions.
standard_setup: one clip set.
execution: code pattern, name one problem, assign one drill, one cue, one sparring constraint.
what_good_looks_like:
Each note names one observable pattern from the clip, never vague advice.
The note finds the first thing that went wrong in the sequence, not only the last.
Each problem gets one drill, one cue and one sparring constraint.
Every finding ends as an action.
common_errors: advice like “be sharper.”
corrections: force note into drill/mitt/bag/partner/spar/fight rule.

name: Pogo Jumps
target_behavior: Bounces off the ankles with a stiff body, little knee bend, quick ground contact and quiet landings, staying low.
purpose: Trains stiff, springy ankles and quick ground contact: fast, low bounces that build reactive spring to carry into light, quick boxing feet.
standard_setup: Flat floor with room for each athlete to bounce in place, feet hip-width, athletes facing or side-on to the coach so the coach sees the knees and hears the landings. No equipment needed; the number of contacts is what the session plan sets.
execution:
Stand tall, feet hip-width.
Jump using ankles only (minimal knee bend).
Stay stiff and bounce quickly off ground.
Land quietly on balls of feet.
what_good_looks_like:
Knee bend minimal (~10–15°)
Quick ground contact
Low height
common_errors: Common errors: bending too much at knees, slow ground contact, heavy landings.
corrections: Fix: Too deep → less knee | Slow → faster

name: Knee tap
target_behavior: Level change and entries
purpose: Shoulder tag aimed at the knee: the low target makes the boxer change level and enter, then get out without being touched.
standard_setup: Same, targeting the knee
execution:
Two boxers face off in stance in open space.

Each tries to touch the partner's knee without being touched, changing level with the legs to reach it.

After each touch the boxer comes back up into stance and out of range.

Coach calls any reach made by bending at the waist or dropping the guard.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The level change comes from the knees; the back stays upright and the guard stays up.
The boxer enters, touches and is back out before the partner can touch back.
Stance is rebuilt after every touch.

name: Feint Before Punch Drill
target_behavior: Every scoring punch starts from a visible, believable feint (shoulder, level or hand), and the athlete stays balanced from the feint into the punch.
purpose: Every scoring punch must begin with a visible feint.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Two athletes face each other in stance, in the sparring gear the gym uses. The coach stands where both athletes' shoulders and hands can be seen, so each feint can be judged before the punch is counted.
execution:
Athlete performs a clear feint (shoulder, level, or hand).
Punch counts only if feint is shown first.
Continue controlled sparring with rule enforced.
what_good_looks_like:
The feint is small, clear and believable, and the partner reacts to it.
The athlete stays balanced after the feint.
The punch that follows is connected to the feint, not rushed after it.

name: Back squat
target_behavior: Squats to at least parallel with a neutral spine, the hips and knees breaking together and the chest staying up.
purpose: the highest-loading knee-and-hip extension pattern; strong evidence base for developing lower-body maximal strength
standard_setup: bar in the high or low position (consistency matters more than which), feet at a width allowing full depth without lumbar flexion, toes slightly out
execution: brace, break at the hips and knees together, descend to at least parallel with a neutral spine, drive up with the chest staying up
what_good_looks_like:
The knees track over the feet, with no inward collapse.
Depth reaches at least parallel without the pelvis tucking under.
The chest stays up out of the bottom, and the boxing check after is clean.
common_errors: knees collapsing inward (glute and adductor weakness, or ankle restriction), butt tucking at depth (ankle dorsiflexion or hip mobility — retest the screen), forward lean (thoracic stiffness or weak trunk)

name: Weighted chin-up and pull-up
target_behavior: Pulls from a full hang to chin over the bar with control, adding mass only once bodyweight reps are clean.
purpose: The main upper-body strength exercise for a boxer: trains the lats (punch retraction and trunk connection), builds strength relative to body mass, and balances pulling against pushing.
standard_setup: A pull-up bar, with a dip belt or weight vest for added mass. Chin-up: palms facing the athlete; pull-up: palms facing away. Coach stands side-on.
execution:
Athlete hangs from the bar at full arm length, shoulders set.

Athlete pulls until the chin clears the bar, without kicking or swinging.

Athlete lowers under control to a full hang.

Run 4 × 3–6 with added mass, or bodyweight progressions (the Long Road's prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
Every rep starts from a full hang and finishes with the chin over the bar.
No kicking or swinging; the lowering is controlled.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Explosive-loose alternation drill
target_behavior: Goes from full explosive output to completely loose movement at once, and back, on every switch of every round.
purpose: Trains going loose on command: bursts of explosive output on the bag alternate with completely loose movement, so the boxer learns to switch tension off as fast as they switch it on.
standard_setup: Heavy bags and a timer (or the coach's calls) for the explosive and loose phases. The coach stands where shoulders, hands and jaw can be seen in the loose phase.
execution: On the bag: 3 × 3 min alternating 5 s of explosive output with 10 s of completely loose movement. The loose phase is the trained skill — most boxers cannot actually go loose on command, and it shows in round 3.
what_good_looks_like:
Explosive phases are truly explosive.
In the loose phase the shoulders drop, the hands soften and the boxer keeps moving easily.
The switch to loose is immediate, not a slow wind-down.
The loose phase still looks loose in round 3.

name: Shadow boxing intervals
target_behavior: Throws and moves at maximal velocity with full movement in every interval, with the technique still recognisable.
purpose: Output and speed with zero impact cost
standard_setup: Open floor or ring with room to move, and a clock. No bag or partner; the method is for times when impact needs limiting. Coach stands where the athlete's guard and feet can be seen.
execution:
Coach names one technical target the shadow must keep (for example hands back to guard after every punch).

Athlete shadow boxes at maximal velocity with full movement for 30 s.

Athlete rests 30–60 s, then repeats, for 8 intervals in all (the Long Road's prescription).

Coach scores the technical target each interval, not only the output.

After the last interval, athlete repeats the same technical check; coach logs clean reps, failed reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
Hands and feet move at full speed for the whole interval.
Every punch comes back to guard and the feet recover to stance.
The technical target looks the same in interval 8 as in interval 1.

name: Combination discipline
target_behavior: Throws no more than three punches per sequence and moves after every sequence, even when tired.
purpose: Keeps combination discipline when tired: on the bag after conditioning, no sequence goes past three punches and every sequence ends with movement.
standard_setup: Bag, tired
execution:
Run in the last 15–20 minutes of a session, after conditioning, once the main behavior of the day is already stable.

Athlete works the bag for 3 × 3 min; each sequence is three punches at most.

After every sequence the athlete moves (angle, pivot or step off) before the next.

Coach counts sequences over three punches and sequences with no movement.
what_good_looks_like:
No sequence goes past three punches.
The last punch is a clear finish and movement starts at once.
The same discipline holds in the last round as in the first.

name: Half-ring only
target_behavior: Working in confined space
purpose: Teaches working in confined space: with only half the ring to use, the boxer has to solve pressure with exits, angles and lane changes instead of running away. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Half-ring only
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: only half the ring is used; the coach marks the half-way line, and crossing it is called and resets the exchange; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Both boxers stay inside the half for the round.

Boxer gets out of trouble with pivots, angles and lane changes inside the space, and arrives in stance after each exit.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer exits to an open lane inside the space instead of backing to the line.
Ropes and the line are decision points, not panic points.
The boxer arrives in stance after every exit.

name: Number call
target_behavior: Decision speed under load
purpose: Trains decision speed under load: mid-exchange the coach calls a number and the boxer must give the matching response at once.
standard_setup: Coach calls a number mid-exchange requiring an immediate specific response
execution:
Before the round the coach sets a short list of numbers, each with one specific response the boxer has already trained (for example an exit, a defense or a set combination).

Boxer and partner spar at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Mid-exchange the coach calls a number; the boxer gives that response at once, then carries on.

Coach watches how fast and how cleanly the response comes.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The called response comes at once and matches the number.
The response is clean and from balance, then the boxer is back in the exchange.
The boxer keeps defending while listening.

name: Body-Only Round
target_behavior: Scores to the body only, changing level by bending the knees, with the guard protecting the head, and exits after scoring.
purpose: Light sparring limited to body shots only.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Two athletes face each other in stance, in the sparring gear the gym uses. The coach stands side-on to both athletes to see the level changes and any shot that goes to the head, with a clock for the round.
execution:
No head contact allowed.
Controlled pace maintained.
Emphasize level changes and exits.
what_good_looks_like:
Level changes come from the knees, not from bending at the waist.
The guard stays up to protect the head on every body shot.
The athlete exits after scoring, every shot stays on the body, and the pace stays controlled.

name: Slow-motion cross
target_behavior: Feeling each link of the chain in sequence
purpose: Lets the boxer feel each link of the rear straight in order (ground, hip, trunk, shoulder, arm) by slowing one cross to 5 seconds in front of a mirror.
standard_setup: Mirror, 5 seconds per punch
execution:
Athlete stands in stance in front of a mirror.

Athlete throws the rear straight in slow motion, 5 seconds per punch: the rear foot turns and drives, the hip turns, then trunk and shoulder, then the arm extends.

Athlete returns to guard on the same line and checks each link in the mirror.

Run 3 × 10 (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Each link moves in order: foot, hip, shoulder, then arm.
The tempo stays slow through the whole punch.
Weight moves onto the lead foot without falling forward.
common_errors: Rushing

name: Combination layering under fatigue
target_behavior: Keeps combinations clean while tired: guard back after every punch, and each combination ending in defense or an exit.
purpose: Primary Focus: Simulation rounds, pacing control, fatigue discipline
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in lines facing the coach with room to step out. Shadow only: no partner and no contact. The coach stands where guards and finishes can be seen.
execution:
Coach builds the combination one layer at a time: 1-2, then 1-2-3, then 1-2-3 with a defensive move or exit at the end.

Athlete keeps working the layered combination continuously for the time the session plan sets, so fatigue builds.

Coach watches for the first thing that breaks (guard, feet or finish) and gives one cue for it.

When technique breaks down, the athlete resets to stance and the coach drops back a layer before building again.
what_good_looks_like: Every combination ends with either a defensive action or an exit, never with the boxer standing still admiring the work

name: Stationary jab reps (10 slow, 10 moderate)
target_behavior: Jabs from a still stance with no telegraph, in a straight line, coming back faster than it went out, guard back every time.
purpose: Primary Focus: Foundational stance, jab, pivot automation
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in lines facing the coach, feet set in stance and not moving. Shadow only: no partner and no contact. The coach stands in front, then walks the lines, watching the shoulder and the returning hand.
execution:
Athlete sets stance and stays stationary for the whole set.

Athlete throws 10 slow jabs, freezing briefly with the hand back at the guard after each so the coach can check.

Athlete throws 10 moderate-speed jabs with the same shape: no shoulder dip, no hand cocking, straight out and faster back.

Coach gives one cue between the slow and the moderate jabs if needed.
what_good_looks_like:
Jab: Initiation without telegraph — no shoulder dip, no hand cocking, no weight shift
Jab: Straight line from the guard to the target, elbow following the hand
Jab: Rotation of the fist so the knuckles land flat, thumb turning down toward the end
Jab: Retraction faster than extension.

name: Jab–Cross Combination
target_behavior: The cross follows the jab with hip rotation, and both hands return to guard with the stance intact.
purpose: Teaches the 1–2: a jab followed by the cross, with the hips rotating into the rear hand, thrown from stance and finished back in stance.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes spread out in stance facing the coach; no partner. The coach stands in front, then checks feet and hips from the side.
execution: 1–2 combination.
what_good_looks_like:
The jab goes out straight and comes back as the cross starts.
The hips turn into the cross; it travels straight, without reaching, looping or over-rotating.
Both hands come back to guard and the feet stay in stance.
