name: Boxer has just been caught cleanly (partner instructed to land one hard shot early) and must respond well
target_behavior: After the clean shot, resets stance, eyes and breathing and goes back to the plan from structure.
purpose: Builds the response to being caught: the partner is told to land one hard shot early, and the boxer practises responding well (reset, then box) instead of retaliating or folding.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, both boxers in full sparring kit. Before the round the coach privately tells the partner to land one hard shot early, then box normally; the coach stands where the boxer's reaction can be seen.
execution:
Coach briefs the partner out of the boxer's hearing: land one hard shot early in the round, then box normally at the drill's open-sparring level.

Partner lands the shot; the boxer must respond well: reset stance, eyes and breathing, then box from structure.

Boxer does not answer emotionally; the next action is chosen, not automatic.

Between rounds the coach names what the response looked like and gives one correction.

Coach logs the response (reset, retaliation or freeze).
what_good_looks_like:
The reset after the shot is visible and fast.
The boxer does not rush back in blindly or freeze.
Breathing stays connected to movement.
The rest of the round is boxed from the plan, not from the hit.

name: Moving Jab
target_behavior: Each jab is thrown from a moving stance, extends straight, comes back quickly, and the feet keep moving after it.
purpose: Joins the jab to footwork: the athlete moves around the floor and throws single jabs that extend straight and come back quickly, without stopping the feet.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for every athlete to move in all directions; no partner. The coach stands where athletes' feet and lead hands can be seen and keeps their paths apart.
execution: Moving jab.

name: Circle drill
target_behavior: Circling toward the partner’s lead hand continuously
purpose: Makes circling toward the partner's lead hand, away from the power hand, the boxer's default direction.
standard_setup: Partner in the middle
execution:
Partner stands in the middle in stance and turns to face the boxer; the boxer starts at range.

Coach tells the boxer the partner's stance before the round, so the boxer knows which side is the lead hand.

Boxer circles continuously toward the partner's lead hand, in stance, keeping the distance; circling into the power hand is the failure mode.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer circles toward the lead hand every time, without being told.
The feet step and slide without crossing.
The distance stays the same as the boxer circles.
common_errors: Circling into the power hand by default

name: Stance line inspection drill
target_behavior: Takes and holds a balanced boxing stance on the line (feet at the right width and angle, guard in place) without the coach having to set it.
purpose: Primary Focus: Foundational stance, jab, pivot automation
standard_setup:
Top View Diagram:
  Athlete Line
  -----------------------------
  |  A  A  A  A  A  A  A  A  |
  Coach walks front and rear checking foot width and guard position.
execution:
Athletes line up along the floor line, each taking stance across it on the coach's call.

Coach walks the front of the line, then the rear, checking foot width and guard position on each athlete.

Coach gives each athlete one cue for the first fault seen (for example feet too narrow or square to the front) and the athlete fixes it.

Athlete steps forward or back on the coach's call and freezes back into stance for a second check.
what_good_looks_like:
Base width roughly shoulder-width plus a half-step, lead foot pointed slightly inward toward the opponent, rear foot at roughly 45°
Weight distribution near 50/50 at rest, shifting to demand — not permanently forward (loses the ability to move back) or permanently back (loses power and forward pressure)
Knees soft and unlocked; hips slightly under, not stuck out behind
Rear heel light, not planted, not up on the toe
what_bad_looks_like: feet too narrow (draw a line on the floor and stand across it); square to the opponent (drill from a taped 45° line); weight on the front foot (drill with the rear foot on a small pad so you can feel loading)

name: Plyometric push-ups, clap push-ups, drop push-ups
target_behavior: Pushes the floor away fast on every rep and lands softly, with the body in one straight line.
purpose: Builds upper-body reactive strength: push-ups driven hard enough for the hands to leave the floor, progressing to clap, drop and depth push-ups.
standard_setup: Open floor; a low box for drop and depth push-ups. Athlete starts in push-up position. Coach kneels side-on to see the hips and elbows.
execution:
Athlete starts in push-up position, body straight.

Athlete lowers under control to full depth, then explodes up so the hands leave the floor.

Athlete lands with soft elbows, absorbing the force, and resets before the next rep.

Run 3–4 × 3–5, full recovery (the Long Road's prescription), at the rung of the progression the athlete has reached.

After the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check; coach logs clean explosive reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
The hips stay level; the body does not sag.
Every rep goes to full depth and leaves the floor with fast intent.
Landings are soft, and the reset check after the set is clean.

name: Entry-and-exit
target_behavior: Every entry has a planned exit
purpose: Makes the exit part of every entry: the boxer enters, lands two and leaves on an angle, with the exit planned before the entry starts.
standard_setup: Enter, land two, exit at an angle
execution:
Coach sets the task: enter, land two, exit at an angle; partner spars at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer picks the exit before entering, then enters behind the feet.

Boxer lands two and leaves at once on an angle, never back down the line of entry.

Coach scores each rep: an entry with no exit is a failed rep, whether or not the shots landed.

Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The exit starts the moment the second shot lands.
The boxer leaves on a new line and arrives in stance facing the partner.
The two shots are finished, not trailing into a third.

name: Sparring at the end of a session when tired
target_behavior: Composure under fatigue — use sparingly
purpose: Tests composure under fatigue: open sparring at the end of a session, when the boxer is tired, to see whether decisions and structure hold. Used sparingly.
standard_setup: Sparring at the end of a session when tired
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: this is the last block of the session, run only once the main behaviour of the day is stable, and left out for an athlete already confused before it starts; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for open sparring.

Boxers spar open rounds at the agreed intensity, tired from the session.

Boxer keeps the day's main behaviour and simple decisions; slow is acceptable, broken is not.

Coach keeps the decision simple enough to see whether the boxer made the correct choice.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
The day's main behaviour survives the fatigue.
The boxer gets slower but not broken: stance, guard and exits hold.
The boxer is still choosing, not just surviving.

name: Band-resisted punch
target_behavior: Overload with preserved velocity
purpose: Overloads the punch with a light band while keeping its speed, as a power exercise; it is not a conditioning round.
standard_setup: Light band anchored behind
execution:
Coach anchors a light band behind the athlete so it resists the punch; the athlete stands in stance at the band's working length.

Athlete throws maximal punches against the band, keeping punch speed close to unbanded speed.

Athlete rests fully between sets.

Run 3–4 × 6–10/side, full recovery (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Punches stay fast; the band barely slows them.
The punch looks like the athlete's normal punch.
Sets stay short, with full rest between them.
common_errors: Rounds of it for conditioning — degrades mechanics

name: SCORE → EXIT UNDER PRESSURE
target_behavior: After scoring, the athlete leaves at once on an angle and arrives balanced in stance while the partner steps forward, instead of backing straight up or staying to trade.
purpose: exit clean while being pressed
standard_setup: Open floor or ring space with room behind and to the sides of the athlete. The partner faces the athlete in stance, ready to step forward after each score; the coach stands side-on to see the exit line and the athlete's feet.
execution: 45 sec / 15 sec × 4. Athlete scores; partner immediately steps forward; athlete exits in balance.
what_good_looks_like:
The exit starts the moment the score lands.
The athlete angles out instead of backing straight up.
The athlete arrives balanced in stance, eyes on the partner, before re-engaging.
common_errors: backing straight up, staying to trade, losing stance
correction_path: angle out and regain stance before re-engaging

name: Two-Choice Cue Counter
target_behavior: The athlete solves the cue the partner actually showed, never a response loaded in advance.
purpose: train response to real boxing cues.
standard_setup: partner shows jab cue or pressure cue.
execution: jab cue = slip/catch-counter; pressure cue = frame/pivot.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete reads the cue first, then gives its matching answer.
At least 80% of cue-responses are correct.
False cues get no bite: the athlete holds position and resets.
No freezing after the cue.
common_errors: preloaded response.
corrections: slow down and require verbal cue ID before response.
transfer: touch / constraint spar with cue-specific scoring.

name: Punch Iso Hold
target_behavior: Holds the punch at extension in line, shoulder packed and chin tucked, rear hand at the guard, without locking the elbow or reaching past the alignment.
purpose: Builds tension and alignment at full punch extension (wrist, elbow and shoulder in line, shoulder packed) so the punch finishes in a strong, protected position; in DOC-089 the punch burst comes straight after it.
standard_setup: Athletes in stance, spaced so an extended punch reaches no one, side-on to the coach so the coach sees the line from wrist to shoulder and the rear hand. No equipment needed; the hold time is what the session plan sets.
execution:
Extend punch fully with proper alignment (shoulder, elbow, wrist stacked).
Hold at extension without locking elbow.
Shoulder stays packed, chin tucked.
Rear hand stays up in guard.
Tension: fist tight, arm active but not rigid.
what_good_looks_like:
Elbow slightly bent (5–10°)
Shoulder packed, not shrugged
Alignment: wrist-elbow-shoulder
Rear hand stays at guard
common_errors: Common errors: overextending, shoulder shrugging, dropping opposite hand.
corrections: Fix: Overreach → pull back slightly | Shoulder up → relax

name: Slip → Pause → Jab
target_behavior: After a small slip the athlete holds a loaded pause, then jabs and resets, so the jab is chosen from control rather than fired automatically.
purpose: Control after defense
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance with room to move, facing the coach. The coach stands in front to give the visual cue for the slip and to see heads and feet.
execution:
Round 1: Slip + pause only
Round 2: Full sequence
what_good_looks_like:
The slip is small and the head moves first.
The pause is held in a loaded stance, not frozen or standing tall.
The jab comes from the pause and the athlete resets every rep.

name: Within one step of ring center
target_behavior: Ring generalship, holding the middle
purpose: Teaches ring generalship by holding the middle: the boxer must stay within one step of ring centre while the partner tries to move them off it. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Boxer must stay within one step of ring center
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the boxer must stay within one step of ring centre (marked with tape), and the partner tries to move the boxer off it; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer holds the middle with feet, angles and the jab, turning with the partner rather than following.

If moved off the centre, the boxer takes it back with the feet, not with a rush.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer owns the middle: balanced, and able to score or deny from it.
The boxer turns with the partner instead of following.
When moved, the boxer takes the centre back with the feet.

name: Land 3 before the partner lands 1
target_behavior: Defensive priority
purpose: Teaches defensive priority: the boxer must land three clean shots before the partner lands one, so getting hit costs more than missing a chance. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Boxer must land 3 shots before the partner lands 1
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the boxer must land 3 shots before the partner lands 1; the coach counts aloud, and a clean shot by the partner sets the boxer's count back to zero; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer defends first, with the feet whenever possible, and scores only from structure.

After landing, the boxer leaves or resets rather than staying to trade for the count.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer is hard to hit: feet first, small defensive movements, eyes on the partner.
Every defence leaves the boxer in a usable spot to answer.
The boxer scores from structure and leaves; the count is never chased by trading.

name: Punch Burst
target_behavior: Throws a short burst of fast, snapping punches, each one back to the guard, staying balanced in stance.
purpose: Turns the tension of the punch iso hold into fast, snapping punches that return straight to the guard, so speed and snap carry into boxing.
standard_setup: Athletes in stance, spaced so punches reach no one, straight after the punch iso hold; shadow punches, no partner and no contact. Athletes face or are side-on to the coach so the coach sees the hands returning. The number of bursts is what the session plan sets.
execution:
After iso hold, throw 3–5 fast punches.
Focus on speed and snap, not power.
Return hands quickly to guard.
Maintain balance and stance.
what_good_looks_like:
3–5 fast punches
Snap back to guard
Stay balanced
common_errors: Common errors: pushing punches, losing form, dropping hands.

name: Trap-bar jump
target_behavior: Jumps as high as possible holding a light trap bar, with a full drive through hips, knees and ankles on every rep.
purpose: A loaded jump with almost no learning curve: jumping with a light trap bar trains the hip, knee and ankle drive (triple extension) behind leg drive.
standard_setup: A trap bar loaded to 20–30% of the athlete's trap-bar deadlift 1RM, on a platform or solid floor. Athlete stands in the handles as for the trap-bar deadlift. Coach stands side-on.
execution:
Athlete stands in the trap bar, grips the handles, arms long, chest up.

Athlete dips quickly and jumps as high as possible, driving through hips, knees and ankles together.

Athlete lands softly with the bar under control and resets before the next rep.

Run 4 × 3 @ 20–30% of trap-bar deadlift 1RM (the Long Road's prescription).

After the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check; coach logs clean explosive reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
Every jump is a full-height effort with hips, knees and ankles extending together.
The landing is soft and the bar stays under control.
The reset check after the set shows no stance collapse or delayed reset.

name: Slip & Return Drill
target_behavior: Slips the jab with a small head movement, eyes forward and balance kept, then returns one punch at once from that position.
purpose: Defender must slip opponent’s jab before returning a punch.
standard_setup: Open mat or ring. Partner and defender face each other in stance at jab range, in the gloves the gym uses for partner work. The coach stands side-on to the defender to see the size of the slip and the return.
execution:
Partner throws light, controlled jab.
Defender slips inside or outside.
Defender immediately returns one punch.
Reset and repeat.
what_good_looks_like:
The slip is small and the eyes stay forward.
The defender stays balanced and the slip finishes in position to punch.
One return comes straight away, then both reset.

name: Shoulder feint — mirror, then partner
target_behavior: Dips the lead shoulder exactly as the jab starts, so a watcher cannot tell feint from jab, and stays balanced and ready after it.
purpose: Builds a shoulder feint that looks exactly like the start of the jab: mirror work first until feint and jab cannot be told apart, then a partner drill.
standard_setup: A mirror for the first part; then open floor with a partner in stance at jab range who watches and calls “feint” or “jab” on each rep. The coach stands beside the mirror, then side-on to the pair.
execution: Mirror work first for indistinguishability, then partner drill
what_good_looks_like:
In the mirror the feint and the start of the jab look the same.
The dip is small enough to recover from and big enough to matter.
After the feint the boxer is balanced, guard in place.
The partner's calls are no better than a guess.

name: Uppercut on entry
target_behavior: Meets the partner's stepping jab with a short rear uppercut on the right path, from stance, and recovers through the guard.
purpose: Gives the boxer a way to meet a pressure fighter as they come: when the partner steps in behind a jab, the boxer meets the entry with the rear uppercut.
standard_setup: Open floor or ring, both in the kit the gym uses for light technical partner work. The partner starts just outside range and steps in with a jab; the coach stands side-on to see the boxer's rear-hand path and stance.
execution: partner steps in with a jab; boxer meets with the rear uppercut. 3 × 2 min each side
what_good_looks_like:
The uppercut meets the partner as they step in, not after they have arrived.
The rear hand travels a short path up and comes back through the guard.
The other hand stays home to protect.
Stance is usable after the punch.

name: Range-find and exit
target_behavior: Jab to measure, then immediately reset distance
purpose: Teaches the jab as a measuring tool: jab to find the range on a moving partner, then reset distance at once instead of staying in front.
standard_setup: Partner moves
execution:
Coach sets the roles: the partner moves around the space at the pace the coach sets; the boxer works at the light technical contact the coach sets.

Boxer jabs to measure the distance as the partner moves, then immediately resets distance (steps out or angles off) before the partner can answer.

Coach calls any rep where the boxer jabs and stays in front; that is the failure mode.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
Every jab is followed at once by a reset of distance.
The exit is never back down the line the jab came in on.
The boxer finishes facing the partner, guard up.
common_errors: Jabbing and staying

name: Push-Up Iso Hold
target_behavior: Holds the push-up position under tension with the body in one straight line, the elbows tucked and the breathing steady through the hold.
purpose: Builds tension and control in the push-up position (chest, triceps and a braced trunk) before the explosive push-ups that turn it into power.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete in push-up position, athletes side-on to the coach so the coach sees the line from head to heel and the elbows. No equipment needed; the hold time is what the session plan sets.
execution:
Set up push-up position: hands under shoulders, body straight.
Lower halfway or to bottom and hold.
Elbows ~45° from body.
Brace core: no sagging hips.
Tension: press hands into ground, engage chest and triceps.
what_good_looks_like:
Elbows ~90° at mid hold
Body straight line head to heel
Elbows 30–45° from body
common_errors: Common errors: flared elbows, hips dropping, holding breath.
corrections: Fix: Sagging hips → squeeze glutes | Elbows flare → tuck slightly

name: Managing the clinch
target_behavior: Tying up the working hand, turning them, working the break
purpose: Gives the clinch its own drilling: the athlete learns to tie up the partner's working hand, turn them off line and work the break, instead of leaving the clinch to chance.
standard_setup: Specific clinch drilling; often neglected entirely
execution:
Coach sets the roles before each rep: one partner comes in to clinch at the pace set; the other athlete manages it.

Athlete ties up the partner's working hand, the one the partner is trying to punch with.

Athlete turns the partner off line using the tie-up, so the partner is not square.

Athlete works the break: comes out of the clinch in stance with the guard up, takes an angle and resets shape before anything else.

Partners switch roles on the coach's call.
what_good_looks_like:
The working hand is tied up before it can punch.
The partner is turned off line, not just held.
The break is clean and the reset is visible and fast.

name: Know their ranges
target_behavior: Estimates a partner's ranges from their build and confirms the estimate early with the range-finding jab, from stance and without over-reaching.
purpose: Teaches the boxer to know an opponent's ranges: measured against partners of different heights and reaches, then estimated from a build and checked early with the range-finding jab.
standard_setup: Repeat the measurement against partners of different heights and reaches. Learn to estimate an opponent’s range from their build, and to verify it in the first thirty seconds of a bout — which is one of the real purposes of the range-finding jab.
execution:
Coach pairs the athlete with partners of different heights and reaches, one at a time.

Partner stands in stance and extends each punch slowly, stopping short; coach and athlete tape the floor where the partner's jab, rear hand, lead hook and uppercut would land.

Before each new partner is measured, the athlete estimates that partner's jab range from their build, then checks it against the tape.

Athlete moves in and out across the partner's taped ranges until the edge of each can be felt without looking, using a range-finding jab to a pad the partner holds.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete's estimate from a build comes close to the taped range.
The athlete can tell when they are inside a partner's range without looking at the tape.
The range-finding jab measures from stance; it does not reach or lean.

name: Every combination ends with a pivot or step-off
target_behavior: Exits
purpose: Teaches exits: every combination the boxer throws must end with a pivot or a step-off, so the way out becomes part of every attack. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Every combination must end with a pivot or step-off
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: every combination must end with a pivot or a step-off, and a combination with no exit is called and does not count; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer pivots or steps off as the last punch lands, not after a pause.

Boxer arrives on the new angle in stance, facing the partner, ready to go again or defend.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Every combination has an exit, and the exit starts as the last punch lands.
The exit is a pivot or a step-off, never the line the boxer came in on.
The boxer arrives on the new angle facing the partner, in stance.

name: Outcome — walking out, the moment of the decision, the aftermath (win and loss)
target_behavior: Rehearses walking out, the moment of the decision and the aftermath of both a win and a loss, in real time with the nerves included, and stays composed through each.
purpose: Familiarization with the emotional context
standard_setup: In kit, standing, gloves on where practical, in the gym (or with photos of the venue if it is known). Week D of the daily imagery rotation (10 min daily).
execution:
Athlete stands in kit and starts the imagery from the walk to the ring.

Athlete images walking out and the bout's end in real time, nerves included.

Athlete images the moment of the decision, once as a win and once as a loss.

Athlete images the aftermath of each: what they do, say and how they carry themselves.

Athlete notes one thing to keep for next time; 10 min daily in the week this content is used.
what_good_looks_like:
The imagery runs in real time, not skipped or sped up.
The nerves are part of it.
Both outcomes are rehearsed, the loss as fully as the win.
The athlete comes out composed and can say how they will carry themselves either way.

name: Half-punch bag drill
target_behavior: Starts every punch the same way, real or half, and stops the half-punch cleanly with stance and guard intact.
purpose: Trains the half-punch feint: on the bag, half the punches start and stop, and they must look the same as real punches at the start, so a watching partner cannot call which.
standard_setup: Heavy bag; a partner stands where they can see the boxer's start and calls “real” or “half” as early as they can; the coach keeps count of correct calls.
execution: Bag drill: 50% of punches are half-punches; a partner watching should not be able to call which
what_good_looks_like:
Real punches and half-punches look the same at the start.
Half-punches stop cleanly; the boxer does not lean or drop the guard.
The watcher's calls are no better than a guess.
About half the punches are half-punches.

name: Real judging, result announced
target_behavior: Performing under evaluation
purpose: Teaches performing under evaluation: the round is judged for real and the result announced, so the boxer learns to box the plan while being scored and to win rounds the way judges see them.
standard_setup: Real judging with the result announced
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the round is judged round by round (every round has a winner) and the result is announced at the end; who judges is set before the bell; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for open sparring.

Boxers box open rounds at the agreed intensity.

Boxer builds the round: establish something early, clean visible work in the middle, finish strongly, and walk to the corner composed.

The result is announced; the coach debriefs with one technical and one tactical point.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer sticks to the plan under evaluation.
Work is clean and visible; efficiency over volume.
The boxer finishes rounds strongly and walks to the corner composed, whatever the score.

name: Three-layer round
target_behavior: Isolating each defensive layer
purpose: Isolates the three defensive layers one round at a time (feet, then head movement, then guard) so each is trained and seen on its own under live pressure.
standard_setup: Round 1 feet only, round 2 head movement only, round 3 guard only
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the bell: the partner attacks at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring; the boxer defends with one layer per round.

Round one, feet only: stepping out of range, angles, pivots.

Round two, head movement only: slips, rolls, pulls.

Round three, guard only: catch, parry, block. In every round a defense may finish with a return, an exit or a reset (the record's rule).

Coach calls any defense from the wrong layer. Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 6).
what_good_looks_like:
Each round shows only its own layer.
Each defense finishes in stance, ready for the next action.
The boxer recovers from each defense without extra balance steps.
common_errors: Mixing layers

name: Eye and head feint — constrained live
target_behavior: Draws the named defensive reaction with the eyes or head first, then scores on the line it opens, staying balanced; no reaction, no score.
purpose: Trains eye and head feints live: the boxer must draw a specific defensive reaction, by looking or moving as if attacking one line, before any punch can score.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, both boxers in sparring kit. Before the round the coach names the reaction the boxer must draw (for example the guard lifting, or a step back) and the line to score on; the coach stands where the partner's reaction can be seen.
execution: Constrained live: boxer must draw a specific defensive reaction before scoring
what_good_looks_like:
The eyes or head sell an attack on one line.
The named reaction appears before the boxer scores.
Points come on the line the reaction opened.
When the reaction does not come, the boxer resets rather than forcing a punch.

name: Distraction training
target_behavior: Keeps technique and focus on the set task while music, movement and talk go on around them.
purpose: Trains holding attention on the task with noise, movement and people around, so the gym or the venue stops pulling the boxer off the work.
standard_setup: The day's normal technical setup (shadow, bag or pads) plus the disruptions: music at volume, people moving nearby, someone talking to the boxer. The coach controls how much disruption is on.
execution: Perform technical work with deliberate noise, movement, and disruption present. Music at volume, people moving nearby, someone talking to you. Progressively increase
what_good_looks_like:
Technique looks the same with the noise on as with it off.
The boxer does not stop, look round or answer the talker.
As the disruption rises, the work still holds.

name: Counter Punch Round
target_behavior:
patience
timing
defensive awareness
clean response after reading the attack
purpose: Develop timing and defensive reading.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Two athletes face each other in stance in the gear the Friday sheet names (wraps, headgear, gloves). The coach states the rule before the bell (only punches thrown after a defensive movement score) and stands where both athletes' defenses and counters can be seen.
execution:
Athlete must first:
slip
block
parry
step back
Then counter.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete waits for the attack and defends first (slip, block, parry or step back).
The counter comes straight after the defense, from balance, not rushed.
When no opening appears, the athlete resets instead of forcing a counter.

name: L-step drill
target_behavior: Changing the line of attack, not just the distance
purpose: Teaches the L-step: a step out followed by a second step onto a new line, so the boxer's movement changes the angle of attack, not just the distance.
standard_setup: Tape an L on the floor
execution:
Coach tapes an L on the floor; the athlete starts in stance at the corner of the L.

Athlete steps out along one arm of the L, then takes the second step along the other arm, finishing in stance on a new line facing the target.

Athlete resets and repeats to both sides as the coach directs; stepping out sideways without the second step is the failure mode.

Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Two steps every time: out, then onto the new line.
The athlete finishes in stance facing the target from the new line.
The feet never cross and the guard stays up.
common_errors: Stepping out sideways without the second step

name: Bench press or floor press
target_behavior: Presses with control at moderate volume, tracked as a strength marker rather than chased.
purpose: A general upper-body strength marker, kept at moderate volume so it never dominates. Floor press is often the better choice for boxers: less shoulder extension at the bottom.
standard_setup: Bench and rack with safety pins for the bench press, or the floor (bar in a rack set low) for the floor press. Athlete lies with the eyes under the bar, feet planted on the bench press or knees bent on the floor press. Coach stands at the head end.
execution:
Athlete sets the shoulder blades back and down and grips the bar.

Bench press: athlete lowers the bar to the chest under control and presses up. Floor press: athlete lowers until the upper arms touch the floor, pauses, and presses up.

Volume stays moderate; sets, reps and load are those the session plan sets (the Long Road gives no prescription).

Coach records the load as a general strength marker.

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The bar path is controlled and the shoulders stay set on the bench or floor.
Volume stays moderate; the press does not take over the session.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Roll-under drill
target_behavior: Rolling under and returning uppercut/hook
purpose: Teaches the roll under a hook with its return: the partner throws hooks at 40% and the boxer rolls under and answers with an uppercut or a hook.
standard_setup: Partner throws hooks at 40%
execution:
Partner throws hooks at 40% at the pace the coach sets (cooperative roles, rung 5).

Boxer rolls under the hook with bent knees, a small U under the punch, and comes back to stance.

Boxer returns a rear uppercut or a lead hook off the roll, then resets.

Coach watches for the boxer rolling into the line of a second punch.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
The roll comes from the legs and ends in stance, eyes on the partner.
The return leaves off the roll: rear uppercut or hook.
The boxer does not come up into the line of a second punch.

name: Consequence attached to the outcome
target_behavior: Performing with stakes
purpose: Teaches performing with stakes: a meaningful consequence, agreed in advance, rides on the result, and the boxer learns to box the same round with something to lose.
standard_setup: Consequence attached to the outcome (something meaningful, agreed in advance)
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the consequence is agreed with both boxers in advance (something meaningful, and not a punishment), along with how the result is decided; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxers spar the round at the agreed pace.

The coach decides the result as agreed and the consequence is applied as agreed, without changing it after the round.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer boxes the same way with stakes as without.
No rushing, freezing or overthrowing because of what is riding on it.
Breathing stays steady and the boxer recovers quickly from mistakes.

name: Landmine punch press
target_behavior: Punching pattern with rotation, loaded
purpose: Trains the punching pattern under load with the rotation kept in: a barbell in a landmine pressed like a punch, as a power exercise.
standard_setup: Barbell in a landmine
execution:
Coach sets a barbell in a landmine at a load the athlete can move fast; the athlete stands in stance holding the bar end at the shoulder on the punching side.

Athlete presses the bar out like a punch, driving from the rear foot and turning the hip, with explosive intent on every rep.

Athlete resets to stance between reps and rests between sets; slow grinding reps are the failure mode.

Run 3 × 6/side (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Every rep is fast and explosive; none grind.
The press turns through the hip like a punch.
The load stays light enough for speed.
common_errors: Slow grinding reps — this is a power exercise

name: Initiation-only
target_behavior: Anticipation
purpose: Trains anticipation: the partner starts punches and stops them halfway, so the boxer learns to respond to the start of an action rather than to the punch.
standard_setup: Partner initiates punches but stops halfway; boxer must already have responded
execution:
Partner starts punches at the pace the coach sets and stops each one halfway; no punch reaches the boxer.

Boxer responds (a defense or a move) to the start of the punch.

Coach scores each rep on whether the response began before the punch was halfway.

Run 4 × 90 s, scored (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The response begins before the punch is halfway.
The response is a real defense or move from stance, not a flinch.
The boxer resets ready for the next start.

name: Visual Tracking Drill
target_behavior: The athlete reads and calls each flash correctly with the eyes doing the work, the head steady and the guard high.
purpose: Trains the eyes to pick up and read a visual signal while the head stays steady and the guard stays high, as preparation for defensive reaction timing.
standard_setup: Athletes in stance, guard up
execution: Coach flashes fingers randomly. Athlete calls out number while maintaining guard.
what_good_looks_like:
The number is called straight after the flash, and correctly.
Only the eyes move; the head stays steady.
The guard stays high and the stance holds the whole time.

name: Round begins with the boxer 2 points down and 1 round left
target_behavior: Raises work rate and intent to win the round clearly while keeping stance, defence and exits: urgency with clarity.
purpose: Builds composure and urgency when behind: the round starts with the boxer told they are 2 points down with 1 round left, so they practise raising urgency without losing structure.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, with a visible scoreboard if the gym has one; both boxers in sparring kit. Before the bell the coach announces the made-up situation.
execution:
Coach announces the scenario to both boxers before the bell: the boxer is 2 points down with 1 round left.

Partner boxes a normal round at the drill's controlled-sparring level.

Boxer has to win the round clearly: more work, earlier initiative, clean visible scoring, without giving up defence and exits.

Coach watches whether urgency rises with structure or turns into rushing.

After the round the coach names one thing that won the round and one that cost.
what_good_looks_like:
Work rate and initiative go up from the first bell.
The boxer lands clean, visible scores and finishes exchanges on purpose.
Defence and exits do not disappear in the rush.
The boxer stays in the present: the next thirty seconds, not the scorecard.

name: Feint-Read-Punish
target_behavior: The athlete punishes only the reaction the feint actually drew, never an automatic combination.
purpose: make feints produce information, not decoration.
standard_setup: mitt/partner gives known reactions.
execution: feint, see reaction, punish only the reaction shown.
what_good_looks_like: maps reaction to correct owner and executes clean answer
what_bad_looks_like: jab answer on defensive cue, counter without trigger, exit with no named destination, no reset
common_errors: automatic combo after feint.
corrections: require athlete to name reaction first.
transfer: tactical touch spar.

name: Mindfulness practice
target_behavior: Notices when attention has drifted and returns it to the chosen focus, calmly, again and again.
purpose: Trains noticing when attention drifts and bringing it back, the same skill a boxer needs when the mind drifts to the scorecard mid-bout.
standard_setup: A quiet place to sit and a timer. Any well-structured protocol the coach or athlete chooses, for example attention on the breath.
execution: Any well-structured protocol. The mechanism is training the noticing and returning of attention, which is precisely the skill required when your mind drifts to the scorecard in round 2 - Mindfulness carries one of the better effect sizes in the sport psychology literature (~1.35 in a meta-analytical review of athletic populations)
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete notices a drift without getting annoyed at it.
Attention comes back to the focus each time.
The athlete can say roughly how often they drifted and came back.

name: Partner solves the primary weapon
target_behavior: Recognises that the primary weapon has been solved and switches, at the right moment, to another way of winning the round.
purpose: Trains adaptability: the partner is told to shut down the boxer's primary weapon, so the boxer has to notice it has been solved and switch to another way of winning the round at the right moment.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat; two boxers in the sparring gear the gym uses, at the controlled-sparring level. Before the round the coach names the boxer's primary weapon and gives the partner a defined role for solving it, told to the partner only. The coach stands where both boxers can be seen.
execution: Partner is instructed to solve the boxer’s primary weapon; the boxer must find another way to win the round
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer notices quickly that the primary weapon is being solved.
The switch comes early and on purpose, not after the round is lost.
The new approach is organised and the boxer still competes to win.

name: Combination Roll – 3 – 6
target_behavior: At close range the athlete rolls under the partner's hook, returns lead hook then rear uppercut, and turns out.
purpose: Roll under the hook, return with hook and uppercut
standard_setup: Roll – 3 – 6
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the rep: the partner throws a single hook at the pace set; the athlete rolls, returns 3 – 6, then turns out.

Partner throws the hook at close range; athlete rolls under it, rotating under the punch with weight shifting to the rear foot.

Athlete comes up from the roll into the lead hook, then the rear uppercut.

Athlete turns out the moment the uppercut lands and resets stance and eyes before the next feed.

Partner feeds the picture and does not try to win the rep.
what_good_looks_like:
The roll goes under the hook and loads the counter; the athlete does not roll into a second punch.
The hook and uppercut come from the end of the roll, short and balanced.
The turn ends in stance, facing the partner.

name: Occlusion drill
target_behavior: Reliance on early cues
purpose: Forces the boxer onto early cues: the partner throws from behind a hand-held screen that comes away at the last moment, so the boxer must respond to the little that is seen.
standard_setup: Partner throws from behind a hand-held screen removed at the last moment
execution:
A hand-held screen is held between the partner and the boxer; the partner throws from behind it at the pace the coach sets.

The screen comes away at the last moment as the punch starts.

Boxer defends from the early part of the action they see, then resets to stance.

Coach watches for guessing (moving before the screen moves).

Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The defense starts as soon as the punch is seen, not after it is fully on the way.
The boxer defends from stance and resets.
The boxer does not guess before the screen moves.

name: Audience watching
target_behavior: Managing observation
purpose: Teaches managing observation: a small audience watching intently adds the pressure of being seen, and the boxer learns to box the same round anyway.
standard_setup: Audience (even three people watching intently)
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: an audience (even three people) watches the round intently; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxers spar the round as normal at the agreed pace; the audience watches but does not coach.

After a mistake the boxer runs the reset (physical cue, breath, task cue) and goes back to the task, not to the audience.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer boxes the same way with people watching as without.
No rushing, freezing or overthrowing for the audience.
After a mistake the boxer resets quickly and returns to the task.

name: Escape-the-corner
target_behavior: Pivot out and reset ring position within 15 s
purpose: Teaches the boxer caught in a corner to pivot out and reset ring position, instead of ducking and covering.
standard_setup: Boxer starts in a corner
execution:
Coach sets the roles: the boxer starts in a corner; the partner pressures from in front, at the pace and light technical contact the coach sets.

Boxer pivots out of the corner, or angles off, and resets ring position facing the partner within 15 s.

Coach resets both athletes after each rep; ducking and covering instead of pivoting is the failure mode.

Run 8 reps (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer pivots or angles out instead of ducking and covering.
The boxer leaves calmly and ends facing the partner in good ring position.
The escape happens inside the time.
common_errors: Ducking and covering instead of pivoting

name: Depth jumps and drop jumps
target_behavior: Off the ground as fast as possible, as high as possible, on every rep.
purpose: The highest-intensity plyometric: stepping off a box and rebounding off the ground as fast and as high as possible, to train the boxer's use of the stretch-and-rebound in the legs.
standard_setup: A low box (starting at 20 cm) on a firm surface with clear space in front. Athlete stands on the box edge. Coach stands side-on to see ground contact and rebound height.
execution:
Athlete steps (not jumps) off the box and lands on both feet.

On landing, athlete rebounds off the ground as fast as possible and as high as possible.

Athlete lands, resets fully and recovers before the next rep.

Run 3–5 × 3–5 with full recovery: very low volume, very high quality (the Long Road's prescription).

Coach stops the exercise at the first sign of degradation; after the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check and the coach logs it.
what_good_looks_like:
Ground contact is short and the rebound is high.
Contact time and height hold from the first rep to the last.
Landings are silent and controlled.

name: Barbell row, dumbbell row, single-arm row
target_behavior: Pulls the weight to the trunk with the back flat and the shoulder blade moving back, without heaving the torso.
purpose: Adds horizontal pulling volume. Boxers need more pulling than pushing (at least 1:1, preferably 2:1), because punching already loads the front of the shoulder heavily.
standard_setup: Barbell, dumbbells, or a bench for single-arm rows. Barbell and dumbbell rows: hinge forward with a flat back. Single-arm row: one hand and knee on the bench. Coach stands side-on.
execution:
Athlete sets the position: flat back, shoulders set, weight hanging at arm's length.

Athlete pulls the weight toward the lower ribs, leading with the elbow and moving the shoulder blade back.

Athlete lowers under control to full arm length.

Pulling volume across the week stays at least equal to pushing, preferably double (the Long Road's ratio); sets and reps are those the session plan sets.

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The back stays flat and still; the torso does not heave.
The shoulder blade moves back on each pull and the weight is lowered under control.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Stance-shift power
target_behavior: Generating force from a moving base
purpose: Trains generating punching force from a moving base, so power does not depend on being set in one position.
standard_setup: Bag
execution:
Athlete works the bag from stance, moving around it.

Athlete punches with power as the base shifts (stepping in, out or to the side) rather than only from a set position.

Coach checks that the feet land under the body as the punch lands, and calls any round that drifts back to set-position punching.

Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Power punches land while the base moves, not only from a set position.
The athlete lands balanced and in stance after each power shot.
No leaning or pushing the bag to make up for a moving base.
common_errors: Only punching from a set position

name: The gap drill
target_behavior: Micro-distance
purpose: Trains the gap: the distance where the boxer's own shots would land and the partner's do not. No punching; the feet do all the work.
standard_setup: Partner throws at fixed rhythm; boxer stays in own range, outside theirs. No punching
execution:
Partner throws at a fixed rhythm at the pace the coach sets, stopping short of the boxer.

Boxer does not punch; the only job is to stay in their own scoring range and outside the partner's.

Boxer adjusts with small steps in, out and off the line as the partner moves.

Coach calls when the boxer drifts too far out (out of own range) or too close (inside the partner's).

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer stays just inside their own range and just outside the partner's for most of the round.
Adjustments are small steps, not big retreats.
Stance and guard stay ready even with no punching.

name: Reaction Sprint + Spar Drill
target_behavior: Keeps sparring technique, a high guard and controlled breathing straight after a short sprint, so the fatigue tests the skill instead of erasing it.
purpose: Short sprint immediately followed by controlled sparring.
standard_setup: A clear sprint lane next to the ring or mat, so athletes go straight from the sprint into the sparring space. Two athletes in the sparring gear the gym uses; the coach stands where the end of the sprint and the start of the round can both be seen, with a clock for the sprint and the round.
execution:
Perform 10–15 second sprint.
Immediately begin sparring round.
Maintain technique under fatigue.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete goes from the sprint into stance and guard straight away.
Breathing is brought under control early in the round, and the guard stays high.
Mechanics stay clean: slower is acceptable, sloppy is not.

name: Nordic hamstring curl
target_behavior: Lowers forward under control for as long as the hamstrings can hold, hips straight, then catches with the hands.
purpose: Trains the hamstrings while they lengthen under load (eccentric): the athlete lowers the body forward from kneeling as slowly as possible. The Long Road calls it the best available eccentric hamstring exercise.
standard_setup: Athlete kneels on a pad with the ankles anchored under a fixed bar or pad, body straight from knees to head. Coach stands side-on to see the hip line.
execution:
Athlete kneels tall, hips extended, body in one line from knees to head.

Athlete lowers forward as slowly as possible, keeping the hips straight, until the hamstrings can no longer hold.

Athlete catches with the hands, pushes back up lightly, and resets.

Run 3 × 5, controlled to the point of failure of the eccentric (the Long Road's prescription); on first exposure, start with 2 × 3 partial-range reps.

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The hips stay straight; the athlete does not bend at the hips to shorten the lever.
The lowering is slow and even all the way to the catch.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Breathing control before each round restart
target_behavior: Uses the break to bring breathing back under control (long breath out, shoulders down) and starts the next round calm and in stance.
purpose: Primary Focus: Simulation rounds, pacing control, fatigue discipline
standard_setup: Used in the break between rounds of the Technical Block's round work. Each athlete stands at their own spot; no partner and no contact. The coach stands where the group's shoulders and faces can be seen.
execution:
At the end of the round, athlete walks back to their spot and stands tall, hands relaxed.

Coach gives a short breath reminder; athlete breathes in under control and lets a long breath out, shoulders dropping.

Athlete repeats a few calm breaths until breathing and shoulders settle.

Before the restart, athlete steps back into stance with the guard up and keeps the breathing calm as the round begins.
what_good_looks_like:
Breathing should lower unnecessary tension, not create more it.
Action breathing should support movement, timing, and controlled effort during work.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete hold breath during effort.
Do shoulders rise and stay tight under pressure.
Does breathing become shallow when frustration rises.

name: Counter-only sparring
target_behavior: Reading and countering
purpose: Teaches the boxer to read before acting: the boxer never starts an exchange, so every punch is an answer to something the partner showed. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Boxer may never lead
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the bell: the boxer may never lead; the partner leads, at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Partner opens exchanges with single shots and short combinations; the boxer defends, then answers only once the partner has thrown.

Boxer may also defend and reset, or reposition, without punching; a punch before the partner commits is a lead, and the coach calls it.

Run 5 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 6).
what_good_looks_like:
Every punch the boxer throws answers something the partner threw.
The boxer counters from balance, then scores and leaves or resets.
When no clean counter is there, the boxer chooses defense, reset or reposition instead of forcing one.
common_errors: Leading “accidentally”

name: Ropes escape and reset
target_behavior: Escapes the ropes with a pivot or angle, not a straight-line retreat, and finishes reset in stance facing the partner, within the time.
purpose: Trains getting off the ropes against pressure: from a start on the ropes the boxer escapes and resets within 15 seconds instead of staying trapped.
standard_setup: Boxer starts on the ropes
execution: must escape and reset within 15 seconds. 8 repetitions
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer leaves on a pivot or angle step, not straight back or along the ropes.
The escape ends back toward the centre, in stance, facing the partner, eyes up.
The boxer stays calm on the ropes; no panic or shelling.
The reset is done within the 15 seconds.

name: Hip thrust
target_behavior: Extends the hips with the glutes to a full lockout, ribs down, without arching the lower back.
purpose: Glute-dominant hip extension with minimal load on the spine; useful in high-sparring weeks.
standard_setup: Upper back against a bench, bar padded across the hips, feet flat about hip-width with the shins near vertical at the top. Coach stands side-on.
execution:
Athlete sets the upper back on the bench, ribs down, chin tucked.

Athlete drives through the heels and extends the hips until the body is straight from shoulders to knees.

Athlete holds the top briefly, then lowers under control.

Sets, reps and load are those the session plan sets (the Long Road gives no prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The hips reach full extension with the glutes, not the lower back.
Ribs stay down and the top is held briefly.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Prediction training
target_behavior: Pattern recognition, measurable
purpose: Makes pattern recognition measurable: in film study the boxer pauses before an action, predicts what happens next, and is scored.
standard_setup: Film study; pause before an action and predict what happens next
execution:
Coach picks film (the boxer's own sparring, a partner, or a bout) and pauses it just before an action.

Boxer says what happens next: the punch, the defense or the movement, and what they saw that says so.

Coach plays on and scores the prediction right or wrong.

Run 20 predictions, scored, weekly (the Long Road's prescription); keep the weekly score to compare.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer predicts from what is visible before the action (feet, shoulders, position), not from guessing.
The score is recorded each week and can be compared.
The boxer can say what they saw that led to the prediction.

name: Bag intervals matched to bout format
target_behavior: Keeps the assigned technique on the bag at the prescribed intensity through every round of the bout format.
purpose: Specific expression, technique under metabolic load
standard_setup: Heavy bag, gloves and wraps, a round clock and a heart-rate monitor. The coach names one technical target and the intensity before round 1.
execution:
Coach names one technical target and the intensity for the rounds.

Athlete works the bag 3 × 3 min with 1 min rest, at the prescribed intensity (the Long Road's prescription, matched to the bout format).

Coach monitors heart rate and notes whether the athlete reaches the red zone.

Coach scores the technical target each round.

After the last round, athlete repeats the same technical check; coach logs clean reps, failed reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
The technical target looks the same in the last round as in the first.
The athlete works at the prescribed intensity, and heart rate is recorded each round.
Punches come back to guard and the feet recover after every combination.

name: Gameplan vs reality
target_behavior: Tactical planning
purpose: Builds tactical planning: the boxer writes a plan before each sparring session and compares it with what actually happened afterwards.
standard_setup: Write a plan before a sparring session; compare afterwards
execution:
Before sparring the boxer writes a short plan: Plan A, and a Plan B for if plan A is not working.

Boxer spars as the session plan sets.

After sparring the boxer and coach compare the plan with what happened, using film where there is some.

Boxer writes down exactly one technical fix and one tactical fix to carry into the next week.

Every sparring session (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The plan is short and specific enough to check afterwards.
The comparison names what matched, what did not, and why.
Each session ends with one technical fix and one tactical fix written down.

name: Deprivation rounds
target_behavior: Wins the round with the primary weapon removed, using a second way of boxing that is organised and chosen.
purpose: Builds a second gear: with the boxer's primary weapon taken away, the boxer has to find another way to win the round, so one bad matchup does not end their progress.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat; two boxers in the sparring gear the gym uses, at the controlled-sparring level. Before the round the coach names the boxer's primary weapon that is removed (for example no jab, no rear hand, or no forward movement) and how the round is won. The coach stands where both boxers' feet and hands can be seen.
execution: Deprivation rounds: remove the primary weapon (no jab, no rear hand, no forward movement) and require the boxer to win the round anyway
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer still competes to win the round without the removed weapon.
The second option looks chosen and organised, not desperate.
The removed weapon stays out; it does not sneak back in.

name: Slip-and-counter pairs
target_behavior: Every slip produces a return within 1 s
purpose: Couples the slip to its return: the partner jabs on a fixed rhythm and every slip is answered with a punch back within a second, so the slip never ends dead.
standard_setup: Partner jabs at fixed rhythm
execution:
Partner jabs at a fixed rhythm at the pace the coach sets (cooperative roles, rung 5).

Boxer slips inside or outside the jab with small head movement.

Boxer returns within 1 s: off the slip to the lead-hand side (outside) a cross, off the slip to the rear-hand side (inside) a lead hook to the body.

Boxer resets to stance before the next jab; the coach calls any slip with no return.

Run 5 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
Each slip is small and the return leaves within a second.
The return comes from balance, eyes forward.
The boxer is back in stance before the next jab arrives.
common_errors: Slipping and admiring

name: Defense-only round (counter on cue)
target_behavior: Defends each called attack and gets back into shape (stance, eyes, guard) before anything else, and counters only on the coach's cue.
purpose: Primary Focus: Simulation rounds, pacing control, fatigue discipline
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes in stance facing the coach with room to step. Shadow only: no partner and no contact; the coach calls the attacks. The coach stands in front where every athlete's guard and feet can be seen.
execution:
Coach calls an attack (for example 'jab' or 'cross').

Athlete answers with defense only (catch, slip or step) and recovers to stance with eyes forward.

On the coach's 'counter' cue, the athlete adds one return from the recovered stance; with no cue, the athlete resets or repositions instead.

Coach runs the round for the time the session plan sets, mixing calls with and without the counter cue.
what_good_looks_like:
The system allows offense after defense only when the athlete has recovered enough structure to make a real choice.
Not every defense must produce an immediate counter.
The most important transfer is usable position, not flashy reply.
what_bad_looks_like:
Does the athlete counter because the picture is there or because the athlete expects every defense to become offense.
Can the athlete choose reset or reposition when that is the better answer.
Does the defensive action leave a clear scoring lane or only emotional urgency.

name: Pivot after every 2 punches
target_behavior: After every two punches, pivots on the lead foot (or the rear foot) to a new angle and arrives in stance facing the target, guard back.
purpose: Primary Focus: Foundational stance, jab, pivot automation
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete to turn, athletes in lines facing the coach. Shadow only: no partner and no contact. The coach stands in front where feet and guards can be seen.
execution:
Coach demonstrates two punches (1-2) followed by a pivot on the lead foot, the rear foot turning around it.

Athlete throws two punches, then pivots and finishes in stance facing the target with the guard up.

Athlete repeats two punches and a pivot, every time, for the time the session plan sets.

Coach switches the pivot to the rear foot once the lead-foot pivot holds posture.
what_good_looks_like: Pivots on the lead foot (turning the rear foot around a fixed lead) and on the rear foot
what_bad_looks_like: Can the athlete pivot or change angle without collapsing posture.

name: 30-second rounds at maximum intensity
target_behavior: Alactic output, round-opening urgency
purpose: Builds short maximal output and round-opening urgency: every round is a 30-second round at maximum intensity, so the boxer learns to start fast and work at full effort from the bell while keeping structure.
standard_setup: 30-second rounds at maximum intensity
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: every round is a 30-second round at maximum intensity (work rate) inside the contact level set for the drill; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer works at full effort from the bell: establishes range, a weapon or a rhythm at once instead of feeling the round out.

Between rounds the boxer resets posture, breathing and eyes; rest is what the session plan sets.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
Full output from the first second.
Bursts stay clean and recognisable, not frantic.
The boxer uses the break to restore posture, breath and eyes.

name: Retraction emphasis
target_behavior: Retraction faster than extension
purpose: Trains the jab to come back faster than it goes out; beginners extend fast and return slowly, which is backwards for both defense and combination speed.
standard_setup: Mirror or bag
execution:
Athlete stands in stance in front of a mirror or at a bag.

Athlete jabs and snaps the hand back to the guard, faster than it went out.

Athlete counts the return, not the punch, on every jab.

Run 4 × 30 jabs, counting the return (the Long Road's prescription).

name: Pivot-out drill
target_behavior: Pivots off the line early, while there is still room, and finishes in stance facing the partner's new line.
purpose: Trains the first answer to a pressure fighter: as the partner walks forward without stopping, the boxer pivots off the line before being backed up, instead of retreating in a straight line.
standard_setup: Open floor or ring with room to move. The partner walks forward continuously without punching; the boxer starts in front at range. The coach stands side-on to see when the boxer starts to give ground.
execution: partner walks forward continuously; boxer must pivot off before being backed up. 4 × 2 min
what_good_looks_like:
The pivot comes before the boxer is backed up, not after.
The boxer finishes off the partner's line, in stance and facing them.
No straight-line retreat.
The boxer stays calm and repeats it each time the partner comes.

name: No straight retreats
target_behavior: Leaves pressure laterally or on an angle, never in a straight line back, even when tired.
purpose: Holds lateral movement under fatigue in live work: tired, the boxer spars with no straight-line backward steps.
standard_setup: Constrained live, tired
execution:
Run in the last 15–20 minutes of a session, after conditioning, once the main behavior of the day is already stable.

Boxer and partner spar at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring; the partner pressures.

Boxer may not step straight back: every retreat is a pivot, an angle or a lateral step.

Coach counts straight-line backward steps per round; the target is zero.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Zero straight-line backward steps in the round.
Exits end in stance facing the partner.
The last round looks like the first.

name: Line work
target_behavior: Step-and-slide in all four directions without crossing feet or leaving stance
purpose: Builds the basic unit of boxing movement: step-and-slide in all four directions on a line without crossing the feet or leaving stance.
standard_setup: A single line on the floor
execution:
Athlete stands in stance across a single line on the floor, guard up.

Athlete steps and slides forward and back along the line (lead foot first going forward, rear foot first going back), then laterally both ways.

Coach checks that the feet never cross and never bounce off the floor together, and that the athlete stays in stance, not upright.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 1).
what_good_looks_like:
Step-and-slide every step: lead foot first forward, rear foot first back.
The feet never cross and never bounce off together.
The athlete stays in stance, not upright, in all four directions.
common_errors: Bouncing off both feet; standing upright

name: Tactical — the gameplan against a specific opponent, round by round
target_behavior: Rehearses the gameplan against a specific opponent round by round, in real time and at the athlete's real skill level, until the plan comes without thinking.
purpose: Plan rehearsal and automation
standard_setup: In kit, standing, gloves on where practical, in the gym or with photos of the venue; the written gameplan to hand. Week B of the daily imagery rotation (10 min daily).
execution:
Coach and athlete agree the gameplan for the opponent, round by round, built on the athlete's usual system.

Athlete stands in kit and images round 1 in real time: the plan, the opponent's likely habits and the athlete's answers.

Athlete images each following round the same way, including what to do if the plan is not working.

Athlete keeps the content at their current skill level, not a fantasy version.

Athlete notes one part of the plan that felt unclear; 10 min daily in the week this content is used.
what_good_looks_like:
Each round of the plan runs in real time, in order.
The plan uses the athlete's own trained skills, at their real level.
The athlete images what to do if the plan is not working.
Afterwards the athlete can state the plan round by round.

name: Body-only sparring
target_behavior: Defense and entry work at near-zero head impact
purpose: Gives live defense and entry work with the head taken out as a target: both boxers spar to the body only.
standard_setup: No head shots at all
execution:
Coach sets the rule before the bell: no head shots at all; body only, at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Both boxers work entries to the body and defend the body; the guard still protects the head.

Boxers change level with the legs, not the waist, and exit after each body shot.

Coach calls any head shot at once.

Run 6 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 6).
what_good_looks_like:
No head shots at any point in the round.
Level changes come from bent knees; the guard stays up for the head.
Each body entry finishes with an exit.
common_errors: Head shots creeping in

name: Slip line
target_behavior: Slipping while moving along the line
purpose: Grooves the slip with the legs while travelling: the boxer moves along a rope set at head height and slips without a partner.
standard_setup: Rope at head height
execution:
Coach sets a rope at head height across the floor.

Athlete stands in stance beside the rope and moves along it with step-and-slide footwork, guard up, eyes forward.

Athlete slips with a small knee bend and a weight transfer, keeping the head movement small; no folding at the waist.

Coach calls any fold at the waist and the athlete resets.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 1).
what_good_looks_like:
Each slip comes from bent knees and a weight shift, not a fold at the waist.
Head movement stays small; guard and eyes stay up.
Feet keep stance while travelling along the line.
common_errors: Bending at the waist instead of the legs

name: Pull counter
target_behavior: Pull back, then land as they fall short
purpose: Teaches the pull-back that sets up the return: the boxer pulls just out of the partner's jab and lands as the jab falls short.
standard_setup: Partner jabs
execution:
Partner jabs at the pace the coach sets (cooperative roles, rung 5).

Boxer pulls back just far enough for the jab to fall short, keeping stance and eyes.

Boxer lands the jab as the partner's jab falls short, then resets.

Coach calls any pull with no return.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
The pull is just big enough for the jab to fall short; stance and eyes stay intact.
The return lands as the jab falls short, not after the partner has reset.
Every pull has a return.
common_errors: Pulling straight back without the return

name: No Backing Straight Out Drill
target_behavior: Leaves danger with a pivot or angle instead of a straight-back retreat, and resets stance after every move.
purpose: Athletes cannot retreat in a straight line.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat; a taped line on the floor helps the coach see straight-back steps. Two athletes face each other in stance, in the sparring gear the gym uses. The coach stands side-on to see the feet and keeps count of points lost.
execution:
If athlete retreats straight back, point is lost.
Must pivot or angle out instead.
Continue round enforcing rule.
what_good_looks_like:
When the athlete leaves, the exit is a pivot or angle, never a straight step back.
The athlete arrives balanced, in stance, with eyes on the partner.
The exit is early enough to look chosen, not desperate.

name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
target_behavior: Owns the bottom position in a split stance: a controlled descent, a pause with no bounce, then a drive through the whole front foot.
purpose: boxing is a staggered-stance sport. Bilateral strength does not automatically transfer to a split stance. This exercise trains the exact position from which you punch
standard_setup: rear foot on a bench roughly knee height, front foot far enough forward that the front shin stays near-vertical at the bottom, torso upright
execution: descend under control until the rear knee approaches the floor, drive through the whole front foot
what_good_looks_like:
The front shin stays near vertical at the bottom and the torso stays upright.
A one-beat pause at the bottom, with no bounce.
The drive comes through the whole front foot, and the boxing check after is clean.

name: Finish every exchange in a different quadrant
target_behavior: Angle creation, exits
purpose: Teaches angle creation and exits: the boxer must finish every exchange in a different quadrant of the ring from the one it started in, so every exchange ends off its starting line. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Boxer must finish every exchange in a different quadrant of the ring
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: every exchange must finish in a different quadrant of the ring (marked with tape) from the one it started in; an exchange that ends where it began is called; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer gets to the new quadrant with pivots, angles and step-offs after scoring, not by running.

Boxer arrives in stance, facing the partner, ready for the next exchange.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Every exchange ends off its starting line, in a new quadrant.
The boxer gets there by angle and pivot, with a destination, not by drifting.
The boxer arrives balanced, facing the partner, able to act.

name: Coping — being hurt, being behind, a bad decision, the opponent doing the thing you fear, and responding well
target_behavior: Rehearses being hurt, being behind, a bad decision or the opponent doing the feared thing, and in each case images responding well and recovering.
purpose: The highest-value imagery and the most avoided. Boxers image winning; they should image recovering
standard_setup: In kit, standing, gloves on where practical, in the gym or with photos of the venue. Week C of the daily imagery rotation (10 min daily).
execution:
Athlete chooses one adversity for the session: being hurt, being behind, a bad decision, or the opponent doing the thing they fear.

Athlete images the moment in real time, with the nerves included.

Athlete images the response: the refocusing routine, then boxing their way back.

Athlete images the rest of the round going on from that response.

Athlete notes the response used; 10 min daily in the week this content is used.
what_good_looks_like:
The adversity is imaged clearly, not skipped.
The nerves are part of it.
Every scenario ends in a response and recovery, not in the bad moment.
The athlete can name the response they rehearsed.

name: Non-telegraph test
target_behavior: Removing the tell
purpose: Removes the tell from the jab: a partner watches and calls “seen” whenever they detect the jab starting, so the boxer learns to start it with no shoulder dip, hand cock or weight shift.
standard_setup: Partner watches, calls “seen” when they detect initiation
execution:
Partner stands in front, out of reach, and watches the boxer's shoulders, hands and weight; the boxer stands in stance.

Boxer jabs at the boxer's own timing; the partner calls “seen” whenever they detect the start.

Coach scores each set (jabs not seen) and tells the partner to call honestly; a partner who is not asked to be honest is the failure mode.

Run 3 × 20 jabs, scored (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Most jabs start with no call of “seen”.
No shoulder dip, no hand cocking, no weight shift before the jab.
The partner calls every tell they see.
common_errors: Not asking the partner to be honest

name: Reaction Commands
target_behavior: Each command gets the right action at once, thrown from stance, and the athlete is back in a balanced stance and moving before the next call.
purpose: Trains a fast, correct response to a spoken command: the athlete moves around the floor and reacts at once to "Jab", "One-two" or "Move".
standard_setup: Open floor with room for every athlete to move; no partner. The coach stands where every athlete can hear the call and be seen.
execution:
Jab
One-two
Move
what_good_looks_like:
The right action follows each command straight away.
The jab and the one-two are thrown from stance and come back to guard without falling in.
The athlete keeps moving between calls.

name: Half-power precision
target_behavior: Perfect sequencing at 50% output
purpose: Trains perfect punch sequencing at half output, so the mechanics are rehearsed cleanly without the noise of maximum effort.
standard_setup: Bag
execution:
Athlete works the bag in stance.

Athlete throws at half power, with every punch in full sequence: rear foot, hip, shoulder, then arm.

Coach watches that the round stays a precision round, not a rest round, and calls any drop in sequence or focus.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Every punch has the full sequence, foot to hand.
Output stays at half; the round is not treated as rest.
The athlete is balanced at the end of every punch.
common_errors: Treating it as a rest round

name: Retreat ban
target_behavior: Lateral movement and pivots instead of straight retreat
purpose: Stops straight-line retreat: live rounds in a taped channel where crossing the back line loses the round, so lateral movement and pivots become the answer to pressure. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Taped channel; back line loses the round
execution:
Coach tapes a channel on the floor and sets the roles before the bell: the partner pressures; the boxer may not leave by the back line; pace and contact are what the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer answers pressure with lateral movement and pivots, not straight steps back.

Coach enforces the line every time: crossing the back line loses the round, even “just once”.

Run 5 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 6).
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer moves laterally or pivots off every time pressure comes.
The boxer never backs straight down the channel.
After each escape the boxer resets facing the partner, in stance.
common_errors: Crossing the line “just once” — enforce it
