name: Jab with step
target_behavior: Jab while stepping in, out, and both laterals
purpose: Joins the jab and the step into one action, jabbing while stepping in, out and to both sides, so the jab becomes a boxing skill rather than an arm movement.
standard_setup: Open floor, lines
execution:
Athlete stands in stance on open floor with lines marked.

Athlete jabs while stepping in, out, left and right along the lines, with the hand and the foot landing together.

Coach calls any rep where the punch comes first and the step after, or the step first and the punch after; they are one action.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Hand and foot land together on every jab.
The jab finishes with the stance and guard recovered.
The athlete keeps moving after the jab rather than standing still.
common_errors: Punching first, then stepping — or vice versa. They are one action

name: Combination Slip out – 2 – 3 – pivot
target_behavior: The athlete slips outside the partner's punch, returns cross then lead hook from mid range, and pivots out on the new angle.
purpose: Defense into offense into angle
standard_setup: Slip out – 2 – 3 – pivot
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the rep: the partner throws a single straight punch at the pace set; the athlete slips outside, returns 2 – 3, then pivots.

Partner throws; athlete slips outside to the lead side, moving from the legs and trunk with a small head movement.

Athlete returns the cross, then the lead hook, from the slip position.

Athlete pivots out the moment the hook lands and resets stance and eyes before the next feed.

Partner feeds the picture and does not try to win the rep.
what_good_looks_like:
The slip is small and comes from the legs and trunk; the athlete does not over-slip.
The 2 – 3 starts from the slip, without a reset first.
The pivot ends on a new angle, facing the partner, in stance.

name: Cable/band rotational chop at speed
target_behavior: Rotates fast from the hips and trunk through the chop, then controls the finish, on every rep.
purpose: Rotational power production
standard_setup: A cable stack or a band anchored high to one side. Athlete stands side-on in an athletic or boxing stance, arms long, handle in both hands. Coach stands in front.
execution:
Athlete braces and turns from the hips and trunk, pulling the handle diagonally down and across the body fast.

Athlete controls the finish, then returns under control to the start.

Athlete turns to face the other way and repeats.

Run 3 × 8/side, fast (the Long Road's prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
Every chop is fast.
The hips and trunk turn together and the arms follow; the finish is balanced.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Mirror Movement Drill
target_behavior: Follows the leader's steps, pivots and level changes in real time while keeping stance, the guard up and the feet uncrossed.
purpose: Athletes mirror each other’s movement without throwing punches to build balance and awareness.
standard_setup: Open mat or ring with room to move in every direction. Two athletes face each other in stance, and the coach names the first leader. The coach stands to the side to see both athletes' feet, with a clock for the role switches.
execution:
Athletes face each other in proper stance.
Assign one athlete as the leader.
Leader moves using steps, pivots, and level changes.
Partner mirrors every movement in real time.
Switch roles every 60–90 seconds.
what_good_looks_like:
The mirror moves with the leader, not a beat behind.
Both athletes keep stance and the guard up through every step, pivot and level change.
The feet never cross.

name: Frame-Pivot Escape
target_behavior: Under pressure the athlete frames, pivots and exits to a better position instead of retreating in a straight line.
purpose: stop straight-line retreat.
standard_setup: feeder pressures slowly.
execution: frame, pivot, jab out or reset.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete frames and pivots off the line before backing up more than two straight steps.
Feet stay uncrossed through the pivot.
The exit arrives balanced in a better spot, ready to jab out or reset.
The exit comes early enough to look chosen, not desperate.
common_errors: backing straight up, crossing feet.
corrections: add floor marker and reduce pressure.
transfer: rope / corner situational spar.

name: Slow-motion sparring
target_behavior: Reading intent rather than defending punches
purpose: Trains reading intent: both boxers spar at 25% speed with full technical freedom, so there is time to see what the partner is about to do instead of only defending punches.
standard_setup: Both boxers at 25% speed, full technical freedom
execution:
Coach sets the rule: both boxers at 25% speed, full technical freedom, contact as the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Both boxers use any punch, defense and footwork, all at the same slow speed.

Each boxer watches the start of the partner's action (shoulders, hips) and answers it early.

Coach calls any speed-up at once.

Run 5 × 3 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Both boxers hold 25% speed for the whole round.
The boxer answers the start of an action, not the punch once it is on the way.
Technique stays complete at slow speed.

name: Face pulls, external rotation at multiple angles, prone Y/T/W, serratus work
target_behavior: Rotates the shoulders and moves the shoulder blades with control against light resistance, without shrugging or arching the back.
purpose: Rotator cuff and shoulder-blade work done 3×/week as standing shoulder-health volume: face pulls, external rotation at several angles, prone Y/T/W and serratus work.
standard_setup: A cable or band at face height for face pulls; a light band or dumbbells for external rotation; a bench or the floor for prone Y/T/W; a wall or the floor for serratus work. Coach moves between the stations.
execution:
Face pull: athlete pulls the rope toward the face, elbows high, finishing with the hands beside the ears.

External rotation: athlete keeps the elbow fixed and rotates the forearm outward against the band, at more than one arm angle.

Prone Y/T/W: athlete lies face down and raises the arms into a Y, a T and a W, squeezing the shoulder blades together.

Serratus: athlete pushes the shoulder blades forward around the ribs (for example a push-up plus or a wall slide).

Run it 3×/week (the Long Road's frequency), with sets and reps from the session plan; afterwards, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery) and the coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
Every rep is controlled, with light resistance.
The shoulders do not shrug and the back does not arch to finish a rep.
It happens 3×/week, and the boxing check after stays clean.

name: Hook-Pivot-Recover
target_behavior: Every hook finishes balanced, with the guard back and the athlete off the line by pivot or step-out.
purpose: make hook finish with position, not spin.
standard_setup: bag or mitt at hook range.
execution: hook, recover guard, pivot or step-out.
what_good_looks_like:
The hook turns from stance rather than swinging, and the rear hand protects.
The athlete does not spin or over-rotate past the target.
The guard recovers and the athlete pivots or steps out after the hook.
8/10 hooks finish balanced with an exit.
common_errors: spin, rear hand drop, wide swing.
corrections: slow single hook to freeze finish.
transfer: pressure touch spar with check-hook rule.

name: Mirror Slip Drill
target_behavior: Every slip is small and comes from the knees, with the spine tall and the guard up, matching the leader's movement.
purpose: Builds small, controlled slips: Partner B copies Partner A's slow left and right movement using small slips only, bending the knees with the spine tall.
standard_setup: Partner A leads slow left/right movement
execution:
Partner B mirrors using small slips only
Switch leader at 2 minutes.
what_good_looks_like:
Slips stay small and match the leader's direction and timing.
The knees bend; the waist does not fold and the spine stays tall.
The guard stays up and the athlete stays balanced through every slip.

name: Silent Round Drill
target_behavior: Works toward the round's stated objective and corrects themselves without coaching cues, keeping emotions under control.
purpose: No coaching cues allowed during the round.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Two athletes face each other in stance, in the sparring gear the gym uses, and the coach states one objective for the round before the bell. The coach watches from outside the action, silent, and notes what to raise at the debrief.
execution:
Begin round with stated objective.
Coach remains silent throughout.
Debrief after round ends.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete works on the stated objective all round without being told.
After a mistake the athlete fixes it alone and stays calm.
At the debrief the athlete can say what they did and what they changed.

name: Defense-only round
target_behavior: Primary defense — using feet and distance
purpose: Makes the feet and distance do the defending: the boxer may not punch, so the partner's attacks must be solved by not being there rather than by covering up.
standard_setup: Boxer may not punch
execution:
Coach sets the roles before the bell: the boxer may not punch; the partner attacks at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer defends first with position and distance: stepping out of range, angles, pivots.

Boxer uses head movement, then the guard, only when the feet are not available, and finishes each defense with an exit or a reset.

Coach calls any turtling (standing still behind the guard).

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 6).
what_good_looks_like:
Most threats are solved by the feet: out of range, off the line, or on a new angle.
The guard is used when the feet are late, not as a place to wait.
The boxer arrives balanced and seeing after each exit.
common_errors: Turtling behind the guard

name: 3-Punch Limit Drill
target_behavior: Caps every exchange at three punches, makes the third punch a visible, controlled finish, and repositions or resets the moment the sequence ends.
purpose: Athletes may throw no more than three punches per exchange.
standard_setup: Use pads, partner gloves, or controlled live partner work. Set a hard cap of three punches. The last punch is the structural finish and must be followed immediately by reposition.
execution:
Maximum of three punches per combination.
Reset after each exchange.
Continue round under control.
what_good_looks_like:
Punch count is disciplined.
The third shot looks intentional rather than accidental.
Exit begins the moment the sequence is over.
Athlete resists the urge to add a fourth punch.
what_bad_looks_like:
Athlete adds a fourth or fifth punch because the moment feels open.
Third punch loses quality because the athlete is already leaning forward.
Exit becomes an afterthought instead of a rule.
The drill turns into flurrying instead of capped scoring.

name: Overhead press (standing)
target_behavior: Presses the bar from the shoulders to overhead lockout with the trunk braced, ribs down and no lean back.
purpose: Trains the link that carries force from the trunk to the shoulders and keeps the athlete able to press overhead.
standard_setup: Barbell in a rack at shoulder height, or dumbbells. Athlete stands with feet about hip-width, trunk braced, bar resting on the front of the shoulders. Coach stands side-on.
execution:
Athlete braces the trunk and squeezes the glutes, ribs down.

Athlete presses the bar straight up, moving the head back slightly to let it pass, then through to lockout overhead.

Athlete lowers under control to the shoulders.

Sets, reps and load are those the session plan sets (the Long Road gives no prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The bar travels straight up and locks out over the middle of the foot.
The ribs stay down; the lower back does not arch to finish.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Catch-and-return
target_behavior: Catch with the rear glove, immediate jab back
purpose: Teaches the catch as a defense that hands a punch straight back: the rear glove catches the partner's jab and the boxer's own jab goes back at once.
standard_setup: Partner jabs
execution:
Partner jabs at the pace the coach sets (cooperative roles, rung 5).

Boxer catches the jab with the rear glove, deflecting it rather than absorbing it palm-forward.

Boxer fires the jab back immediately, then resets stance and guard.

Coach calls any catch made with the palm pushed forward.

Run 4 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).
what_good_looks_like:
The rear glove meets the jab and deflects it; it does not reach out palm-first.
The jab back leaves straight away, from stance.
Guard and feet are set again before the next jab.
common_errors: Catching with the palm forward, absorbing rather than deflecting

name: CONSTRAINT ROUNDS
target_behavior: Under live reads and fatigue, the athlete scores with one or two punches at most, exits after every score and never chases.
purpose: apply the rule under fatigue and live reads
standard_setup: Ring or open mat with room to exit on angles. Two athletes face each other in stance for live rounds; the coach states the rule before the bell and stands where every score and exit can be seen.
execution: 3 rounds at 45 sec / 15 sec. One to two punches max. Must exit after every score. No chase.
what_good_looks_like:
Each score is one or two clean punches, then an immediate exit.
No chasing and no panic combinations.
The athlete resets after each exit; the round stays clean.
common_errors: staying, chasing, panic combos, scoring without leaving
correction_path: stop immediately and reset the rule before restarting

name: Herding
target_behavior: Moving the opponent where you want them
purpose: Teaches moving the opponent where the boxer wants them: the boxer scores only by steering the partner into a taped area, using feet, angles and position rather than punches.
standard_setup: Boxer scores by getting the partner to a specific taped area
execution:
Coach tapes a target area on the floor (a corner or a box) and sets the roles: the partner moves continuously at the pace set and tries to stay out of it; the boxer may not punch or push.

Boxer cuts off the partner's easy lanes with steps and angles, taking away escape routes rather than following.

Boxer scores when the partner is in the taped area; the rep resets in the middle.

Partners switch roles on the coach's call.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer cuts across the partner's line instead of following.
Pressure looks calm; the feet stay under the boxer.
The partner runs out of lanes before reaching the edge of the taped area.

name: BOXING MIRROR DRILL
target_behavior: Every rep follows observe, decide, execute, reset: no movement without a decision, a pause in every rep, balance held, and a return to a safe position.
purpose:
Build centerline awareness
Develop controlled reactions
Connect head movement, footwork, and punching
Train decision-making before action
standard_setup: Open floor with room to slip, step and pivot; athletes in stance facing a partner or a mirror, as the coach sets it. The coach stands where heads and centerlines can be seen and calls the freezes.
execution:
Core Flow System
Observe → Decide → Execute → Reset (+ Pause)
Slip → Step → Jab
“SEE THE JAB”
“SLIP FIRST”
“STEP INTO RANGE”
“HIT THE LINE”
“RESET SAFE”
Slip → Slip → Pivot
“LEFT — RIGHT”
“STAY TIGHT”
“TURN THE CORNER”
“NEW ANGLE”
Roll → Hook → Step Out
“GO UNDER”
“COME UP STRONG”
“STEP OUT”
Jab → Slip → Cross → Pivot
“TOUCH”
“EXPECT RETURN”
“SLIP”
“FIRE BACK”
“EXIT”
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete can say what they decided before each move.
Movements are small and controlled; the head comes off line before the punch.
The punch returns to the centerline and the athlete resets to a safe position every rep.
The athlete can freeze at any moment, in balance.
correction_path:
1. Rushing → “SLOW DOWN”
2. Over-moving → “TOO BIG”
3. Bad balance → “FREEZE — HOLD IT”
4. No reset → “YOU’RE STILL IN DANGER”

name: Split Squat Iso Hold
target_behavior: Holds the split-squat position under tension with the front knee tracking over the toes, the front heel down and the hips square, without rising out of it.
purpose: Builds tension and control in the split-squat position so the legs learn a strong, stable base before explosive work; the jump lunge that follows in DOC-089 starts from this position.
standard_setup: Open floor with room for each athlete to step into a long split stance, athletes side-on to the coach so the coach sees the front knee, front heel and torso. No equipment needed; the hold time is what the session plan sets.
execution:
Step into a split stance: front foot flat, back heel elevated.
Lower until front thigh is about parallel to ground.
Hold position: knee tracks over toes, heel stays down.
Torso slightly forward, hips square.
Tension: push through front foot, squeeze glute.
what_good_looks_like:
Front thigh just above parallel
Back knee 1–3 inches off floor
Front knee slightly over toes, heel stays down
70% weight front leg
Torso slight forward lean
common_errors: Common errors: collapsing knee inward, rising out of position, weight shifting back.
corrections: Fix: Too high → drop 2 inches | Knee cave → push out | Heel up → drive through heel

name: Clean landed shots only, misses deduct
target_behavior: Accuracy, range discipline — directly targets the air-rate metric
purpose: Teaches accuracy and range discipline: only clean landed shots score and each miss costs a point, so the boxer learns to throw from range and stop throwing hopeful punches. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Only clean landed shots count; each miss deducts a point
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: only clean landed shots count, each miss deducts a point, and the coach keeps the score; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer throws only when in range and the shot is there; a held punch costs nothing.

Boxer finds range with the feet first, then lets the hands finish.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Few misses: punches are thrown from range, not from outside it.
Landed shots are clean and visible.
The boxer holds a punch rather than throwing a hopeful one, and stays in stance.

name: 3–5 round structured simulation format
target_behavior: Holds technique and the guard through 3–5 shadow rounds, each with its own job, as fatigue builds.
purpose: Primary Focus: Simulation rounds, pacing control, fatigue discipline
standard_setup: Open floor or ring, athletes spaced in stance with room to move, and a round clock. Shadow only: no partner and no contact. The coach stands where the whole group can be seen and names each round's job before the bell.
execution:
Coach names the job of each round before the bell: Round 1 technical scoring, Round 2 movement, Round 3 sustained pace.

Round 4, when used, is defense discipline; Round 5, when used, is fatigue management.

Athlete works each round in shadow on that round's job only, guard back after every punch.

Between rounds, athlete resets breathing and stance before the next bell; round and rest lengths are what the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Each round shows its own job: scoring, movement, pace, defense, fatigue management.
The guard comes back after every punch in the last round as in the first.
The athlete finishes the rounds clean, without technical breakdown.

name: Jab-Only Round
target_behavior: Controls distance and scores with the jab alone: full extension and recoil, stepping with the jab, rear hand at the chin.
purpose: Controlled sparring using only the jab to develop distance and timing.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Two athletes face each other in stance at jab range, in the sparring gear the gym uses. The coach stands where both rear hands and both front feet can be seen, with a clock for the round.
execution:
Both athletes may throw jabs only.
No rear-hand punches allowed.
Maintain light, controlled contact.
Round length: 60–120 seconds.
what_good_looks_like:
The jab reaches full extension and comes straight back.
The front foot steps with the jab, and the rear hand stays at the chin.
Contact stays light and controlled for the whole round.

name: Sprint Interval Training (SIT)
target_behavior: Attacks every sprint (30 seconds maximal effort) from the first second, with no pacing.
purpose: peripheral adaptation
standard_setup: A curved treadmill (ideal), an air bike or Watt bike (an excellent low-impact alternative), or outdoor sprints on grass or a track with distance targets. A way to record speed or power at 7 s, 17 s and 27 s of each rep. Placed early in preparation blocks, once weekly, away from sparring in both directions.
execution: Intent is the entire point. No pacing strategy. Attack from the first second and accept the decline
what_good_looks_like:
Every rep starts at full speed, with no pacing.
Peak output and the drop-off within each rep are recorded at 7 s, 17 s and 27 s.
The boxing check after the session is still trainable.

name: Score-and-Leave
target_behavior: Success ends the exchange: score, exit, reset.
purpose: prevent greedy continuation after success.
standard_setup: touch or technical sparring.
execution: score once or twice, then exit/reset.
what_good_looks_like:
Most clean scores are followed by a safe exit.
The exit starts as soon as the score lands; the athlete does not try to force a second success from the same moment.
The athlete arrives balanced, able to score again from the next picture or reset.
common_errors: staying after scoring.
corrections: reduce allowed punches to one.

name: Olympic lift derivatives — hang clean, clean pull, high pull, snatch pull
target_behavior: Drives the bar with a fast, full extension of hips, knees and ankles; the pulls get most of the benefit without catching the bar.
purpose: among the highest measured power outputs of any resistance exercise, and they train the rapid triple extension that underlies leg drive
standard_setup: Barbell and bumper plates on a lifting platform. Hang clean and high pull start from the hang (bar at mid-thigh); clean and snatch pulls may start from the floor. The coach running it knows the lifts, as the Long Road asks.
execution:
Athlete sets the start: bar at mid-thigh (hang) or over mid-foot (from the floor), back flat, arms long.

Athlete drives through the floor and extends hips, knees and ankles fast, keeping the bar close to the body.

Hang clean: athlete pulls under and catches the bar on the front of the shoulders. Clean pull, high pull and snatch pull: no catch; the bar is lowered under control.

Run 4–5 × 3 @ 70–85% (the Long Road's prescription).

After the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check; coach logs clean explosive reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
The hips, knees and ankles extend fast and fully before the arms pull.
The bar stays close to the body all the way up.
The reset check after the set shows no stance collapse or delayed reset.

name: Range measurement
target_behavior: Knowing your own ranges
purpose: Measures and marks the boxer's own punching ranges on the floor so the feel of each range becomes known without looking.
standard_setup: Tape on the floor at jab/cross/hook range
execution:
Coach and athlete measure, against a bag or pad, the distance at which the jab lands at full extension without over-reaching, then the rear hand, then the lead hook.

Coach marks each distance on the floor with tape.

Athlete drills from each mark until the feel of each range is known, then steps away and finds each range again with eyes up, checking the tape after.

Run 15 min, once, then revisit (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete can stand at jab, rear-hand and hook range on the tape and land each punch without leaning.
With eyes up, the athlete finds each range again and the tape confirms it.
The athlete can say their own ranges.

name: Last 20 seconds scored double
target_behavior: Round-closing behavior
purpose: Teaches round-closing behaviour: the last 20 seconds of each round score double, so the boxer learns to finish rounds strongly with clean, visible work.
standard_setup: Last 20 s of each round scored double
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the last 20 seconds of each round score double, the coach keeps the score and calls the start of the last 20 seconds; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxers spar the round as normal at the agreed pace.

In the last 20 seconds the boxer raises output with clean, visible work and finishes the round composed, not staggering.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
Output rises in the last 20 seconds and stays clean.
Scoring is visible, not buried in volume.
The boxer reaches the bell composed and in stance.

name: Combination 2 – 3 (body) – 2 (head)
target_behavior: From mid range the athlete throws the cross, changes level for the lead hook to the body, comes back up with the cross to the head the body shot opened, and steps back.
purpose: Level change to open the head
standard_setup: 2 – 3 (body) – 2 (head)
execution:
Coach names the sequence and its exit before the rep: 2 – 3 to the body – 2 to the head, then step back.

Athlete starts in stance at mid range (shadow, bag or pads) and throws the cross to the head.

Athlete bends at the knees, not the waist, for the lead hook to the body, and returns to stance from it.

Athlete throws the cross to the head, steps back the moment it lands, and resets stance and eyes before the next rep.

Coach moves the sequence up the coupling ladder only when it holds at the current rung.
what_good_looks_like:
The level change comes from the knees; the head stays off the centre line.
The body hook returns to stance before the cross to the head goes.
The step back ends in stance.

name: Cone ring escape drill (45° exit)
target_behavior: Leaves the corner with a pivot at a 45° angle and arrives in stance facing the target, never backing straight out.
purpose: Primary Focus: Slip-counter integration, combination layering, ring control
standard_setup:
Top View Ring Simulation:
  C           C
      Athlete
  C           C
  Cones represent corners; athlete pivots at 45° angle to exit.
execution:
Athlete starts in stance in the middle of the four cones.

On the coach's signal, athlete moves in stance toward one cone (a corner).

Before reaching the corner, athlete pivots at a 45° angle and steps out to open space.

Athlete arrives in stance facing the target, guard up, eyes forward, then returns to the middle for the next corner, both directions.
what_good_looks_like: Escaping the ropes with a pivot rather than by ducking and covering
what_bad_looks_like: Can the athlete pivot or change angle without collapsing posture.

name: Angle Exit Round
target_behavior:
not standing in front
controlling position
entering and exiting safely
maintaining stance during movement
purpose: Develop footwork after combinations.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat with room to move off line. Two athletes face each other in stance in the gear the Friday sheet names (wraps, headgear, gloves). The coach states the rule before the bell (every combination ends with a pivot or angle step) and stands side-on to see the exits.
execution:
Athletes throw combinations then immediately move off line.
Examples:
jab cross pivot
jab hook angle step
double jab step out
jab to body, pivot outside

Every combination ends with a pivot or an angle step, straight away.
The athlete creates a new line and does not stay in front.
The stance holds through the movement; the pivot is on the lead foot.
No admiring the work after punching.

name: Combination 1 (body) – 2 (head)
target_behavior: From mid range the jab to the body draws the guard down, the cross goes to the head it opened, and the athlete leaves with a lateral step.
purpose: The body jab draws the guard down
standard_setup: 1 (body) – 2 (head)
execution:
Coach names the sequence and its exit before the rep: 1 to the body – 2 to the head, then a lateral step.

Athlete starts in stance at mid range (shadow, bag or pads) and bends at the knees for the jab to the body, returning to stance from it.

Athlete throws the cross to the head the body jab opened.

Athlete takes the lateral step the moment the cross lands and resets stance and eyes before the next rep.

Coach moves the sequence up the coupling ladder only when it holds at the current rung.
what_good_looks_like:
The body jab reaches its target from a knee bend and returns to stance; the head does not drop.
The cross to the head follows the guard down.
The lateral step ends in stance.

name: Lead-Leg Drive Jab Ladder
target_behavior: The feet place the jab: it starts from stance, returns, and the stance survives.
purpose: connect jab to base and lower-body sequencing.
standard_setup: floor line; target at correct range.
execution: static jab, step-jab, double jab, jab-exit.
what_good_looks_like:
The lead foot or lead-leg pressure starts the jab when distance demands it; no reaching without the feet.
The rear hand stays responsible and the fist returns on the same line or into guard.
Each rung finishes with stance recovery, angle or reset.
At least 80% of reps are clean jab-recovery-exit.
common_errors: reaching without feet.
corrections: shorten range and freeze finish.
transfer: jab-only touch spar.

name: Three-beat rhythm feint drill
target_behavior: Makes the first two 1-2s alike in rhythm and look, then breaks the pattern on the third with a different ending, balanced and ready.
purpose: Trains the rhythm feint: the boxer shows the same 1-2 twice to set a pattern, then changes the ending the third time, so the pattern itself becomes the feint.
standard_setup: Pads with the coach (or shadow, or a bag). The holder shows the same targets for the first two 1-2s; the coach stands where both rhythm and stance can be seen.
execution: Three-beat drill: establish 1-2 twice, third time change the ending
what_good_looks_like:
The first two 1-2s are the same speed, rhythm and look.
The third starts the same way, then changes (a different finish, a pause, a body shot).
The boxer is balanced and ready after the change.
The change looks chosen, not frantic.

name: Landmine rotation
target_behavior: Rotates a loaded bar through range from one hip to the other, turning from the hips and trunk with the arms long.
purpose: Loaded rotation through range
standard_setup: A barbell anchored in a landmine (or a corner), loaded at the free end. Athlete faces the anchor, feet about shoulder-width, holding the bar end at arm's length in front of the chest. Coach stands in front.
execution:
Athlete braces and turns the bar down toward one hip, pivoting the foot on the side the bar turns away from as the hips and trunk rotate.

Athlete brings the bar back through the middle and on to the other hip, arms long.

Each side counts as one rep per side.

Run 3 × 8/side (the Long Road's prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The hips and trunk turn the bar; the arms stay long.
The bar moves through the full arc under control, side to side.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Slip → Roll → Reset
target_behavior: Every slip and roll keeps stance, balance and guard, and ends with a full reset to stance.
purpose: Teaches the defensive sequence in order: slip left and right, roll under a simulated hook, then slip, roll and reset to stance, building calm, balanced defense before speed.
standard_setup: Open floor, athletes spread out in stance facing the coach; no partner. The coach teaches each piece in order and stands where knees, heads and guards can be seen.
execution:
Slip (Left & Right)
Roll (Under Hook Simulation)
Slip → Roll → Reset
what_good_looks_like:
Slip Mechanics
Small knee bend
Minimal head movement (2–3 inches)
Weight transfer, not leaning
Guard remains intact
Roll Mechanics
Slip left
Small “U” shape under imaginary punch
Return to stance

name: Pocket Integrity
target_behavior: The athlete scores inside with short punches and exits before posture or sight fails.
purpose: score inside without losing posture or sight.
standard_setup: mitts/body shield; close range.
execution: short uppercut/hook, cover/frame, pivot.
what_good_looks_like:
Short base, soft knees, head in a responsible position; the athlete does not stand tall.
Punches stay compact (short uppercut or hook) and are followed by cover or frame.
The athlete pivots out before getting stuck; no stuck exchanges in the final round.
common_errors: standing tall, wide punch, no frame.
corrections: freeze pocket position; rebuild head/hands.
transfer: inside-only situational spar, low contact.

name: The negative self-talk audit
target_behavior: Catches the habitual negative thought and answers it with its specific replacement at the moment it comes.
purpose: Finds what the boxer actually says to themselves when hit, after a mistake or after losing a round, then replaces each habitual thought with a specific counter.
standard_setup: A notebook (or notes on a phone) kept for two weeks, and a quiet time with the coach afterwards to build the replacement table.
execution:
For two weeks, write down what you actually say to yourself when you get hit, make a mistake, or lose a round. Most boxers are shocked by the content.
Then build specific replacements. Not vague positivity — a specific counter for a specific thought:
what_good_looks_like:
The log has real entries from real moments, in the boxer's own words.
Each habitual thought has one specific replacement, not vague positivity.
The boxer can give the replacement straight away when given the thought.
In training the replacement shows up after hits and mistakes.

name: Box drill
target_behavior: Moving forward, back and laterally around a fixed shape
purpose: Builds movement forward, back and to both sides around a fixed square while staying in stance and facing one way.
standard_setup: 4 cones in a square, 2 m sides
execution:
Coach sets 4 cones in a square, 2 m sides; the athlete starts at one corner in stance, facing one fixed direction.

Athlete moves around the square: forward along one side, laterally along the next, back along the third and laterally along the last, always step-and-slide.

Athlete keeps facing the same direction the whole way; turning the body to face each direction is the failure mode.

Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete stays in stance and faces one way on all four sides.
Step-and-slide on every side, feet never crossing.
Corners are taken without a reset or a turn of the body.
common_errors: Turning the body to face each direction instead of staying in stance

name: Taped 2 m square
target_behavior: Forces infighting
purpose: Teaches infighting: with both boxers held inside a taped 2 m square, the round is forced to close range, where head position, hand-fighting, short shots and the break decide it. Live pressure, one constraint.
standard_setup: Taped 2 m square both boxers must stay inside
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: both boxers must stay inside the taped 2 m square, and a step out is called and resets the exchange; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxers work inside: head position, hand-fighting and short shots.

When an exchange is over or the picture breaks, the boxer resets shape inside the square before re-engaging.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval; the round runs for the time the session plan sets.
what_good_looks_like:
Head position and hand-fighting win the inside position.
Punches stay short; nothing loops or reaches.
The boxer resets shape before re-engaging, even in the tight space.

name: Broad jump, vertical jump, box jump
target_behavior: Takes off fast and lands quietly and under control on every jump.
purpose: Foundational jumps that teach landing and give numbers to track: jump far, jump high, or jump onto a moderate box.
standard_setup: Open floor with a tape line and a measuring tape for broad jumps, a wall or jump mat for vertical jumps, and a moderate-height box. Coach stands side-on to see takeoff and landing.
execution:
Broad jump: athlete swings, jumps forward as far as possible and sticks a quiet two-foot landing; coach measures the distance.

Vertical jump: athlete dips and jumps as high as possible, landing softly in place; coach records the height.

Box jump: athlete jumps onto a moderate box, focusing on takeoff speed and landing quality, then steps down (does not jump down).

Athlete resets fully between jumps; sets and reps are those the session plan sets (the record gives no prescription).

After the set, athlete runs an immediate reset or skill check; coach logs clean reps and the first failure.
what_good_looks_like:
Takeoff is fast.
Landings are silent and controlled, the knees tracking over the feet.
Distance and height are recorded, and box jumps finish with a step down.

name: Counter-Only Round
target_behavior: The countering athlete waits for the opponent to throw, reads the shoulders and hips, and punches only after the opponent's punch comes, without guessing.
purpose: Athlete may only punch after opponent throws first.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Two athletes face each other in stance, in the sparring gear the gym uses, and the coach names who initiates and who counters before the bell. The coach stands where the counter athlete's eyes, feet and timing can be seen, with a clock to call the switch halfway through.
execution:
Assign one athlete to initiate offense.
Second athlete waits and counters only.
Switch roles halfway through round.
what_good_looks_like:
The counter athlete waits, defends, then punches only after the opponent has thrown.
The counter comes from balance because the opening is there, not on a guess.
When no clean counter is there, the athlete resets or repositions instead of forcing one.

name: Visible scoreboard and clock
target_behavior: Score awareness, urgency management
purpose: Teaches score awareness and urgency management: with a scoreboard and clock both boxers can see, the boxer has to read where the round stands and adjust urgency without chasing or coasting.
standard_setup: Visible scoreboard and clock
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: a scoreboard (the coach scores it) and the round clock are set where both boxers can see them; both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Boxer checks the score and the clock between exchanges, not during them.

Behind, the boxer raises urgency without chasing; ahead, the boxer keeps working instead of banking the round.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer reads the board between exchanges and knows the score.
Urgency changes with the score, but the feet still set up the hands.
A boxer who is ahead keeps working.

name: Post-conditioning sparring
target_behavior: Keeps composure, structure and decisions in live sparring when genuinely tired.
purpose: Tests composure and technique under real fatigue: sparring straight after a conditioning finisher, used sparingly because of its cost.
standard_setup: Light sparring immediately after a conditioning finisher
execution:
Use sparingly (the Long Road: high cost), and only once the main behavior of the day is already stable.

Straight after the conditioning finisher, boxer and partner spar at the contact the coach sets for this drill.

Coach gives the round one role or focus (for example exits, or reset after contact).

Coach watches composure and technique through the round.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer keeps stance, guard and exits while tired.
Decisions stay readable: the boxer resets after contact instead of rushing back in.
Breathing stays coachable and the boxer still answers one cue.

name: Pivot circuit
target_behavior: Pivot 90° off the lead foot, reset, repeat; then rear-foot pivots
purpose: Builds balanced pivots: 90° off the lead foot with a reset each time, then the same off the rear foot.
standard_setup: One cone
execution:
Athlete stands in stance with the lead foot beside one cone.

Athlete pivots 90° on the ball of the lead foot, the rear foot travelling around, then resets in stance; repeat.

Athlete then does the same pivoting on the rear foot.

Run 3 × 90 s each (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
Each pivot turns on the ball of the foot, not a flat foot.
The athlete is balanced and in stance at the end of every pivot.
On lead-foot pivots the lead foot stays put and the rear foot travels.
common_errors: Pivoting on a flat foot; losing balance at the end

name: Edge rounds (own range boundary)
target_behavior: Holds position on the boundary of their own range for the whole round, adjusting the feet to every partner movement, ready to score from there.
purpose: Trains living at the edge of one's own range: for a whole round the boxer stays within 5 cm of the boundary of their own range, in the gap where their rear hand lands and the partner's does not.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, both in sparring kit; the boxer's own range against this partner measured and marked beforehand. The coach stands side-on to judge the gap between the front feet.
execution: “Edge” rounds: the boxer must remain within 5 cm of the boundary of their own range for the entire round
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer is at the edge of their range all round, not inside it and not drifting out.
Every partner step is answered with a matching step.
From the edge the boxer can land the rear hand; the partner's falls short.
Stance and guard hold while the feet keep adjusting.

name: Trap and scapular work (upper trap shrugs, scapular retraction)
target_behavior: Shrugs straight up and draws the shoulder blades back with control, neck long, with no rolling or jerking.
purpose: Strengthens the upper traps and the shoulder-blade muscles that support the neck, done as part of the shoulder work; the neck does not act alone.
standard_setup: Dumbbells or a bar for shrugs; a band or cable for scapular retraction. Done inside the shoulder work. Coach stands side-on to see head and shoulder position.
execution:
Shrug: athlete stands tall holding the weight, lifts the shoulders straight up toward the ears, pauses, and lowers under control.

Scapular retraction: athlete holds the band or cable with arms long and draws the shoulder blades back and together without bending the elbows, then releases slowly.

Dose is integrated with the shoulder work, as the session plan sets (the Long Road gives no separate prescription).

Athlete then runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the exposure and the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The shrug goes straight up and down, with no rolling.
The shoulder blades move back together while the arms stay long.
The head stays level, and the boxing check after shows no stiffness or guard loss.

name: Frame-and-reset
target_behavior: Frames with the forearm as the partner closes, steps off at an angle at once, and finishes in stance facing the partner.
purpose: Gives the boxer a way to stop a pressure fighter's close: when the partner closes, the boxer puts up a forearm frame and steps off at an angle, resetting the partner's position.
standard_setup: Open floor or ring, both in the kit the gym uses for light technical partner work. The partner starts at range and closes; the coach stands side-on to see the frame and the feet.
execution: partner closes; boxer uses forearm frame and steps off at an angle. 3 × 2 min
what_good_looks_like:
The frame comes up as the partner arrives and holds them for a moment.
The step-off follows at once, at an angle, not straight back.
The boxer finishes in stance, facing the partner's new line.
No wrestling or shoving.

name: Jaw and shoulder audit
target_behavior: Once every round, checks the jaw (not clenched beyond biting the mouthguard) and the shoulders (not at the ears) and releases them, without stopping work.
purpose: A once-a-round tension check: the boxer looks for a clenched jaw and raised shoulders and lets them go, so tension does not build through the round.
standard_setup: Any rounds the boxer is already doing (shadow, bag, pads), mouthguard in. The coach can prompt the check at first and watches the shoulders.
execution: Every round, once: check the jaw is not clenched (beyond biting the mouthguard) and the shoulders are not at the ears.
what_good_looks_like:
The check happens once in every round.
The jaw holds the mouthguard without clenching.
The shoulders sit down, away from the ears.
Work does not stop for the check.

name: Side plank variants
target_behavior: Holds a straight line from head to feet on the side, hips up, for the whole hold.
purpose: Lateral trunk endurance
standard_setup: A mat. Athlete lies on one side with the forearm under the shoulder and the feet stacked or staggered. Coach stands in front or behind to see the hip line.
execution:
Athlete lifts the hips so the body forms a straight line from head to feet.

Athlete holds, breathing steadily, without letting the hips sag or roll.

Athlete lowers, turns to the other side and repeats.

Run 2 × 30–45 s/side (the Long Road's prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The body is a straight line from head to feet.
The hips do not sag or roll for the whole hold.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Combination 6 (rear uppercut) – 3
target_behavior: At close range the rear uppercut lifts the head, the lead hook follows onto the lifted head, and the athlete turns out as if from the clinch.
purpose: Uppercut lifts the head; hook follows on the lifted head
standard_setup: 6 (rear uppercut) – 3
execution:
Coach names the sequence and its exit before the rep: 6 – 3, then turn out.

Athlete starts in stance at close range (shadow, bag or pads) and drives the rear uppercut up a short path, with the rear foot driving and the other hand protecting.

Athlete follows with a short lead hook onto the lifted target.

Athlete turns out the moment the hook lands, as if turning out of a clinch, and resets stance and eyes before the next rep.

Coach moves the sequence up the coupling ladder only when it holds at the current rung.
what_good_looks_like:
The uppercut travels a short upward path and comes back through the guard; it does not scoop or drift into a hook.
The lead hook lands on the lifted target, short and balanced.
The turn out ends in stance, facing the target.

name: Reset Under Noise
target_behavior: Every reset is complete (stance, guard, eyes and breath back) before the athlete goes again, without looking lost.
purpose: re-establish stance, breathing, guard, and sight after action.
standard_setup: athlete shadowboxes or works bag; coach calls reset unpredictably.
execution: stop action, regain stance, guard, vision, breath, and angle.
what_good_looks_like: immediate balanced visually engaged reset
what_bad_looks_like: tall stance, dropped hands, turn away, delayed reset
common_errors: athlete restarts before balanced.
corrections: freeze stance and check feet/hands/eyes.
transfer: post-exchange reset in touch / technical sparring.

name: Rotational deceleration (catch and stop a rotational throw)
target_behavior: Catches the ball and stops the rotation quickly in a strong position, ready to throw or punch again.
purpose: The ability to stop rotation — protects the spine and allows the next punch
standard_setup: A medicine ball and a partner or coach a few steps to the athlete's side to toss it (or a solid wall to throw against and catch the rebound). Athlete stands side-on in an athletic or boxing stance. The ball is the only thing that passes between them.
execution:
Partner tosses the ball across the athlete's body (or the athlete throws it against the wall).

Athlete catches the ball and stops the rotation with the hips and trunk in a short range, holding the stop briefly.

Athlete returns the ball and resets to stance.

Run 3 × 6/side (the Long Road's prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
The rotation stops quickly after the catch, without being pulled past the stop.
The feet stay planted and the stance stays usable.
The athlete is ready for the next action, and the boxing check after is clean.

name: Partial vision rounds
target_behavior: Reliance on non-visual cues, distance feel
purpose: Builds distance feel and reliance on non-visual cues: with one eye covered or the light dimmed, the boxer has to judge range and read the partner without a full picture.
standard_setup: Partial vision (one eye occluded, or dim light)
execution:
Coach states the rule and the roles before the bell: the vision constraint is set before the bell (one eye covered, or the light dimmed); both boxers work at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring.

Partner boxes at the agreed pace; the boxer keeps distance by feel and uses the jab to find range.

When the picture is unclear, the boxer slows down and resets instead of guessing.

Coach stays silent during the round and gives one note in the interval.
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer holds distance by feel and the jab, not by leaning in to see.
Stance and guard hold when the picture is unclear.
The boxer resets rather than guessing.

name: Belt squat / hack squat / safety-bar squat
target_behavior: Squats the legs hard through full range on equipment that takes load off the spine and shoulders, knees tracking over the feet.
purpose: Loads the legs with less demand on the spine and shoulders; in high-sparring weeks it stands in for axial-loaded back squatting.
standard_setup: A belt squat machine (belt at the hips), a hack squat machine, or a safety-bar squat in a rack (padded yoke, handles in front). Coach stands side-on.
execution:
Athlete sets up in the chosen equipment, feet about shoulder-width, trunk braced.

Athlete descends with the hips and knees bending together, to the depth held with a neutral spine.

Athlete drives up through the whole foot, knees tracking over the toes.

Sets, reps and load are those the session plan sets (the Long Road gives no prescription).

After the set, athlete runs one boxing check (stance reset or jab recovery); coach logs the first degradation.
what_good_looks_like:
Depth is consistent with a neutral spine.
The knees track over the feet; no inward collapse.
The boxing check after the set stays clean.

name: Blinding jab
target_behavior: Disruption rather than damage
purpose: Trains the blinding jab: a loose, low-power jab that obscures the partner's vision and disrupts their rhythm while they try to throw; disruption, not damage.
standard_setup: Partner tries to throw; boxer’s jab must obscure vision
execution:
Coach sets the roles: the partner tries to throw; the boxer's job is to keep the partner's vision covered with the jab, at the pace and light technical contact the coach sets.

Boxer flicks the jab loose and light from a lower guard into the partner's line of sight, often, to break up the partner's attempts to throw.

Coach calls any jab thrown to hurt; trying to hurt with it is the failure mode.

Run 3 × 2 min (the Long Road's prescription, rung 5).

The jab is loose, light and frequent, not hard.
The partner's attempts to throw are broken up or delayed.
The boxer stays in stance with the rear hand ready.
common_errors: Trying to hurt with it

name: Tell hunting
target_behavior: Pattern recognition
purpose: Turns film into live reading: the boxer films a partner, names their specific tells, then spars that partner hunting them.
standard_setup: Film a partner; identify their specific tells; spar hunting those tells
execution:
Coach and boxer film the partner sparring.

Boxer reviews the film and names the partner's specific tells, for example a shoulder dip before the cross or a weight shift before the entry.

Boxer spars the same partner at the pace and contact the coach sets for controlled sparring, hunting those tells: seeing the tell and answering it.

After the session coach and boxer note which tells were read and answered.

One session per partner (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The boxer can name each tell before sparring.
In sparring the boxer sees the tell and answers it rather than guessing.
The tells named are repeated habits, not one-off moments.

name: Rear foot screw
target_behavior: Ground connection first; hip before shoulder
purpose: Teaches the rear straight to start from the ground: the rear foot screws into the floor and the hip turns before the shoulder, so the punch is not armed.
standard_setup: Bag, slow tempo
execution:
Athlete stands in stance at the bag at rear-straight range.

Athlete throws slow crosses: the rear heel turns out and the ball of the foot drives into the floor first, then the hip turns, then the shoulder and arm follow.

Athlete returns to guard on the same line after each cross.

Run 3 × 15 slow crosses (the Long Road's prescription).
what_good_looks_like:
The rear heel turns out on every cross; it never stays flat.
The hip turns before the shoulder; the arm comes last.
Weight moves onto the lead foot without falling forward.
common_errors: Arming the punch; heel staying flat

name: FAKE OPENING → NO THROW
target_behavior: The athlete throws only when the opening is real and keeps the hands still on fake looks, even as pace and fatigue rise.
purpose: keep decision control under fatigue
standard_setup: Open floor or ring space. A partner faces the athlete in stance and shows real and fake openings; the athlete starts in stance at range. The coach agrees the looks with the partner and stands where both the looks and the athlete's hands can be seen.
execution: 30 sec rounds × 5. Partner alternates real and fake looks quickly. Throw only on real openings.
what_good_looks_like:
The athlete scores only when the picture is real.
On a fake look the hands stay still and the stance holds; no guessing or panic punches.
The athlete resets and stays ready after each hold.
common_errors: guessing, panic punches, reacting to every movement

name: Score deficit announced mid-round
target_behavior: On the announcement, raises urgency at once (more work, earlier initiative, clean scoring) without losing structure: urgency with clarity.
purpose: Trains live re-planning under a score: the coach announces mid-round that the boxer is behind, and the boxer has to change urgency on the spot.
standard_setup: Ring and timer, both in sparring kit, with a visible scoreboard if the gym has one. The coach decides beforehand when to announce the deficit and how big it is; the partner boxes normally.
execution: Score deficits announced mid-round requiring a change in urgency
what_good_looks_like:
The change in urgency is visible within a few exchanges of the announcement.
Scoring stays clean and visible.
Defence and exits stay in place.
The boxer boxes the next exchange, not the scoreboard.

name: Glute bridge
target_behavior: Hip strength without equipment, for a second strength day in the week.
purpose: Hip strength without equipment, for a second strength day in the week.
standard_setup: Lying on your back on the floor, knees bent, with an arm's length of clear space all round.
execution: U12: 2 × 8 · 12–17: 3 × 10 · Adult: 3 × 10 each leg (single-leg) or 3 × 15 · rest 30 s / 45 s / 45 s. Push through the heels; squeeze 2 seconds at the top.
what_good_looks_like: Push through the heels and squeeze 2 seconds at the top, with the ribs down and the lower back not arched.

name: Jump Rope Progression: Rhythm, Alternating Feet, High Knees
target_behavior: Warm up on the rope in three stages, keeping rhythm and posture as the feet get faster.
purpose: Raise the heart rate and wake up the feet before technical work, in the 0-8 min warm-up.
standard_setup: Each athlete has a rope and clear space all round, spaced so no rope can reach another athlete. The coach stands where every athlete's feet and posture can be seen.
execution: Skip in three stages: an easy rhythm first, then alternating feet, then high knees. Move to the next stage only while the rope keeps turning cleanly. The warm-up's 0-8 minutes are shared with dynamic mobility.
what_good_looks_like: Tall posture, light and quiet landings on the balls of the feet, and an even rhythm in every stage: posture before speed.

name: Dynamic Mobility for Hips, Upper Back and Shoulders
target_behavior: Move the hips, upper back and shoulders through a comfortable range before boxing.
purpose: Prepare the joints boxing uses most, in the 0-8 min warm-up.
standard_setup: Athletes in open space, an arm's length apart. The coach stands in front and shows each movement first.
execution: Controlled moving stretches for the hips, then turning through the upper back (thoracic rotation), then the shoulders. Each movement grows from small to a full, comfortable range; no bouncing at the end of the range.
what_good_looks_like: Smooth, controlled movement through a comfortable range, posture tall and breathing easy.

name: Applied Round 1: Technical Scoring Only
target_behavior: Work a round in which only clean technique counts.
purpose: Start the applied rounds (20-35 min) by putting the session's technique into a round, judged on form, not speed or volume.
standard_setup: Each athlete in their own space, in stance, with no partner and no contact. Shadow work, as in the manual's Weeks 9-12 round format. The coach stands where every stance and guard can be seen.
execution: Athletes work the round with the session's technical material. The coach scores technique only: stance, punch shape, and the guard returning after every punch. Speed, power and volume do not score. The movement exit and the defensive trigger come in rounds 2 and 3.
what_good_looks_like: Stance holds, punches keep their shape and the guard returns after every punch, for the whole round.

what_good_looks_like: An exit after every action, in stance, guard up, feet not crossing.

what_good_looks_like: The defensive move comes straight after the trigger, and the athlete is back in stance, guard up, before the next action.

name: Breathing Reset: 4-Second Inhale, 6-Second Exhale
target_behavior: Settle breathing with an out-breath longer than the in-breath.
purpose: Calm the body after training, in the 50-60 min character block.
standard_setup: Athletes standing or seated in their own space; no partner and no contact. The coach leads the count where everyone can see and hear.
execution: Breathe in for 4 seconds and out for 6 seconds at the coach's count, for several slow cycles, shoulders low and relaxed.
what_good_looks_like: Slow, quiet breathing; the out-breath longer than the in-breath; shoulders dropping.

name: Life-Skill Talk Tied to Training (2 Minutes)
target_behavior: Link one lesson from today's training to life outside the gym.
purpose: Close the character block with a short talk that ties training to a life skill.
standard_setup: Athletes seated or standing in a circle with the coach; no equipment, no partner work and no contact.
execution: For about 2 minutes the coach links one moment from today's training to a life skill (the session's character focus), asks one or two athletes to share, and closes on one sentence.
what_good_looks_like: About 2 minutes, tied to something that happened in training, with athletes speaking, not only the coach.

name: Straight Punch Bursts, 5 x 20 Seconds
target_behavior: Fast straight punches in short bursts, the guard returning every time.
purpose: Weeks 1-4 conditioning block (35-50 min): short, fast bursts of straight punches.
standard_setup: Each athlete in their own space, in stance, with no partner and no contact. Shadow punches that reach no one. The coach keeps time where every guard can be seen.
execution: Five bursts of 20 seconds of fast straight punches in shadow, with 40 seconds of controlled footwork between bursts (the next step). Speed comes from snap and return, not from losing the stance.
what_good_looks_like: Straight punches, the guard back after every punch, the stance held to the end of each burst.

name: Controlled Footwork Between Bursts, 40 Seconds
target_behavior: Keep moving in stance, under control, between punch bursts.
purpose: Active recovery between the Weeks 1-4 punch bursts.
standard_setup: Each athlete in their own space, in stance, with no partner and no contact. The coach keeps time where every athlete's feet can be seen.
execution: Between punch bursts, 40 seconds of controlled footwork in stance: small steps in every direction, guard up, breathing settling, ready for the next burst.
what_good_looks_like: Small, balanced steps, feet not crossing, guard up, breathing slowing.

name: Punch Bursts, 4 x 30 Seconds
target_behavior: Fast punches in 30-second bursts, the guard returning every time.
purpose: Weeks 5-8 conditioning block (35-50 min): four 30-second punch bursts.
standard_setup: Each athlete in their own space, in stance, with no partner and no contact. Shadow punches that reach no one. The coach keeps time where every guard can be seen.
execution: Four bursts of 30 seconds of fast punches in shadow, with the recovery between bursts the coach sets. In Weeks 7-8 a fourth simulated round is added (the next step).
what_good_looks_like: Punches stay sharp to the end of each burst; the guard back after every punch; the stance held.

purpose: In Weeks 7-8, add a fourth simulated round, following the manual's Weeks 9-12 round format.

what_good_looks_like: The fourth round looks like the first: the stance held, the guard back after every punch.

name: Conditioning Bursts, 5 x 30 Seconds
target_behavior: Five hard 30-second bursts, technique held to the end.
purpose: Weeks 9-12 conditioning block (35-50 min): five 30-second bursts, for pacing and fatigue discipline.
standard_setup: Each athlete in their own space, in stance, with no partner and no contact. Shadow punches that reach no one. The coach keeps time where every guard can be seen.
execution: Five bursts of 30 seconds of fast punches, as the punch bursts of Weeks 1-8, in shadow, with strict 1-minute rests between them (the next step).
what_good_looks_like: Technique holds to the end of every burst: the guard back after every punch, the stance held.

name: Strict 1-Minute Rest Intervals
target_behavior: Recover in exactly one minute between bursts and be ready on time.
purpose: Weeks 9-12: fixed 1-minute rests between bursts train pacing and fatigue discipline (the template's focus).
standard_setup: Athletes in their own space; no partner and no contact. The coach keeps time where everyone can see.
execution: Between bursts, rest exactly 1 minute: walk, breathe slowly, hands relaxed, and be back in stance when the coach calls time. The rest is neither cut short nor stretched.
what_good_looks_like: Every athlete back in stance, guard up, when the minute ends.

name: Character Focus: Confidence and Leadership
target_behavior: Name the character focus, Confidence and Leadership: execute under fatigue, model standards for peers, and tie it to one moment from training.
purpose: Open the 50-60 min character block with the Weeks 9-12 character focus.
standard_setup: Athletes seated or standing in a circle with the coach; no equipment, no partner work and no contact.
execution: The coach names the focus, Confidence and Leadership: execute under fatigue, model standards for peers. The coach points to one moment from today's session that shows it, then moves on to the breathing reset and the life-skill talk.
what_good_looks_like: Athletes can say what the focus means and give one example of it from today's session.

name: Jump Rope or Boxer Bounce, Moving Around the Floor
target_behavior: Light, rhythmic feet with the hands up, moving around the floor.
purpose: Open the class with 5 minutes of light rhythm work (4:00-4:05 warm-up).
standard_setup: Athletes spread around the floor with clear space all round, those with ropes spaced so no rope can reach another athlete. The coach stands where everyone's feet can be seen.
execution: Jump rope, or boxer bounce without a rope, while moving around the floor for the 5 minutes: light on the toes, hands up, shoulders relaxed, finding a steady rhythm.
what_good_looks_like: Light on the toes, hands up, shoulders relaxed, a steady rhythm while moving.
equipment_needed: jump rope (none for the boxer bounce)

name: Progressive Combo Shuffle
target_behavior: Build a seven-move combination one move at a time, restarting from the shuffle each time.
purpose: Conditioning block (4:35-4:40): a combination built up step by step while the work continues.
standard_setup: Each athlete in their own space, in stance, with no partner and no contact. Shadow work: the sequence names no partner or target. The coach keeps time and calls each new move.
execution: Shuffle only for the first 30 seconds, then add one move every 15 seconds, restarting the combination from the beginning each time a move is added: shuffle, jab, cross, slip, jab, pivot, cross. Keep repeating the full combination until time ends.
what_good_looks_like: Each added move is clean before the next one comes, and the combination restarts from the shuffle every time.

name: Ten Fast Punches, Duck and Reset
target_behavior: Ten fast straight punches, a duck, and a clean reset of the stance.
purpose: Conditioning block (4:45-4:50): fast punching, then a duck and a clean reset.
standard_setup: Each athlete in their own space, in stance, with no partner and no contact. Shadow punches that reach no one; the duck is under an imaginary punch.
execution: Throw 10 fast straight punches, duck under an imaginary punch, then reset the stance; repeat until the block ends.
what_good_looks_like: Fast straight punches, a duck that bends the knees rather than the back, and the stance and guard reset before the next burst.

name: Arrival and Preparation: Wraps, Headgear, Gloves, Light Movement
target_behavior: Arrive ready: hands wrapped, headgear on, gloves ready, body moving, before the drill rounds start.
purpose: The Friday block's first 10 minutes (3:30 to 3:40): get ready for sparring without being chased.
standard_setup: Athletes in the gym in their own space. The coach organises sparring partners and the non-contact athletes' expectations while they get ready.
execution: Athletes wrap their hands, put on headgear, get gloves ready and begin light movement or shadowboxing. The coach organises sparring partners, reviews sparring expectations, explains the drill rounds and assigns the non-contact athletes their expectations.
what_good_looks_like: Every athlete wrapped, in headgear, gloves ready and moving lightly before the drill rounds, without being chased.

execution: Athletes choose an individual workout, shadowboxing rounds, heavy bag rounds, observation training or gym service, and keep working until the block ends, showing discipline, integrity, responsibility and initiative.

name: Friday Live Rounds, Rotating Partners
target_behavior: Apply the week's skills in live rounds with more freedom and realism, rotating partners, still controlled.
purpose: The Friday open sparring block (4:10 to 5:20): live rounds that look like applied learning, not emotional brawling.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Pairs the coach organised, in stance, in the gear the Friday sheet names (wraps, headgear, gloves). The coach watches every pair.
execution: Open sparring rounds of 2 to 3 minutes, at least 3 rounds per athlete, rotating partners. Intensity slightly higher than weekday technical sparring, but still controlled. Athletes keep soft knees, relaxed shoulders, controlled punching power, a balanced stance and breathing during exchanges, and protect training partners; the key habit is punch, move, reset position. The coach watches defensive reactions, foot positioning, balance, clean punches, composure, angle exits and recovery after mistakes, and corrects between rounds.
what_good_looks_like: Applied learning, not emotional brawling: controlled power, composure under pressure, and punch, move, reset every exchange.

name: Box Breathing 4-4-4-4 (Trauma-Informed Option)
target_behavior: A calm start: four slow cycles of inhale, hold, exhale, hold, each for 4.
purpose: Arrival and breathing reset (5 minutes) on the Defense Day, whose theme is emotional regulation.
standard_setup: Athletes standing or seated in their own space; no partner and no contact. The coach leads the count in a calm tone.
execution: Feet flat. Inhale for 4, hold for 4, exhale for 4, hold for 4. Repeat for 4 cycles. Holds may be reduced to 2 seconds, eyes may stay open, and athletes may stand or sit. Calm tone; no forced breathing.
what_good_looks_like: Slow, easy cycles at the coach's count; nobody forcing a breath.

what_good_looks_like: Small, precise slips right on the cue, returning to stance and guard each time.

name: Stay Calm Circuit: Wall Sit, Plank, Jump Rope
target_behavior: Two rounds of wall sit, plank and jump rope, breathing steadily, quality movement only.
purpose: The Defense Day's conditioning finisher (5 minutes): stay calm while working.
standard_setup: Each athlete with a wall nearby, floor space for a plank and room to skip; no partner and no contact.
execution: 20 seconds wall sit, 20 seconds plank, 20 seconds jump rope (or phantom rope), 60 seconds rest; repeat for 2 rounds.
what_good_looks_like: Steady breathing and quality movement in every station: knees and back set on the wall, a straight plank, light skipping.
equipment_needed: jump rope (or none for phantom rope), a wall

what_good_looks_like: Athletes answer from today's session, and the circle closes on the line.

name: Set Tone: Seeing Before Moving
target_behavior: Start the session calm, spaced and paying attention: seeing before moving.
purpose: The first two minutes of the non-contact hour (4:00-4:02): establish calm, spacing and attention.

what_good_looks_like: Athletes spaced apart, eyes on the coach, calm and still.

name: Jab and Keep Moving
target_behavior: Add the jab to the small-step movement without stopping or leaning.
purpose: Non-contact hour (4:04-4:06): the jab added to movement.

what_good_looks_like: The jab lands in the air from a balanced stance, the feet keep moving, and the stance resets after each punch.

name: Technical Spar: Jab Only, Jab and Cross, Then Open but Controlled
target_behavior: Three controlled rounds that widen the tools step by step: jab only, then jab and cross, then open but controlled.
purpose: The contact hour's technical spar (5:00-6:00 Contact): sparring that tests decisions, not ego.
standard_setup: Ring or open mat. Pairs in stance, in sparring gear. Before each bell the coach names the round's role, purpose and coaching focus.
execution: Three rounds in the sheet's format (2-minute rounds, 1-minute reset): round 1 jab only; round 2 jab and cross; round 3 open but controlled. The coach sets the intensity within controlled sparring, the step's contact level; round 3 stays controlled sparring.
what_good_looks_like: Each round keeps to its tools and stays controlled, defense first, with a reset every rep.
